      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.145"><b>169.145</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.97.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 97</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.147">
        <h1 class="shn">169.147 TRAFFIC SAFETY CAMERA SYSTEM PILOT PROGRAM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Camera-based traffic enforcement" means enforcement of traffic control through the use of a red light camera system, speed limits through the use of a speed safety camera system, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) "Commissioner" means the commissioner of transportation.</p>
          <p>(d) "Commissioners" means the commissioner of transportation as the lead in coordination with the commissioner of public safety.</p>
          <p>(e) "Implementing authority" means either:</p>
          <p>(1) the commissioners with respect to trunk highways for the work zone pilot program provided under subdivision 17; or</p>
          <p>(2) a local authority specified in paragraph (f) that implements the traffic safety camera system pilot program.</p>
          <p>(f) "Local authority" means either the city of Minneapolis or the city of Mendota Heights, which are authorized to conduct the pilot program.</p>
          <p>(g) "Monitoring site" means a location at which a traffic safety camera system is placed and operated under this section.</p>
          <p>(h) "Pilot program" means the traffic safety camera pilot program established in this section.</p>
          <p>(i) "Traffic enforcement agent" means a licensed peace officer or an employee of a local authority who is designated as provided in this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Pilot program establishment.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) In conformance with this section, the commissioner of transportation, in coordination with the commissioner of public safety, must establish a traffic safety camera pilot program that provides for education and enforcement of speeding violations, traffic-control signal violations, or both in conjunction with use of traffic safety camera systems.</p>
          <p>(b) The authority for camera-based traffic enforcement under the pilot program is limited to August 1, 2025, to July 31, 2029.</p>
          <p>(c) Only the following may implement camera-based traffic enforcement under the pilot program:</p>
          <p>(1) the commissioners, as provided under paragraph (d);</p>
          <p>(2) the city of Minneapolis, as provided under paragraph (e); and</p>
          <p>(3) the city of Mendota Heights.</p>
          <p>(d) Under the pilot program, the commissioners must, beginning August 1, 2025, commence enforcement of speeding violations in trunk highway work zones as specified under subdivision 17.</p>
          <p>(e) The city of Minneapolis is prohibited from implementing the pilot program or camera-based traffic enforcement through or in substantive coordination with the city's police department.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Local authority requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>Prior to implementation of camera-based traffic enforcement, a local authority must:</p>
          <p>(1) incorporate both camera-based traffic enforcement and additional strategies designed to improve traffic safety in a local traffic safety action plan, transportation plan, or comprehensive plan; and</p>
          <p>(2) review and ensure compliance with the requirements under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Traffic safety camera system requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) By July 1, 2025, the commissioners must establish traffic safety camera system standards that include:</p>
          <p>(1) recording and data requirements as specified in subdivision 15;</p>
          <p>(2) requirements for monitoring site signage in conformance with the requirements under subdivision 5, paragraph (b), clause (3);</p>
          <p>(3) procedures for traffic safety camera system placement in conformance with the requirements under subdivision 6;</p>
          <p>(4) training and qualification of individuals to inspect and calibrate a traffic safety camera system;</p>
          <p>(5) procedures for initial calibration of the traffic safety camera system prior to deployment; and</p>
          <p>(6) requirements for regular traffic safety camera system inspection and maintenance by a qualified individual.</p>
          <p>(b) Prior to establishing the standards under paragraph (a), the commissioners must solicit review and comments and consider any comments received.</p>
          <p>(c) An implementing authority must follow the requirements and standards established under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Public engagement and notice.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner and each implementing authority must maintain information on their respective websites that, at a minimum:</p>
          <p>(1) summarizes implementation of traffic safety camera systems under the pilot program;</p>
          <p>(2) provides each camera system impact study performed by the implementing authority under subdivision 6, paragraph (b);</p>
          <p>(3) provides information and procedures for a person to contest a citation under the pilot program; and</p>
          <p>(4) identifies the enforcement locations under the pilot program.</p>
          <p>(b) An implementing authority must:</p>
          <p>(1) implement a general public engagement and information campaign prior to commencing camera-based speed enforcement under the pilot program;</p>
          <p>(2) perform public engagement as part of conducting a camera system impact study under subdivision 6, paragraph (b); and</p>
          <p>(3) place conspicuous signage prior to the motorist's arrival at each monitoring site, which must:</p>
          <p>(i) notify motor vehicle operators of the use of a traffic safety camera system to detect violations; and</p>
          <p>(ii) if a speed safety camera is in use, identify the speed limit.</p>
          <p>(c) Public engagement under paragraph (b) must include but is not limited to:</p>
          <p>(1) outreach to populations that are traditionally underrepresented in public policy or planning processes;</p>
          <p>(2) consolidation and analysis of public feedback; and</p>
          <p>(3) creation of an engagement summary that identifies public feedback and the resulting impacts on implementation of camera-based traffic enforcement.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Placement requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A local authority with fewer than 10,000 residents may place no more than one traffic safety camera system, whether the camera system is activated or inactive. A local authority with at least 10,000 residents may place no more than one traffic safety camera system per 10,000 residents, whether the camera system is activated or inactive. An implementing authority may move the location of a traffic safety camera system if the placement requirements under this subdivision are met.</p>
          <p>(b) An implementing authority may only place a traffic safety camera system in conformance with the results of a camera system impact study. At a minimum, the study must:</p>
          <p>(1) include evaluation of crash rates and severity, vehicle speed, equity, and traffic safety treatment alternatives;</p>
          <p>(2) identify traffic safety camera system locations; and</p>
          <p>(3) explain how the locations comply with the placement requirements under paragraph (d).</p>
          <p>(c) An implementing authority may only place a traffic safety camera system:</p>
          <p>(1) in a trunk highway work zone; or</p>
          <p>(2) at a location that:</p>
          <p>(i) is within 2,000 feet of (A) a public or nonpublic school, (B) a school zone established under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.14#stat.169.14.5a">169.14, subdivision 5a</a>, or (C) a public or private postsecondary institution; and</p>
          <p>(ii) has an identified traffic safety concern, as indicated by crash or law enforcement data, safety plans, or other documentation.</p>
          <p>(d) An implementing authority that places more than one traffic safety camera system must ensure that the cameras are placed in geographically distinct areas and in multiple communities with differing socioeconomic conditions.</p>
          <p>(e) An implementing authority may place a traffic safety camera system on a street or highway that is not under its jurisdiction only upon approval by the road authority that has jurisdiction.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Traffic-control devices.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An implementing authority must not adjust the change interval for the steady yellow indication in a traffic-control signal:</p>
          <p>(1) for one month prior to beginning to operate a red light camera system at the associated intersection; or</p>
          <p>(2) during the period that the red light camera system is operated at the associated intersection.</p>
          <p>(b) The yellow change interval for a traffic-control signal that is subject to paragraph (a) must meet or exceed the standards and guidance specified in the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.1">169.06, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) An implementing authority that adjusts the yellow change interval for a traffic-control signal at an intersection where a red light camera system is being operated must deactivate the red light camera system and subsequently meet the requirements under paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Traffic enforcement agents.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) To meet the requirement established in subdivision 2, paragraph (e), the city of Minneapolis must designate one or more permanent employees of the authority, who is not a licensed peace officer, as a traffic enforcement agent. An employee of a private entity may not be designated as a traffic enforcement agent. A traffic enforcement agent who is not a licensed peace officer has the authority to issue citations under this section only while engaged in job duties and otherwise has none of the other powers and privileges reserved to peace officers.</p>
          <p>(b) The city of Mendota Heights must designate a sworn peace officer as a traffic enforcement agent.</p>
          <p>(c) An implementing authority must ensure that a traffic enforcement agent is properly trained in the use of equipment and the requirements governing traffic safety camera implementation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Citations; warnings.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A traffic enforcement agent under the pilot program has the exclusive authority to issue a citation to the owner or lessee of a motor vehicle for (1) a violation under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.10">169.06, subdivision 10</a>, and (2) a violation under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.14">169.14</a>, subdivision 13.</p>
          <p>(b) A traffic enforcement agent may only issue a citation if:</p>
          <p>(1) the violation is committed at least 30 days after the relevant implementing authority has commenced camera-based traffic enforcement;</p>
          <p>(2) with respect to speed limits, the speeding violation is at least ten miles per hour in excess of the speed limit; and</p>
          <p>(3) a traffic enforcement agent has inspected and verified recorded images provided by the traffic safety camera system.</p>
          <p>(c) An implementing authority must provide a warning for a traffic-control signal violation under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.10">169.06, subdivision 10</a>, or a speeding violation under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.14">169.14</a>, subdivision 13, for the period from (1) the date when camera-based traffic enforcement is first commenced, to (2) the date when citations are authorized under paragraph (b), clause (1).</p>
          <p>(d) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.022">169.022</a>, an implementing authority may specify a speed in excess of the speed limit that is higher than the amount specified in paragraph (b), clause (2), at which to proceed with issuance of a citation.</p>
          <p>(e) A citation may be issued through the United States mail if postmarked within: (1) 14 days of the violation for a vehicle registered in Minnesota; or (2) 30 days of the violation for a vehicle registered outside of Minnesota. Section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.346#stat.168.346.2">168.346, subdivision 2</a>, applies to a private entity that provides citation mailing services under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Uniform citation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) There must be a uniform traffic safety camera citation issued throughout the state by a traffic enforcement agent for a violation as provided under this section. The uniform traffic safety camera citation is in the form and has the effect of a summons and complaint.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner of public safety must prescribe the detailed form of the uniform traffic safety camera citation. As appropriate, the citation design must conform with the requirements for a uniform traffic ticket under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.99">169.99, subdivisions 1</a> and 1d. The citation design must include:</p>
          <p>(1) a brief overview of the pilot program and implementation of traffic safety camera systems;</p>
          <p>(2) a summary of the circumstances of the citation that includes identification of the motor vehicle involved, the date and time of the violation, and the location where the violation occurred;</p>
          <p>(3) copy of the recorded image or primary images used to identify a violation;</p>
          <p>(4) a notification that the recorded images under clause (3) are evidence of a violation under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.10">169.06, subdivision 10</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.14#stat.169.14.13">169.14, subdivision 13</a>;</p>
          <p>(5) a statement signed by the traffic enforcement agent who issued the citation stating that the agent has inspected the recorded images and determined that the violation occurred in the specified motor vehicle;</p>
          <p>(6) a summary of the limitations under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.11">169.06, subdivision 11</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.14">169.14</a>, subdivision 14;</p>
          <p>(7) notification that an owner is ineligible for diversion if the violation was committed by a holder of a class A, B, or C commercial driver's license or commercial driver learner's permit, without regard to whether the violation was committed in a commercial motor vehicle or another vehicle;</p>
          <p>(8) information on the diversion and traffic safety course eligibility and requirements under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.10">169.06, subdivision 10</a>, paragraph (b), and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.14#stat.169.14.13">169.14, subdivision 13</a>, paragraph (b);</p>
          <p>(9) the total amount of the fine imposed;</p>
          <p>(10) a notification that the person has the right to contest the citation;</p>
          <p>(11) information on the process and procedures for a person to contest the citation; and</p>
          <p>(12) a statement that payment of the fine constitutes a plea of guilty and failure to appear in court is considered a plea of guilty, as provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.91">169.91</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner of public safety must make the information required under paragraph (b) available in languages that are commonly spoken in the state and in each area in which a local authority has implemented camera-based traffic enforcement.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Traffic safety course.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioners must establish a traffic safety course that provides at least 30 minutes of instruction on speeding, traffic-control signals, and other traffic safety topics. The curriculum must include safety risks associated with speed and speeding in school zones and work zones.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioners must not impose a fee for an individual who is authorized to attend the course under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.10">169.06, subdivision 10</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.14#stat.169.14.13">169.14, subdivision 13</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Third-party agreements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An implementing authority may enter into agreements with a private entity for operations, services, or equipment under this section. Payment under a contract with a private entity must not be based on the number of violations, citations issued, or other similar means.</p>
          <p>(b) An implementing authority that enters into a third-party agreement under this subdivision must perform a data practices audit of the private entity to confirm compliance with the requirements under subdivisions 14 to 16 and chapter 13. An audit must be undertaken at least every other year.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Use of revenue.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Revenue from citations received by an implementing authority that is attributable to camera-based traffic enforcement must be allocated as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) first as necessary to provide for implementation costs, which may include but are not limited to procurement and installation of traffic safety camera systems, traffic safety planning, and public engagement; and</p>
          <p>(2) the remainder for traffic safety measures that perform traffic calming.</p>
          <p>(b) The amount expended under paragraph (a), clause (2), must supplement and not supplant existing expenditures for traffic safety.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Data practices; general requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) All data collected by a traffic safety camera system are private data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02">13.02, subdivision </a>12, or nonpublic data as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.9">13.02, subdivision 9</a>, unless the data are public under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.82#stat.13.82.2">13.82, subdivision 2</a>, 3, or 6, or are criminal investigative data under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.82#stat.13.82.7">13.82, subdivision 7</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) An agreement with a private entity and an implementing authority pursuant to subdivision 12 is subject to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.05">13.05, subdivisions 6</a> and 11.</p>
          <p>(c) A private entity must use the data gathered under this section only for purposes of camera-based traffic enforcement under the pilot program and must not share or disseminate the data with an entity other than the appropriate implementing authority, except pursuant to a court order. Nothing in this subdivision prevents a private entity from sharing or disseminating summary data, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.19">13.02, subdivision 19</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) Traffic safety camera system data are not subject to subpoena, discovery, or admission into evidence in any prosecution, civil action, or administrative process that is not taken pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.10">169.06, subdivision 10</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.14#stat.169.14.13">169.14, subdivision 13</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Data practices; traffic safety camera system.</span></h2>
          <p>A traffic safety camera system:</p>
          <p>(1) is limited to collection of the following data:</p>
          <p>(i) recorded video or images of the rear license plate of a motor vehicle;</p>
          <p>(ii) recorded video or images of motor vehicles and areas surrounding the vehicles to the extent necessary to (A) identify a violation of a traffic-control device, or (B) calculate vehicle speeds;</p>
          <p>(iii) date, time, and vehicle location that correlates to the data collected under item (i) or (ii); and</p>
          <p>(iv) general traffic data:</p>
          <p>(A) collected specifically for purposes of pilot program analysis and evaluation;</p>
          <p>(B) that does not include recorded video or images;</p>
          <p>(C) in which individuals or unique vehicles are not identified; and</p>
          <p>(D) from which an individual or unique vehicle is not ascertainable;</p>
          <p>(2) must not record in a manner that makes any individual personally identifiable, including but not limited to the motor vehicle operator or occupants; and</p>
          <p>(3) may only record or retain the data specified in clause (1), items (i) to (iii), if the traffic safety camera system identifies an appropriate potential violation for review by a traffic enforcement agent.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Data practices; destruction of data.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/138.17">138.17</a>, and except as otherwise provided in this subdivision, data collected by a traffic safety camera system must be destroyed within 30 days of the date of collection unless the data are criminal investigative data under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.82#stat.13.82.7">13.82, subdivision 7</a>, related to a violation of a traffic-control signal or a speed limit.</p>
          <p>(b) Upon written request to a law enforcement agency from an individual who is the subject of a pending criminal charge or complaint, along with the case or complaint number and a statement that the data may be used as exculpatory evidence, data otherwise subject to destruction under paragraph (a) must be preserved by the law enforcement agency until the charge or complaint is resolved or dismissed.</p>
          <p>(c) Upon written request from a program participant under chapter 5B, data collected by a traffic safety camera system related to the program participant must be destroyed at the time of collection or upon receipt of the request, whichever occurs later, unless the data are active criminal investigative data. The existence of a request submitted under this paragraph is private data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/138.17">138.17</a>, data collected by a traffic safety camera system must be destroyed within three years of the resolution of a citation issued pursuant to this section.</p>
          <p>(e) The destruction requirements under this subdivision do not apply to: (1) general traffic data as provided under subdivision 15, clause (1), item (iv); and (2) data that identifies the number of warnings or citations issued to an individual under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Work zone pilot project.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) By August 1, 2025, the commissioners must implement a speed safety camera pilot project that provides for education of speeding violations in conjunction with the development and study of the use of speed safety camera systems.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioners must issue a warning for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.14">169.14, subdivision </a>13, captured by a speed safety camera system and must not impose any fine for a second or subsequent violation.</p>
          <p>(c) The warning issued by the commissioners must include easily understandable information on speeding, traffic-control signals, and other safety risks associated with speed and speeding in work zones.</p>
          <p>(d) The commissioner must establish an implementation schedule that begins commencement of camera-based traffic enforcement on at least two, but no more than four, trunk highway work zone segments by August 1, 2025. The commissioners may select different trunk highway work zones. The commissioners must conduct the work zone pilot project in geographically diverse areas and must consider traffic patterns, work zone accident rates, historic speed enforcement and citation rates, and other factors to study further deployment of speed camera systems in additional work zones.</p>
          <p>(e) By July 1, 2025, the commissioners of transportation and public safety must establish standards, schedules, curricula, and requirements for camera-based traffic enforcement in a trunk highway work zone.</p>
          <p>(f) The authority for the work zone pilot project is limited to August 1, 2025, to July 31, 2029.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.18">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.<span class="headnote">Exempt from rulemaking.</span></h2>
          <p>Rules adopted to implement this section are exempt from rulemaking under chapter 14 and are not subject to exempt rulemaking procedures under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.386">14.386</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.147.19">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.<span class="headnote">Expiration.</span></h2>
          <p>This section expires July 31, 2029.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.147.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.3.52.0">2024 c 127 art 3 s 52</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.15">
        <h1 class="shn">169.15 IMPEDING TRAFFIC; INTERSECTION GRIDLOCK.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.15.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Impeding traffic; slow speed.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall drive a motor vehicle at such a slow speed as to impede or block the normal and reasonable movement of traffic except when reduced speed is necessary for safe operation or in compliance with law or except when the vehicle is temporarily unable to maintain a greater speed due to a combination of the weight of the vehicle and the grade of the highway.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.15.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Intersection gridlock; stop or block traffic.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), a driver of a vehicle shall not enter an intersection controlled by a traffic-control signal until the driver is able to move the vehicle immediately, continuously, and completely through the intersection without impeding or blocking the subsequent movement of cross traffic.</p>
          <p>(b) Paragraph (a) does not apply to movement of a vehicle made:</p>
          <p>(1) at the direction of a city-authorized traffic-control agent or a peace officer;</p>
          <p>(2) to facilitate passage of an authorized emergency vehicle with its emergency lights activated; or</p>
          <p>(3) to make a turn, as permitted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.19">169.19</a>, that allows the vehicle to safely leave the intersection.</p>
          <p>(c) A violation of this subdivision does not constitute grounds for suspension or revocation of the violator's driver's license.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.15.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-179</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.29.0">1937 c 464 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.8.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/351/#laws.0.29.0">2010 c 351 s 29</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.16"><b>169.16</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/227/#laws.1.23.0">2014 c 227 art 1 s 23</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.17">
        <h1 class="shn">169.17 EMERGENCY VEHICLE.</h1>
        <p>The speed limitations set forth in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.14">169.14</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.17">169.17</a> do not apply to an authorized emergency vehicle responding to an emergency call. Drivers of all emergency vehicles shall sound an audible signal by siren and display at least one lighted red light to the front, except that law enforcement vehicles shall sound an audible signal by siren or display at least one lighted red light to the front. This provision does not relieve the driver of an authorized emergency vehicle from the duty to drive with due regard for the safety of persons using the street, nor does it protect the driver of an authorized emergency vehicle from the consequence of a reckless disregard of the safety of others.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.17.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-181</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.31.0">1937 c 464 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.14.0">1947 c 428 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/143/#laws.0.13.0">1997 c 143 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/159/#laws.2.22.0">1997 c 159 art 2 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/263/#laws.0.1.0">1998 c 263 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.18">
        <h1 class="shn">169.18 DRIVING RULES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Keep to the right.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Upon all roadways of sufficient width a vehicle shall be driven upon the right half of the roadway, except as follows:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) when overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction under the rules governing such movement;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) when the right half of a roadway is closed to traffic while under construction or repair;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) upon a roadway divided into three marked lanes for traffic under the rules applicable thereon;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) upon a roadway designated and signposted for one-way traffic as a one-way roadway; or</p>
          <p class="in">(5) as necessary to comply with subdivision 11 when approaching an authorized vehicle parked or stopped on the roadway.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Meeting.</span></h2>
          <p>Drivers of vehicles proceeding in opposite directions, shall pass each other to the right, and upon roadways having width for not more than one line of traffic in each direction each driver shall give to the other at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the roadway, as nearly as possible.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Passing.</span></h2>
          <p>The following rules shall govern the overtaking and passing of vehicles proceeding in the same direction, subject to the limitations, exceptions, and special rules hereinafter stated:</p>
          <p>(1) the driver of a vehicle overtaking another vehicle proceeding in the same direction shall pass to the left thereof at a safe distance and shall not again drive to the right side of the roadway until safely clear of the overtaken vehicle;</p>
          <p>(2) except when overtaking and passing on the right is permitted, the driver of an overtaken vehicle shall give way to the right in favor of the overtaking vehicle on audible warning, and shall not increase the speed of the overtaken vehicle until completely passed by the overtaking vehicle; and</p>
          <p>(3) the operator of a motor vehicle overtaking a bicycle or individual proceeding in the same direction on the roadway shall leave a safe distance, but in no case less than three feet clearance, when passing the bicycle or individual and shall maintain clearance until safely past the overtaken bicycle or individual.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Passing on the right.</span></h2>
          <p>The driver of a vehicle may overtake and pass upon the right of another vehicle only upon the following conditions:</p>
          <p>(1) when the vehicle overtaken is making or about to make a left turn;</p>
          <p>(2) upon a street or highway with unobstructed pavement not occupied by parked vehicles of sufficient width for two or more lines of moving vehicles in each direction;</p>
          <p>(3) upon a one-way street, or upon any roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction of movement, where the roadway is free from obstructions and of sufficient width for two or more lines of moving vehicles;</p>
          <p>(4) when the driver of a vehicle may overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right only under conditions permitting such movement in safety. In no event shall such movement be made by driving in a bicycle lane or onto the shoulder, whether paved or unpaved, or off the pavement or main-traveled portion of the roadway.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Driving left of roadway center; exception.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) No vehicle shall be driven to the left side of the center of the roadway in overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction unless such left side is clearly visible and is free of oncoming traffic for a sufficient distance ahead to permit such overtaking and passing to be completely made without interfering with the safe operation of any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction or any vehicle overtaken. In every event the overtaking vehicle must return to the right-hand side of the roadway before coming within 100 feet of any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Except on a one-way roadway, no vehicle shall, in overtaking and passing another vehicle or at any other time, be driven to the left half of the roadway under the following conditions:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) when approaching the crest of a grade or upon a curve in the highway where the driver's view along the highway is obstructed within a distance of 700 feet;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) when approaching within 100 feet of any underpass or tunnel, railroad grade crossing, intersection within a city, or intersection outside of a city if the presence of the intersection is marked by warning signs; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) where official signs are in place prohibiting passing, or a distinctive centerline is marked, which distinctive line also so prohibits passing, as declared in the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices adopted by the commissioner.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) Notwithstanding paragraph (b), clause (3), a motor vehicle may be driven to the left side of the roadway to safely overtake a bicycle under the following circumstances:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the bicycle is proceeding in the same direction as the motor vehicle;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the driver of the motor vehicle either (i) provides a safe clearance distance, in no case less than the greater of three feet or one-half the width of the motor vehicle, or (ii) completely enters the left lane of the highway;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the operator of the bicycle is not (i) making a left turn, or (ii) signaling that the bicycle operator intends to make a left turn; and</p>
          <p class="in">(4) the driver of the motor vehicle complies with all other applicable requirements under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">One-way traffic.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Upon a roadway designated and signposted for one-way traffic as a one-way roadway, a vehicle shall be driven only in the direction designated.</p>
          <p>(b) A vehicle passing around a rotary traffic island shall be driven only to the right of such island.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Laned highway.</span></h2>
          <p>When any roadway has been divided into two or more clearly marked lanes for traffic, the following rules, in addition to all others consistent with this subdivision, apply:</p>
          <p>(1) a vehicle shall be driven as nearly as practicable entirely within a single lane and shall not be moved from the lane until the driver has first ascertained that the movement can be made with safety;</p>
          <p>(2) upon a roadway which is not a one-way roadway and which is divided into three lanes, a vehicle shall not be driven in the center lane except when overtaking and passing another vehicle where the roadway is clearly visible and the center lane is clear of traffic within a safe distance, or in preparation for a left turn or where the center lane is at the time allocated exclusively to traffic moving in the direction the vehicle is proceeding, and is signposted to give notice of the allocation. The left lane of a three-lane roadway which is not a one-way roadway shall not be used for overtaking and passing another vehicle;</p>
          <p>(3) official signs may be erected directing slow-moving traffic to use a designated lane or allocating specified lanes to traffic moving in the same direction, and drivers of vehicles shall obey the sign;</p>
          <p>(4) whenever a bicycle lane has been established on a roadway, any person operating a motor vehicle on the roadway shall not drive in the bicycle lane except to perform parking maneuvers in order to park where parking is permitted, to enter or leave the highway, to prepare for a turn as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.19#stat.169.19.1">169.19, subdivision 1</a>, or to stop a school bus for the purpose of receiving or discharging any person provided the school bus is equipped and identified as provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.441">169.441</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.442#stat.169.442.1">169.442, subdivision 1</a>, and the flashing red signals are activated and stop-signal arm is extended; and</p>
          <p>(5) notwithstanding clause (1), the operator of a vehicle with a total length in excess of 40 feet, a total width in excess of ten feet, or any combination of vehicles may, with due regard for all other traffic, deviate from the lane in which the operator is driving to the extent necessary to approach and drive through a roundabout.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Following vehicle too closely.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The driver of a motor vehicle shall not follow another vehicle more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicles and the traffic upon and the conditions of the highway.</p>
          <p>(b) The driver of any motor vehicle drawing another vehicle, or the driver of any motor truck or bus, when traveling upon a roadway outside of a business or residence district, shall not follow within 500 feet of another vehicle. The provisions of this paragraph shall not be construed to prevent overtaking and passing nor shall the same apply upon any lane specially designated for use by motor trucks. This paragraph does not apply to following vehicles in a vehicle platoon if the operator has an approved plan in compliance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.881">169.881</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) The driver of a motor vehicle shall not follow within 500 feet of an authorized emergency vehicle that is traveling in response to an emergency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Divided highway; crossovers.</span></h2>
          <p>Whenever any highway has been divided into two or more roadways by leaving an intervening space or by a physical barrier or clearly indicated dividing section so constructed as to impede vehicular traffic, every vehicle shall be driven only upon the right-hand roadway unless directed or permitted to use another roadway by official traffic-control devices or police officers. No vehicle shall be driven over, across, or within any such dividing space, barrier section, except through an opening in such physical barrier, or dividing section or space or at a crossover or intersection established by public authority.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Slower vehicles.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Upon a roadway with one lane in the direction of travel, a person proceeding at a speed that is sufficiently low as to create a traffic hazard, including when operating an animal-drawn vehicle upon a roadway or shoulder of a roadway, must operate the vehicle as close as practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway.</p>
          <p>(b) Upon a roadway with more than one lane in the same direction of travel, a person must move out of the left-most lane to allow another vehicle to pass, when practicable under existing conditions. A left-most lane under this paragraph is the lane adjacent to one designated and posted for a specific type of traffic, including as provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/160.93">160.93</a>. This paragraph does not apply when:</p>
          <p>(1) overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction;</p>
          <p>(2) preparing for a left turn at an intersection or into a private road or driveway;</p>
          <p>(3) preparing to exit a controlled-access highway on the left side of the road;</p>
          <p>(4) the lane is designated and posted for a specific type of traffic; or</p>
          <p>(5) the vehicle is an authorized emergency vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Passing parked authorized vehicle; citation; probable cause.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this subdivision, "authorized vehicle" means an authorized emergency vehicle, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.011#stat.169.011.3">169.011, subdivision 3</a>; a tow truck or towing vehicle, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168B.011#stat.168B.011.12a">168B.011, subdivision 12a</a>; a freeway service patrol vehicle; a road maintenance vehicle; a utility company vehicle; a construction vehicle; a postal service vehicle; a solid waste vehicle; or a recycling vehicle.</p>
          <p>(b) When approaching and before passing an authorized vehicle with its emergency, flashing, or warning lights activated that is parked or otherwise stopped on or next to a street or highway having two lanes in the same direction, the driver of a vehicle must safely move the vehicle to the lane farthest away from the authorized vehicle, if it is possible to do so.</p>
          <p>(c) When approaching and before passing an authorized vehicle with its emergency, flashing, or warning lights activated that is parked or otherwise stopped on or next to a street or highway having more than two lanes in the same direction, the driver of a vehicle must safely move the vehicle so as to leave a full lane vacant between the driver and any lane in which the authorized vehicle is completely or partially parked or otherwise stopped, if it is possible to do so.</p>
          <p>(d) If a lane change under paragraph (b) or (c) is impossible, or when approaching and before passing an authorized vehicle with its emergency, flashing, or warning lights activated that is parked or otherwise stopped on or next to a street or highway having only one lane in the same direction, the driver of a vehicle must reduce the speed of the motor vehicle to a speed that is reasonable and prudent under the conditions until the motor vehicle has completely passed the parked or stopped authorized vehicle, if it is possible to do so.</p>
          <p>(e) A peace officer may issue a citation to the driver of a motor vehicle if the peace officer has probable cause to believe that the driver has operated the vehicle in violation of this subdivision within the four-hour period following the termination of the incident or a receipt of a report under paragraph (f). The citation may be issued even though the violation was not committed in the presence of the peace officer.</p>
          <p>(f) Although probable cause may be otherwise satisfied by other evidentiary elements or factors, probable cause is sufficient for purposes of this subdivision when the person cited is operating the vehicle described by a member of the crew of an authorized emergency vehicle or a towing vehicle as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168B.011#stat.168B.011.12a">168B.011, subdivision 12a</a>, responding to an incident in a timely report of the violation of this subdivision, which includes a description of the vehicle used to commit the offense and the vehicle's license plate number. For the purposes of issuance of a citation under paragraph (e), "timely" means that the report must be made within a four-hour period following the termination of the incident.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.11a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11a.<span class="headnote">Passing stalled or disabled vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this subdivision, "stalled vehicle" means any motor vehicle that is disabled, parked, inoperable, or otherwise stopped on or next to a street or highway.</p>
          <p>(b) When approaching and before passing a stalled vehicle with either its hazard lights activated or people visibly present outside the vehicle on or next to a street or highway having two lanes in the same direction, the driver of a vehicle must, if it is possible to do so, safely move the vehicle to the lane farthest away from the stalled vehicle.</p>
          <p>(c) When approaching and before passing a stalled vehicle with either its hazard lights activated or people visibly present outside the vehicle on or next to a street having two or more lanes in the same direction, the driver of a vehicle must, if it is possible to do so, safely move the vehicle so as to leave a full lane vacant between the driver and any lane in which the stalled vehicle is completely or partially parked or otherwise stopped.</p>
          <p>(d) If a lane change under paragraph (b) or (c) is impossible when approaching and before passing a stalled vehicle with either its hazard lights activated or people visibly present outside the vehicle on or next to a street or highway having only one lane in the same direction, the driver of a vehicle must reduce the speed of the motor vehicle to a speed that is reasonable and prudent under the conditions until the motor vehicle has completely passed the stalled vehicle, if it is possible to do so.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/18/#laws.0.5.0">2019 c 18 s 5</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.18.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Impeding motorcycle.</span></h2>
          <p>An operator of a motor vehicle must not intentionally impede or attempt to prevent the operation of a motorcycle when the motorcycle is operated under the conditions specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.974#stat.169.974.5">169.974, subdivision 5</a>, paragraph (g).</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.18.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-182</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-183</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-184</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-185</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-186</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-187</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-188</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-189</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.32.0">1937 c 464 s 32</a>-39; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.7.0">1939 c 430 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.15.0">1947 c 428 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/363/#laws.0.1.0">1951 c 363 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/521/#laws.0.2.0">1959 c 521 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/357/#laws.0.5.0">1963 c 357 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/627/#laws.0.1.0">1963 c 627 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/138/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 138 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/123/#laws.5.7.0">1973 c 123 art 5 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/739/#laws.0.7.0">1978 c 739 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/26/#laws.0.2.0">1993 c 26 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/187/#laws.0.4.0">1993 c 187 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/72/#laws.0.1.0">1995 c 72 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/456/#laws.0.20.0">1996 c 456 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.2.42.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 2 s 42</a>,43; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/120/#laws.0.2.0">2005 c 120 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/6/#laws.3.43.0">1Sp2005 c 6 art 3 s 43</a>-45; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/212/#laws.1.9.0">2006 c 212 art 1 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.30.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 30</a>-32; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/86/#laws.1.27.0">2009 c 86 art 1 s 27; 2012 c 287 art 3 s 64</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/127/#laws.0.28.0">2013 c 127 s 28</a>,29; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/75/#laws.2.21.0">2015 c 75 art 2 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/3/#laws.3.49.0">1Sp2017 c 3 art 3 s 49</a>,50; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/159/#laws.0.1.0">2018 c 159 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/18/#laws.0.3.0">2019 c 18 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.36.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 36</a>-39; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.1.53.0">2020 c 83 art 1 s 53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/5/#laws.4.56.0">1Sp2021 c 5 art 4 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.4.45.0">2023 c 68 art 4 s 45</a>,46; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.3.53.0">2024 c 127 art 3 s 53</a></p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>Subdivision 13, as added by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 3, section 53, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 3, section 53, the effective date.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.19">
        <h1 class="shn">169.19 TURNING, STARTING, AND SIGNALING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.19.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Turning at intersection.</span></h2>
          <p>The driver of a vehicle intending to turn at an intersection shall do so as follows:</p>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph, both the approach for a right turn and a right turn shall be made as close as practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway. When necessary to accommodate vehicle configuration, a driver is permitted to make a right turn into the farthest lane of a roadway with two or more lanes in the same direction in order to make a U-turn at a reduced conflict intersection, if it is safe to do so.</p>
          <p>(b) Approach for a left turn on other than one-way roadways shall be made in that portion of the right half of the roadway nearest the centerline thereof, and after entering the intersection the left turn shall be made so as to leave the intersection to the right of the centerline of the roadway being entered. Whenever practicable the left turn shall be made in that portion of the intersection to the left of the center of the intersection.</p>
          <p>(c) Approach for a left turn from a two-way roadway into a one-way roadway shall be made in that portion of the right half of the roadway nearest the centerline thereof and by passing to the right of such centerline where it enters the intersection.</p>
          <p>(d) A left turn from a one-way roadway into a two-way roadway shall be made from the left-hand lane and by passing to the right of the centerline of the roadway being entered upon leaving the intersection.</p>
          <p>(e) Where both streets or roadways are one way, both the approach for a left turn and a left turn shall be made as close as practicable to the left-hand curb or edge of the roadway.</p>
          <p>(f) Local authorities in their respective jurisdictions may cause markers, buttons, or signs to be placed within or adjacent to intersections and thereby require and direct that a different course from that specified in this section be traveled by vehicles turning at an intersection, and when markers, buttons, or signs are so placed no driver of a vehicle shall turn a vehicle at an intersection other than as directed and required by such markers, buttons, or signs.</p>
          <p>(g) Whenever it is necessary for the driver of a motor vehicle to cross a bicycle lane adjacent to the driver's lane of travel to make a turn, the driver shall first signal the movement, then drive the motor vehicle into the bicycle lane prior to making the turn, but only after it is safe to do so. The driver shall then make the turn consistent with any traffic markers, buttons, or signs, yielding the right-of-way to any vehicles or bicycles approaching so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.19.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">U-turn.</span></h2>
          <p>The operator of a vehicle must not turn to proceed in the opposite direction upon any curve, or upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade, where the vehicle cannot be seen by the operator of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 1,000 feet. The operator of a vehicle must not turn the vehicle to proceed in the opposite direction unless the movement can be made safely and without interfering with other traffic. The operator of a vehicle is permitted to make a right-hand turn into the farthest lane of a roadway with two or more lanes in the same direction in order to make a U-turn at a reduced-conflict intersection if it is safe to do so.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.19.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Starting parked car.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall start a vehicle which is stopped, standing, or parked unless and until such movement can be made with reasonable safety.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.19.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Change of course.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall turn a vehicle at an intersection unless the vehicle is in proper position upon the roadway as required in this section, or turn a vehicle to enter a private road or driveway or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course or move right or left upon a highway unless and until the movement can be made with reasonable safety after giving an appropriate signal in the manner hereinafter provided.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.19.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Signal to turn.</span></h2>
          <p>A signal of intention to turn right or left shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled by the vehicle before turning. A person whose vehicle is exiting a roundabout is exempt from this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.19.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Signal to stop.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall stop or suddenly decrease the speed of a vehicle without first giving an appropriate signal in the manner provided herein to the driver of any vehicle immediately to the rear unless there is a good and sufficient reason for not being able to do so.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.19.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Signaling methods.</span></h2>
          <p>The signals herein required shall be given either by means of the hand and arm or by a signal lamp or signal device of a type approved by the commissioner of public safety, but when a vehicle is so constructed or loaded that a hand and arm signal would not be visible in normal sunlight, and at night both to the front and rear of such vehicle, then the signals must be given by such a lamp or device.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.19.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Hand signals.</span></h2>
          <p>When the signal is given by means of the hand and arm the driver shall indicate intention to start, stop, or turn by extending the hand and arm from and beyond the left side of the vehicle in the following manner and these signals shall indicate as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) left turn: hand and arm extended horizontally;</p>
          <p>(2) right turn: hand and arm extended upward, except that a bicyclist or motorcyclist may extend the right hand and arm horizontally to the right side of the bicycle or motorcycle;</p>
          <p>(3) stop or decrease speed: hand and arm extended downward.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.19.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-190</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-191</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-192</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-193</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-194</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-195</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.40.0">1937 c 464 s 40</a>-45; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.8.0">1939 c 430 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.16.0">1947 c 428 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/521/#laws.0.3.0">1959 c 521 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/286/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 286 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/587/#laws.0.1.0">1978 c 587 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/739/#laws.0.8.0">1978 c 739 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/204/#laws.0.1.0">1989 c 204 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/287/#laws.4.19.0">2012 c 287 art 4 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/127/#laws.0.30.0">2013 c 127 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/287/#laws.0.10.0">2014 c 287 s 10</a>,11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/104/#laws.1.34.0">2024 c 104 art 1 s 34</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.20">
        <h1 class="shn">169.20 RIGHT-OF-WAY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.20.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Approaching intersection.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) When two vehicles enter an uncontrolled intersection from different highways at approximately the same time, the driver of the vehicle on the left shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on the right.</p>
          <p>(b) When two vehicles enter an intersection controlled by stop signs or by blinking red traffic signals requiring drivers or vehicles from any direction to stop before proceeding, the driver of the vehicle on the left shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on the right.</p>
          <p>(c) At an uncontrolled approach to a T-shaped intersection, the driver required to turn shall yield to the cross traffic.</p>
          <p>(d) The driver of any vehicle traveling at an unlawful speed shall forfeit any right-of-way which the driver might otherwise have hereunder.</p>
          <p>(e) The foregoing rules are modified as hereinafter stated in this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.20.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Left turn.</span></h2>
          <p>The driver of a vehicle intending to turn to the left within an intersection or into an alley, private road, or driveway shall yield the right-of-way to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction which is within the intersection or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.20.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Through highway; stop sign.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The driver of a vehicle shall stop as required by this chapter at the entrance to a through highway and shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from the through highway or which are approaching so closely on the through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard, but the driver having so yielded may proceed, and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection on the through highway shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicles so proceeding into or across the through highway.</p>
          <p>(b) The driver of a vehicle shall likewise stop in obedience to a stop sign, as required herein, at an intersection where a stop sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto although not a part of a through highway, and shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles not so obliged to stop which are within the intersection or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard, but may then proceed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.20.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Vehicle entering roadway.</span></h2>
          <p>The driver of a vehicle about to enter or cross a roadway from any place other than a roadway shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles approaching on the roadway to be entered or crossed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.20.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Emergency vehicle; penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Upon the immediate approach of an authorized emergency vehicle equipped with at least one lighted lamp exhibiting red light visible under normal atmospheric conditions from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle and, except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b), when the driver is giving audible signal by siren, the driver of each other vehicle shall yield the right-of-way and shall immediately drive to a position parallel to and as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb of the highway clear of any intersection, and shall stop and remain in this position until the authorized emergency vehicle has passed, except when otherwise directed by a police officer. The driver of another vehicle on a one-way roadway shall drive to the closest edge or curb and stop.</p>
          <p>(b) The driver of an authorized emergency vehicle escorting the movement of an oversize or overweight vehicle or load need not sound an audible signal by siren but shall exhibit the light required by paragraph (a). The driver of each other vehicle then shall yield the right-of-way, as required by paragraph (a), to the emergency vehicle escorting the oversize or overweight vehicle or load.</p>
          <p>(c) Upon the approach of an authorized emergency vehicle the driver of each streetcar shall immediately stop the car clear of any intersection and keep it in this position and keep the doors and gates of the streetcar closed until the authorized emergency vehicle has passed, except when otherwise directed by a police officer.</p>
          <p>(d) This subdivision does not operate to relieve the driver of an authorized emergency vehicle from the duty to drive with due regard for the safety of persons using the highways.</p>
          <p>(e) A driver who fails to comply with paragraph (a), (b), or (c) is guilty of a petty misdemeanor and may be penalized according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.89">169.89</a>.</p>
          <p>(f) A driver who intentionally obstructs an emergency vehicle or otherwise intentionally fails to comply with paragraph (a), (b), or (c) is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.20.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Arrest; citation; probable cause.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A peace officer may arrest the driver of a motor vehicle if the peace officer has probable cause to believe that the driver has operated the vehicle in violation of subdivision 5, paragraph (a), (b), or (f), within the four-hour period following the termination of the emergency incident or a receipt of a report under paragraph (c). The arrest may be made even though the violation was not committed in the presence of the peace officer.</p>
          <p>(b) A peace officer may issue a citation in lieu of arrest to the driver of a motor vehicle if the peace officer has probable cause to believe that the driver has operated the vehicle in violation of subdivision 5.</p>
          <p>(c) Although probable cause may be otherwise satisfied by other evidentiary elements or factors, probable cause is sufficient for purposes of this subdivision when a member of the crew of an authorized emergency vehicle responding to an emergency incident makes a timely report of the violation of subdivision 5 and provides a description of the vehicle used to commit the offense and the vehicle's license plate number. For the purposes of an arrest under paragraph (a), "timely" means that the report must be made within a four-hour period following the termination of the emergency incident.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.20.5b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5b.<span class="headnote">Violation; penalty for owner or lessee.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If a motor vehicle is operated in violation of subdivision 5, the owner of the vehicle, or for a leased motor vehicle the lessee of the vehicle, is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) Paragraph (a) does not apply if (1) a person other than the owner or lessee was operating the vehicle at the time the violation occurred, or (2) the owner presents written evidence that the motor vehicle had been reported to a law enforcement agency as stolen at the time of the violation.</p>
          <p>(c) Paragraph (a) does not apply to a lessor of a motor vehicle if the lessor keeps a record of the name and address of the lessee.</p>
          <p>(d) Paragraph (a) does not prohibit or limit the prosecution of a motor vehicle operator who violates subdivision 5.</p>
          <p>(e) A violation under paragraph (a) does not constitute grounds for revocation or suspension of the owner's or lessee's driver's license.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.20.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Funeral procession.</span></h2>
          <p>When any funeral procession identifies itself by using regular lights on all cars and by keeping all cars in close formation, the driver of every other vehicle, except an emergency vehicle, shall yield the right-of-way.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.20.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Transit bus; school bus.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The driver of a vehicle traveling in the right-hand lane of traffic shall yield the right-of-way to any transit bus attempting to enter that lane from a bus stop or shoulder, as indicated by a flashing left turn signal.</p>
          <p>(b) The driver of a vehicle traveling in the right-hand lane of traffic shall yield the right-of-way to any school bus attempting to enter that lane from a shoulder, right-turn lane, or other location where the school bus has stopped to load or unload passengers. The school bus must indicate the intent to enter the right-hand lane of traffic by activating a flashing left turn signal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.20.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Roundabouts.</span></h2>
          <p>If two vehicles with a total length in excess of 40 feet, a total width in excess of ten feet, or any combination of vehicles, approach or drive through a roundabout at approximately the same time or so closely as to constitute a hazard of collision, the operator of the vehicle or combination of vehicles on the right must yield the right-of-way to the vehicle or combination of vehicles on the left and, if necessary, must reduce speed or stop in order to so yield.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="section" id="stat.169.201">
        <h1 class="shn">169.201 YIELD SIGN.</h1>
        <p>The driver of a vehicle approaching a yield sign shall slow to a speed that is reasonable for conditions of traffic and visibility, and stop if necessary, and yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian legally crossing the roadway, and to all vehicles on the intersecting street or highway which are so close as to constitute an immediate hazard.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.201.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1955/0/606/#laws.0.1.0">1955 c 606 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/521/#laws.0.4.0">1959 c 521 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/0/65/#laws.0.1.0">1961 c 65 s 1</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">PEDESTRIANS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.202">
        <h1 class="shn">169.202 BLIND PERSON CARRYING WHITE CANE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.202.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Limitation on carrying.</span></h2>
          <p>It shall be unlawful for any person to carry a white painted cane unless said person is a blind person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.202.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Blind pedestrian has right-of-way.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person operating a motor vehicle in this state shall bring such motor vehicle to a stop and give the right-of-way at any intersection of any street, avenue, alley or other public highway to a blind pedestrian who is carrying a cane predominantly white or metallic in color, with or without red tip, or using a guide dog, when such blind person enters said intersection.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.202.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.49.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 49</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.202.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/369/#laws.0.1.0">1945 c 369 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/391/#laws.0.1.0">1949 c 391 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/70/#laws.0.2.0">1971 c 70 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.21">
        <h1 class="shn">169.21 PEDESTRIAN.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.21.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Obey traffic-control signals.</span></h2>
          <p>Pedestrians shall be subject to traffic-control signals at intersections as heretofore declared in this chapter, but at all other places pedestrians shall be accorded the privileges and shall be subject to the restrictions stated in this section and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.22">169.22</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.21.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Rights in absence of signal.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Where traffic-control signals are not in place or in operation, the driver of a vehicle shall stop to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing the roadway within a marked crosswalk or at an intersection with no marked crosswalk. The driver must remain stopped until the pedestrian has passed the lane in which the vehicle is stopped. No pedestrian shall suddenly leave a curb or other place of safety and walk or run into the path of a vehicle which is so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield. This provision shall not apply under the conditions as otherwise provided in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) When any vehicle is stopped at a marked crosswalk or at an intersection with no marked crosswalk to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway, the driver of any other vehicle approaching from the rear shall not overtake and pass the stopped vehicle.</p>
          <p>(c) It is unlawful for any person to drive a motor vehicle through a column of school children crossing a street or highway or past a member of a school safety patrol or adult crossing guard, while the member of the school safety patrol or adult crossing guard is directing the movement of children across a street or highway and while the school safety patrol member or adult crossing guard is holding an official signal in the stop position. A peace officer may arrest the driver of a motor vehicle if the peace officer has probable cause to believe that the driver has operated the vehicle in violation of this paragraph within the past four hours.</p>
          <p>(d) A person who violates this subdivision is guilty of a misdemeanor. A person who violates this subdivision a second or subsequent time within one year of a previous conviction under this subdivision is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.21.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Crossing between intersections.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Every pedestrian crossing a roadway at any point other than within a marked crosswalk or at an intersection with no marked crosswalk shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles upon the roadway.</p>
          <p>(b) Any pedestrian crossing a roadway at a point where a pedestrian tunnel or overhead pedestrian crossing has been provided shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles upon the roadway.</p>
          <p>(c) Between adjacent intersections at which traffic-control signals are in operation pedestrians shall not cross at any place except in a marked crosswalk.</p>
