          <p>(d) Notwithstanding the other provisions of this section every driver of a vehicle shall (1) exercise due care to avoid colliding with any bicycle or pedestrian upon any roadway and (2) give an audible signal when necessary and exercise proper precaution upon observing any child or any obviously confused or incapacitated person upon a roadway.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.21.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Use right half of crosswalk.</span></h2>
          <p>Pedestrians shall move when practicable upon the right half of crosswalks.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.21.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Walk on left side of roadway.</span></h2>
          <p>Pedestrians when walking or moving in a wheelchair along a roadway shall, when practicable, walk or move on the left side of the roadway or its shoulder giving way to oncoming traffic. Where sidewalks are provided and are accessible and usable it shall be unlawful for any pedestrian to walk or move in a wheelchair along and upon an adjacent roadway.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.21.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p class="in">[Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.0701">171.0701, subd 1b</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.21.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-202</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-203</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-204</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-205</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-207</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.52.0">1937 c 464 s 52</a>-55,57; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.10.0">1939 c 430 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.18.0">1947 c 428 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/193/#laws.0.1.0">1973 c 193 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/379/#laws.0.2.0">1974 c 379 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/739/#laws.0.11.0">1978 c 739 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/468/#laws.0.3.0">1982 c 468 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.12.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.2.31.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 2 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/333/#laws.0.1.0">1996 c 333 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/159/#laws.2.23.0">1997 c 159 art 2 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.6.3.0">2000 c 488 art 6 s 3</a>,4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/10/#laws.3.11.0">2005 c 10 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.33.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 33</a>;</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.212">
        <h1 class="shn">169.212 OPERATION OF ELECTRIC PERSONAL ASSISTIVE MOBILITY DEVICES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.212.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Rights and responsibilities of pedestrians.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as otherwise provided by law, a person operating an electric personal assistive mobility device has the rights and responsibilities of a pedestrian.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.212.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Operation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An electric personal assistive mobility device may be operated on a bicycle path.</p>
          <p>(b) No person may operate an electric personal assistive mobility device on a roadway, sidewalk, or bicycle path at a rate of speed that is not reasonable and prudent under the conditions. Every person operating an electric personal assistive mobility device on a roadway, sidewalk, or bicycle path is responsible for becoming and remaining aware of the actual and potential hazards then existing on the roadway or sidewalk and must use due care in operating the device.</p>
          <p>(c) An electric personal assistive mobility device may be operated on a roadway only:</p>
          <p>(1) while making a direct crossing of a roadway in a marked or unmarked crosswalk;</p>
          <p>(2) where no sidewalk is available;</p>
          <p>(3) where a sidewalk is so obstructed as to prevent safe use;</p>
          <p>(4) when so directed by a traffic-control device or by a peace officer; or</p>
          <p>(5) temporarily in order to gain access to a motor vehicle.</p>
          <p>(d) An electric personal assistive mobility device may not be operated at any time on a roadway with a speed limit of more than 35 miles per hour except to make a direct crossing of the roadway in a marked crosswalk.</p>
          <p>(e) An electric personal assistive mobility device may not be operated at any time while carrying more than one person.</p>
          <p>(f) A person operating an electric personal assistive mobility device on a sidewalk must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians at all times. A person operating an electric personal assistive mobility device on a bicycle path must yield the right-of-way to bicycles at all times.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.212.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reflectors.</span></h2>
          <p>An electric personal assistive mobility device may not be operated unless the device bears reflectorized material on the front, back, and wheels, visible at night from 600 feet when illuminated by the lower beams of headlamps of a motor vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.212.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Local regulation.</span></h2>
          <p>A local road authority may not further regulate the operation of electric personal assistive mobility devices, except that a local road authority may allow and regulate the operation of these devices on roadways within its jurisdiction that have a speed limit of more than 35 miles per hour.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.212.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/285/#laws.0.4.0">2002 c 285 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.215">
        <h1 class="shn">169.215 CROSSING FOR SENIORS OR DISABLED PERSONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.215.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Designation of crossings.</span></h2>
          <p>Local authorities may designate a crossing for senior citizens or disabled persons on any street or highway in the vicinity of a senior citizen housing project, senior citizen nursing home, or residential care facility for disabled persons on the basis of an engineering and traffic investigation prescribed by the commissioner and subject to the uniform specifications adopted pursuant to subdivision 2. Designation of a crossing for senior citizens or disabled persons on a trunk highway is subject to the written consent of the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.215.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Uniform specifications.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall adopt uniform specifications for crossings for senior citizens or disabled persons. The specifications shall include criteria for determining the need for a crossing and the type and design of traffic-control devices or signals that may be used at the crossing. The specifications shall be incorporated as a part of the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices required pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06">169.06</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.215.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/185/#laws.0.1.0">1979 c 185 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/497/#laws.0.10.0">1990 c 497 s 10</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.2151">
        <h1 class="shn">169.2151 PEDESTRIAN SAFETY CROSSINGS.</h1>
        <p>A local road authority may provide by ordinance for the designation of pedestrian safety crossings on highways under the road authority's jurisdiction where pedestrian safety considerations require extra time for pedestrian crossing in addition to the time recommended under the Minnesota Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices for pedestrian signals. The ordinance may provide for timing of pedestrian signals for such crossings, consistent with the recommendations of the uniform manual for pedestrian signal timing at senior citizen and disabled pedestrian crossings. Cities other than cities of the first class may designate a pedestrian safety crossing only with the approval of the road authority having jurisdiction over the crossing. The authority of local road authorities to determine pedestrian signal timing under this section is in addition to any other control exercised by local road authorities over the timing of pedestrian signals.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.2151.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.6.5.0">2000 c 488 art 6 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/56/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 56 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.219">
        <h1 class="shn">169.219 PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENTS.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner of public safety shall include in the department's series of public service announcements information that educates the public about traffic regulations that are frequently violated, including the requirement for a vehicle driver to stop to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian in a crosswalk. The commissioner shall distribute these announcements for broadcast in this state on radio and television.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.219.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/333/#laws.0.3.0">1996 c 333 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.22">
        <h1 class="shn">169.22 HITCHHIKING; SOLICITATION OF BUSINESS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.22.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Soliciting ride.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride from the driver of any private vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.22.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Soliciting employment, business, or contributions.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall stand on a roadway for the purpose of soliciting employment, business, or contributions from the occupant of any vehicle.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.22.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-206</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.56.0">1937 c 464 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/379/#laws.0.3.0">1974 c 379 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.221"><b>169.221</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/739/#laws.0.15.0">1978 c 739 s 15</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">BICYCLES AND MOTORIZED BICYCLES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.222">
        <h1 class="shn">169.222 OPERATION OF BICYCLE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Traffic laws apply.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Every person operating a bicycle has all of the rights and duties applicable to the driver of any other vehicle by this chapter, except in respect to those provisions in this chapter relating expressly to bicycles and in respect to those provisions of this chapter which by their nature cannot reasonably be applied to bicycles. This subdivision applies to a bicycle operating on the shoulder of a roadway.</p>
          <p>(b) A person lawfully operating a bicycle (1) on a sidewalk, or (2) across a roadway or shoulder while using a crosswalk has all the rights and duties applicable to a pedestrian under the same circumstances.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Manner and number riding.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this subdivision,"bicycle" includes a tandem bicycle, electric-assisted bicycle, cargo or utility bicycle, or trailer.</p>
          <p>(b) No person may operate a bicycle while carrying more than the number of riders for which the bicycle is designed or equipped.</p>
          <p>(c) Notwithstanding paragraph (b), an adult bicycle operator may carry a child in a trailer or seat designed for carrying children that is securely attached to a bicycle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Clinging to vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>Persons riding upon any bicycle, coaster, roller skates, toboggan, sled, skateboard, or toy vehicle shall not attach the same or themselves to any street car or vehicle upon a roadway.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Riding rules.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Every person operating a bicycle on a road must ride as close to the right-hand curb or edge of the road as the bicycle operator determines is safe. A person operating a bicycle is not required to ride as close to the right-hand curb or edge when:</p>
          <p>(1) overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction;</p>
          <p>(2) preparing for a left turn at an intersection or into a private road or driveway;</p>
          <p>(3) reasonably necessary to avoid conditions that make it unsafe to continue along the right-hand curb or edge, including fixed or moving objects, vehicles, pedestrians, animals, surface hazards, or narrow-width lanes;</p>
          <p>(4) operating on the shoulder of a roadway or in a bicycle lane; or</p>
          <p>(5) operating in a right-hand turn lane before entering an intersection.</p>
          <p>(b) If a bicycle is traveling on a shoulder of a roadway, the bicycle operator must travel in the same direction as adjacent vehicular traffic.</p>
          <p>(c) Persons riding bicycles upon a roadway or shoulder must not ride more than two abreast and, on a laned roadway, shall ride within a single lane.</p>
          <p>(d) A person operating a bicycle upon a sidewalk, or across a roadway or shoulder on a crosswalk, must yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian and give an audible signal when necessary before overtaking and passing any pedestrian. A person must not ride a bicycle upon a sidewalk within a business district unless permitted by local authorities. Local authorities may prohibit the operation of bicycles on any sidewalk or crosswalk under their jurisdiction.</p>
          <p>(e) An individual operating a bicycle or other vehicle on a bikeway must (1) give an audible signal a safe distance prior to overtaking a bicycle or individual, (2) leave a safe clearance distance when overtaking a bicycle or individual proceeding in the same direction, and (3) maintain clearance until safely past the overtaken bicycle or individual.</p>
          <p>(f) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.4">169.06, subdivision 4</a>, a bicycle operator may cross an intersection proceeding from the leftmost one-third of a dedicated right-hand turn lane without turning right.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Stopping requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this subdivision, "in the vicinity" means located in an intersection or approaching an intersection in a manner that constitutes a hazard of collision during the time that a bicycle operator would occupy the intersection.</p>
          <p>(b) A bicycle operator who approaches a stop sign must slow to a speed that allows for stopping before entering the intersection or the nearest crosswalk. Notwithstanding subdivision 1 and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.4">169.06, subdivision 4</a>, if there is not a vehicle in the vicinity, the operator may make a turn or proceed through the intersection without stopping.</p>
          <p>(c) Nothing in this subdivision alters the right-of-way requirements under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.20">169.20</a>. The provisions under this subdivision do not apply when traffic is controlled by a peace officer or a person authorized to control traffic under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06">169.06</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Carrying articles.</span></h2>
          <p>No person operating a bicycle shall carry any package, bundle, or article which prevents the driver from keeping at least one hand upon the handle bars or from properly operating the brakes of the bicycle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Bicycle equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) No person shall operate a bicycle at nighttime unless the bicycle or its operator is equipped with (1) a lamp which emits a white light visible from a distance of at least 500 feet to the front; and (2) a red reflector of a type approved by the Department of Public Safety which is visible from all distances from 100 feet to 600 feet to the rear when directly in front of lawful lower beams of headlamps on a motor vehicle. A bicycle equipped with lamps that are visible from a distance of at least 500 feet from both the front and the rear is deemed to fully comply with this paragraph.</p>
          <p>(b) No person may operate a bicycle at any time when there is not sufficient light to render persons and vehicles on the highway clearly discernible at a distance of 500 feet ahead unless the bicycle or its operator is equipped with reflective surfaces that shall be visible during the hours of darkness from 600 feet when viewed in front of lawful lower beams of headlamps on a motor vehicle. The reflective surfaces shall include reflective materials on each side of each pedal to indicate their presence from the front or the rear and with a minimum of 20 square inches of reflective material on each side of the bicycle or its operator. Any bicycle equipped with side reflectors as required by regulations for new bicycles prescribed by the United States Consumer Product Safety Commission shall be considered to meet the requirements for side reflectorization contained in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(c) A bicycle may be equipped with a front lamp that emits a white flashing signal, or a rear lamp that emits a red flashing signal, or both.</p>
          <p>(d) A bicycle may be equipped with tires having studs, spikes, or other protuberances designed to increase traction.</p>
          <p>(e) No person shall operate a bicycle unless it is equipped with a rear brake or front and rear brakes which will enable the operator to make a braked wheel skid on dry, level, clean pavement. A bicycle equipped with a direct or fixed gear that can make the rear wheel skid on dry, level, clean pavement shall be deemed to fully comply with this paragraph.</p>
          <p>(f) A bicycle may be equipped with a horn or bell designed to alert motor vehicles, other bicycles, and pedestrians of the bicycle's presence.</p>
          <p>(g) No person shall operate upon a highway any two-wheeled bicycle equipped with handlebars so raised that the operator must elevate the hands above the level of the shoulders in order to grasp the normal steering grip area.</p>
          <p>(h) No person shall operate upon a highway any bicycle which is of such a size as to prevent the operator from stopping the bicycle, supporting it with at least one foot on the highway surface and restarting in a safe manner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.6a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6a.<span class="headnote">Electric-assisted bicycle; riding rules.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person may operate an electric-assisted bicycle in the same manner as provided for operation of other bicycles, including but not limited to operation on the shoulder of a roadway, a bicycle lane, and a bicycle route, and operation without the motor engaged on a bikeway or bicycle trail.</p>
          <p>(b) A person may operate a class 1 or class 2 electric-assisted bicycle with the motor engaged on a bicycle path, bicycle trail, or shared use path unless prohibited under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/85.015">85.015</a>, subdivision 1d; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/85.018#stat.85.018.2">85.018, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (d); or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/160.263#stat.160.263.2">160.263, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (b), as applicable.</p>
          <p>(c) A person may operate a class 3 electric-assisted bicycle or multiple mode electric-assisted bicycle with the motor engaged on a bicycle path, bicycle trail, or shared use path unless the local authority or state agency having jurisdiction over the bicycle path or trail prohibits the operation.</p>
          <p>(d) The local authority or state agency having jurisdiction over a trail or over a bike park that is designated as nonmotorized and that has a natural surface tread made by clearing and grading the native soil with no added surfacing materials may regulate the operation of an electric-assisted bicycle.</p>
          <p>(e) A person under the age of 15 must not operate an electric-assisted bicycle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.6b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6b.<span class="headnote">Electric-assisted bicycle; equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The manufacturer or distributor of an electric-assisted bicycle must apply a label to the bicycle that is permanently affixed in a prominent location. The label must contain the class number, top assisted speed, and motor wattage of the electric-assisted bicycle, and must be printed in a legible font with at least 9-point type. A multiple mode electric-assisted bicycle must have labeling that identifies the highest class or each of the electric-assisted bicycle classes in which it is capable of operating.</p>
          <p>(b) A person must not modify an electric-assisted bicycle to change the motor-powered speed capability or motor engagement so that the bicycle no longer meets the requirements for the applicable class, unless:</p>
          <p>(1) the person replaces the label required in paragraph (a) with revised information; or</p>
          <p>(2) for a vehicle that no longer meets the requirements for any electric-assisted bicycle class, the person removes the labeling as an electric-assisted bicycle.</p>
          <p>(c) An electric-assisted bicycle must operate in a manner so that the electric motor is disengaged or ceases to function: (1) when the brakes are applied; or (2) except for a class 2 electric-assisted bicycle or a multiple mode electric-assisted bicycle operating in class 2 mode, when the rider stops pedaling.</p>
          <p>(d) A class 3 electric-assisted bicycle or multiple mode electric-assisted bicycle must be equipped with a speedometer that displays the speed at which the bicycle is traveling in miles per hour.</p>
          <p>(e) A multiple mode electric-assisted bicycle equipped with a throttle must not be capable of exceeding 20 miles per hour on motorized propulsion alone in any mode when the throttle is engaged.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Sale with reflectors and other equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) No person shall sell or offer for sale any new bicycle unless it is equipped with reflectors and other equipment as required by subdivision 6, paragraphs (b) and (e) and by applicable regulations for new bicycles prescribed by the United States Consumer Product Safety Commission.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), a new bicycle may be sold or offered for sale without pedals if the bicycle otherwise meets the requirements of paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Turning, lane change.</span></h2>
          <p>An arm signal to turn right or left shall be given continuously during the last 100 feet traveled by the bicycle before turning, unless the arm is needed to control the bicycle, and shall be given while the bicycle is stopped waiting to turn.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Bicycle parking.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person may park a bicycle on a sidewalk unless prohibited or restricted by local authorities. A bicycle parked on a sidewalk shall not impede the normal and reasonable movement of pedestrian or other traffic.</p>
          <p>(b) A bicycle may be parked on a roadway at any location where parking is allowed if it is parked in such a manner that it does not obstruct the movement of a legally parked motor vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Bicycle events.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Bicycle events, parades, contests, or racing on a highway shall not be unlawful when approved by state or local authorities having jurisdiction over that highway. Approval shall be granted only under conditions which assure reasonable safety for all participants, spectators and other highway users, and which prevent unreasonable interference with traffic flow which would seriously inconvenience other highway users.</p>
          <p>(b) By agreement with the approving authority, participants in an approved bicycle highway event may be exempted from compliance with any traffic laws otherwise applicable thereto, provided that traffic control is adequate to assure the safety of all highway users.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.222.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Peace officer operating bicycle.</span></h2>
          <p>The provisions of this section governing operation of bicycles do not apply to bicycles operated by peace officers while performing their duties.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.222.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/739/#laws.0.12.0">1978 c 739 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/255/#laws.0.14.0">1987 c 255 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.2.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 2</a>; art 7 s 2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/72/#laws.0.2.0">1995 c 72 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/287/#laws.3.29.0">2012 c 287 art 3 s 29</a>-31; art 4 s 20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/127/#laws.0.31.0">2013 c 127 s 31</a>-34; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/5/#laws.4.57.0">1Sp2021 c 5 art 4 s 57</a>-60; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.4.47.0">2023 c 68 art 4 s 47</a>,48; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.3.55.0">2024 c 127 art 3 s 55</a>-57</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.223">
        <h1 class="shn">169.223 MOTORIZED BICYCLE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.223.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Safety equipment; parking.</span></h2>
          <p> Section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.974">169.974</a> relating to motorcycles is applicable to motorized bicycles, except as otherwise provided in this section and except that:</p>
          <p>(1) protective headgear includes headgear that meets the standards under Code of Federal Regulations, title 16, part 1203, or successor requirements;</p>
          <p>(2) a motorized bicycle equipped with a headlight and taillight meeting the requirements of lighting for motorcycles may be operated during nighttime hours;</p>
          <p>(3) protective headgear is not required for operators 18 years of age or older; and</p>
          <p>(4) the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.222">169.222</a>, subdivision 9, governing the parking of bicycles apply to motorized bicycles.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.223.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">License or permit.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A motorized bicycle may be operated under either a driver's license or a motorized bicycle permit issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.02#stat.171.02.3">171.02, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) A person under the age of 16 operating a motorized bicycle under a motorized bicycle permit is subject to the restrictions imposed by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.974#stat.169.974.2">169.974, subdivision 2</a>, on operation of a motorcycle under a two-wheel instruction permit, except that:</p>
          <p>(1) a parent or guardian of an operator under the age of 16 may also ride on the motorized bicycle as a passenger or operator if the motorized bicycle is equipped with a seat and footrests for a second passenger;</p>
          <p>(2) a motorized bicycle equipped with a headlight and taillight meeting the requirements of lighting for motorcycles may be operated during nighttime hours;</p>
          <p>(3) protective headgear includes headgear described in subdivision 1; and</p>
          <p>(4) protective headgear is required only until the operator reaches the age of 18 years.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.223.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sidewalk and passenger prohibitions.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall operate a motorized bicycle upon a sidewalk at any time, except when such operation is necessary for the most direct access to a roadway from a driveway, alley or building. No person shall operate a motorized bicycle that is carrying any person other than the operator, except as allowed under subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.223.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Headlight requirement.</span></h2>
          <p>The provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.974#stat.169.974.5">169.974, subdivision 5</a>, paragraph (k), apply to motorized bicycles that are equipped with headlights. A new motorized bicycle sold or offered for sale in Minnesota must be equipped with a headlight.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.223.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Other operation requirements and prohibitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person operating a motorized bicycle on a roadway shall ride as close as practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway except in one of the following situations:</p>
          <p>(1) when overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction;</p>
          <p>(2) when preparing for a left turn at an intersection or into a private road or driveway; or</p>
          <p>(3) when reasonably necessary to avoid conditions, including fixed or moving objects, vehicles, pedestrians, animals, surface hazards, or narrow width lanes, that make it unsafe to continue along the right-hand curb or edge.</p>
          <p>(b) Persons operating motorized bicycles on a roadway may not ride more than two abreast and may not impede the normal and reasonable movement of traffic. On a laned roadway, a person operating a motorized bicycle shall ride within a single lane.</p>
          <p>(c) This section does not permit the operation of a motorized bicycle on a bicycle path or bicycle lane that is reserved for the exclusive use of nonmotorized traffic.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.223.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/214/#laws.0.8.0">1977 c 214 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/227/#laws.0.1.0">1979 c 227 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/269/#laws.0.5.0">1987 c 269 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/331/#laws.0.22.0">1989 c 331 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/435/#laws.0.15.0">1996 c 435 s 15</a>,16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/287/#laws.3.32.0">2012 c 287 art 3 s 32</a>,33; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/25/#laws.0.80.0">2023 c 25 s 80</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.3.58.0">2024 c 127 art 3 s 58</a></p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendment to subdivision 4 by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 3, section 58, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 3, section 58, the effective date.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.224">
        <h1 class="shn">169.224 NEIGHBORHOOD AND MEDIUM-SPEED ELECTRIC VEHICLES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.224.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">For purposes of this section, "road authority" means the commissioner, as to trunk highways; the county board, as to county state-aid highways and county highways; the town board, as to town roads; and the governing body of a city, as to city streets.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.224.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Required equipment.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Notwithstanding any other law, a neighborhood electric vehicle or a medium-speed electric vehicle may be operated on public streets and highways if it meets all equipment and vehicle safety requirements in Code of Federal Regulations, title 49, section 571.500, and successor requirements.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.224.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Operation.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) A neighborhood electric vehicle or a medium-speed electric vehicle may not be operated on a street or highway with a speed limit greater than 35 miles per hour, except to make a direct crossing of that street or highway.</p>
          <p>(b) A person may operate a three-wheeled neighborhood electric vehicle without a motorcycle endorsement if the person has a valid driver's license issued under chapter 171.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.224.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Restrictions and prohibitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) A road authority, including the commissioner of transportation by order, may prohibit or further restrict the operation of neighborhood electric vehicles and medium-speed electric vehicles on any street or highway under the road authority's jurisdiction.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Neither a neighborhood electric vehicle nor a medium-speed electric vehicle may be used to take any examination to demonstrate ability to exercise control in the operation of a motor vehicle as required under section 171.13.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.224.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/189/#laws.0.5.0">2006 c 189 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.34.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/3/#laws.3.51.0">1Sp2017 c 3 art 3 s 51</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/104/#laws.1.35.0">2024 c 104 art 1 s 35</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">MOTORIZED FOOT SCOOTER</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.225">
        <h1 class="shn">169.225 MOTORIZED FOOT SCOOTER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.225.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application of traffic laws.</span></h2>
          <p>Every person operating a motorized foot scooter shall have all rights and duties applicable to the operator of a bicycle, except in respect to those provisions relating expressly to motorized foot scooters and in respect to those provisions of law that by their nature cannot reasonably be applied to motorized foot scooters.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.225.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Sidewalk and passenger prohibition.</span></h2>
          <p>No person may operate a motorized foot scooter upon a sidewalk, except when necessary to enter or leave adjacent property. No person may operate a motorized foot scooter that is carrying any person other than the operator.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.225.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Minimum age for operator.</span></h2>
          <p>No person under the age of 12 years may operate a motorized foot scooter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.225.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Protective headgear.</span></h2>
          <p>No person under the age of 18 years may operate a motorized foot scooter without wearing properly fitted and fastened protective headgear that complies with standards established by the commissioner of public safety.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.225.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Required lighting equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>A motorized foot scooter must be equipped with a headlight and a taillight that comply with standards established by the commissioner of public safety if the vehicle is operated under conditions when vehicle lights are required by law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.225.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Operation requirements and prohibitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person operating a motorized foot scooter on a roadway shall ride as close as practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway, except in the following situations:</p>
          <p>(1) when overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction;</p>
          <p>(2) when preparing for a left turn, in which case the operator shall stop and dismount at the right-hand curb or right edge of the roadway, and shall complete the turn by crossing the roadway on foot, subject to restrictions placed by law on pedestrians; or</p>
          <p>(3) when reasonably necessary to avoid impediments or conditions that make it unsafe to continue along the right-hand curb or edge, including, but not limited to, fixed or moving objects, vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians, animals, surface hazards, or narrow lanes.</p>
          <p>(b) A person may operate a motorized foot scooter on a bicycle path, bicycle lane, bicycle trail, or bikeway that is not reserved for the exclusive use of nonmotorized traffic, unless the local authority or governing body having jurisdiction over that path, lane, trail, or bikeway prohibits operation by law.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.225.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/135/#laws.0.6.0">2005 c 135 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.228"><b>169.228</b> MS 2012 [Expired, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.35.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 35</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.23"><b>169.23</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1965/0/45/#laws.0.73.0">1965 c 45 s 73</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.24"><b>169.24</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/0/561/#laws.0.17.0">1961 c 561 s 17</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.25"><b>169.25</b> MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/104/#laws.1.110.0">2024 c 104 art 1 s 110</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">RAILROAD CROSSINGS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.26">
        <h1 class="shn">169.26 SPECIAL STOPS AT RAILROAD CROSSING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.26.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.28#stat.169.28.1">169.28, subdivision 1</a>, when any person driving a vehicle approaches a railroad grade crossing under any of the circumstances stated in this paragraph, the driver shall stop the vehicle not less than ten feet from the nearest railroad track and shall not proceed until safe to do so and until the roadway is clear of traffic so that the vehicle can proceed without stopping until the rear of the vehicle is at least ten feet past the farthest railroad track. These requirements apply when:</p>
          <p>(1) a clearly visible electric or mechanical signal device warns of the immediate approach of a railroad train or other on-track equipment; or</p>
          <p>(2) an approaching railroad train or other on-track equipment is plainly visible and is in hazardous proximity.</p>
          <p>(b) The fact that a moving railroad train or other on-track equipment approaching a railroad grade crossing is visible from the crossing is prima facie evidence that it is not safe to proceed.</p>
          <p>(c) The driver of a vehicle shall stop and remain stopped and not traverse the grade crossing when (1) a human flagger signals the approach or passage of a railroad train or other on-track equipment, or (2) a crossing gate is lowered warning of the immediate approach or passage of a railroad train or other on-track equipment. No person may drive a vehicle past a flagger at a railroad crossing until the flagger signals that the way is clear to proceed or drive a vehicle past a lowered crossing gate.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.26.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Violation.</span></h2>
          <p>A police officer may arrest the driver of a motor vehicle if the police officer has probable cause to believe that the driver has operated the vehicle in violation of subdivision 1 within the past four hours.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.26.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A driver who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) The owner or, in the case of a leased vehicle, the lessee of a motor vehicle is guilty of a petty misdemeanor if a motor vehicle owned or leased by that person is operated in violation of subdivision 1. This paragraph does not apply to a lessor of a motor vehicle if the lessor keeps a record of the name and address of the lessee. This paragraph does not apply if the motor vehicle operator is prosecuted for violating subdivision 1. A violation of this paragraph does not constitute grounds for revocation or suspension of the owner's or lessee's driver's license.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.26.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Driver training.</span></h2>
          <p>All driver education courses approved by the commissioner of public safety must include instruction on railroad-highway grade crossing safety. The commissioner of public safety shall by rule establish minimum standards of course content relating to operation of vehicles at railroad-highway grade crossings.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.26.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Pedestrians; penalty.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) A pedestrian shall not pass through, around, over, or under any crossing gate or barrier at a railroad grade crossing while the gate or barrier is closed or is being opened or closed.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) A pedestrian shall not enter, remain upon, or traverse over a railroad track, grade crossing, or pedestrian walkway crossing a railroad track when an audible bell or clearly visible electric or mechanical signal device is operational and warning of the presence, approach, passage, or departure of a railroad train or other on-track equipment.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) A person who violates this subdivision is subject to a fine of up to $100.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.26.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-211</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.61.0">1937 c 464 s 61</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/468/#laws.0.2.0">1990 c 468 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/298/#laws.2.2.0">1991 c 298 art 2 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.16.13.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 16 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/403/#laws.0.13.0">1998 c 403 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/371/#laws.1.43.0">2002 c 371 art 1 s 43</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.10.7.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 10 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/229/#laws.0.1.0">2004 c 229 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/351/#laws.0.30.0">2010 c 351 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.42.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 42</a>,43</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.27"><b>169.27</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/166/#laws.0.119.0">1976 c 166 s 119</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.28">
        <h1 class="shn">169.28 CERTAIN VEHICLES TO STOP AT RAILROAD CROSSING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.28.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The driver of any motor vehicle carrying passengers for hire, or of any school bus whether carrying passengers or not, or of any Head Start bus whether carrying passengers or not, or of any vehicle that is required to stop at railroad grade crossings under Code of Federal Regulations, title 49, section 392.10, before crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad, shall stop the vehicle not less than 15 feet nor more than 50 feet from the nearest rail of the railroad and while so stopped shall listen and look in both directions along the track for any approaching railroad train or other on-track equipment, and for signals indicating the approach of a railroad train or other on-track equipment, except as otherwise provided in this section. The driver must not proceed until safe to do so and until the roadway is clear of traffic so that the vehicle can proceed without stopping until the rear of the vehicle is at least ten feet past the farthest railroad track. The driver must not shift gears while crossing the railroad tracks.</p>
          <p>(b) A school bus or Head Start bus shall not be flagged across railroad grade crossings except at those railroad grade crossings that the local school administrative officer may designate.</p>
          <p>(c) A type III vehicle, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.011">169.011</a>, is exempt from the requirement of school buses to stop at railroad grade crossings.</p>
          <p>(d) The requirements of this subdivision do not apply to the crossing of light rail vehicle track or tracks that are located in a public street when:</p>
          <p>(1) the crossing occurs within the intersection of two or more public streets;</p>
          <p>(2) the intersection is controlled by a traffic-control signal; and</p>
          <p>(3) the intersection is marked with signs indicating to drivers that the requirements of this subdivision do not apply. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the owner or operator of the track or tracks is authorized to place, maintain, and display the signs upon and in the view of the public street or streets.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.28.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Exempt crossing.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner may designate a crossing as an exempt crossing:</p>
          <p>(1) if the crossing is on a rail line on which service has been abandoned;</p>
          <p>(2) if the crossing is on a rail line that carries fewer than five railroad trains each year, traveling at speeds of ten miles per hour or less; or</p>
          <p>(3) as agreed to by the operating railroad and the Department of Transportation, following a diagnostic review of the crossing.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner shall direct the railroad to erect at the crossing signs bearing the word "Exempt" that conform to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06">169.06</a>. The installation or presence of an exempt sign does not relieve a driver of the duty to use due care.</p>
          <p>(c) A railroad train or other on-track equipment must not proceed across an exempt crossing unless a police officer is present to direct traffic or a railroad employee is on the ground to warn traffic until the railroad train enters the crossing.</p>
          <p>(d) A vehicle that must stop at grade crossings under subdivision 1 is not required to stop at a marked exempt crossing unless directed otherwise by a police officer or a railroad employee.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.28.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-213</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.63.0">1937 c 464 s 63</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/1/38/#laws.0.1.0">Ex1937 c 38 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/0/29/#laws.0.1.0">1961 c 29 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/146/#laws.0.2.0">1969 c 146 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/444/#laws.0.1.0">1982 c 444 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/397/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 397 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/603/#laws.0.3.0">1994 c 603 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/371/#laws.1.44.0">2002 c 371 art 1 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.1.44.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 1 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/229/#laws.0.2.0">2004 c 229 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/245/#laws.0.1.0">2004 c 245 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/6/#laws.3.46.0">1Sp2005 c 6 art 3 s 46</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.96.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 96</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.44.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 44</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.29">
        <h1 class="shn">169.29 CROSSING RAILROAD TRACKS WITH CERTAIN EQUIPMENT.</h1>
        <p>(a) No person shall operate or move any caterpillar tractor, steam shovel, derrick, roller, or any equipment or structure having a normal operating speed of six or less miles per hour or a vertical body or load clearance of less than nine inches above the level surface of a roadway upon or across any tracks at a railroad grade crossing without first complying with this section.</p>
        <p>(b) Before making any crossing, the person operating or moving any vehicle or equipment set forth in this section shall first stop the same not less than ten, nor more than 50, feet from the nearest rail of the railway, and while so stopped shall listen and look in both directions along the track for any approaching railroad train or other on-track equipment and for signals indicating the approach of a railroad train or other on-track equipment, and shall not proceed until the crossing can be made safely.</p>
        <p>(c) No crossing shall be made when warning is given by automatic signal or crossing gates or a flagger or otherwise of the immediate approach of a railroad train or other on-track equipment or car.</p>
        <p>(d) A stop is not required at a crossing on a rail line on which service has been abandoned and where a sign erected in conformance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06">169.06</a> and bearing the word "Exempt" has been installed, unless directed otherwise by a flagger. The installation or presence of an exempt sign shall not relieve any driver of the duty to use due care.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.29.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-214</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.64.0">1937 c 464 s 64</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/444/#laws.0.2.0">1982 c 444 s 2</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.45.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CONTROLLED-ACCESS AND THROUGH HIGHWAYS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.30">
        <h1 class="shn">169.30 DESIGNATION OF THROUGH HIGHWAYS.</h1>
        <p>(a) The commissioner, with reference to state trunk highways, and local authorities, with reference to other highways under their jurisdiction, may designate through highways by erecting stop signs or yield signs at entrances thereto or may designate any intersection as a stop or yield intersection by erecting like signs at one or more entrances to such intersection; provided, that local authorities, with the consent of the commissioner, may designate through highway or stop or yield intersections on state trunk highways.</p>
        <p>(b) Every driver of a vehicle shall stop at a stop sign or at a clearly marked stop line before entering the intersection, except when directed to proceed by a police officer or traffic-control signal.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.30.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-215</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.65.0">1937 c 464 s 65</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.11.0">1939 c 430 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/0/16/#laws.0.1.0">1961 c 16 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.305">
        <h1 class="shn">169.305 CONTROLLED-ACCESS RULES AND PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.305.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Entrance and exit; crossover; use regulations; signs; rules.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) No person shall drive a vehicle onto or from any controlled-access highway except at such entrances and exits as are established by public authority.</p>
          <p>(b) When special crossovers between the main roadways of a controlled-access highway are provided for emergency vehicles or maintenance equipment and such crossovers are signed to prohibit "U" turns, it shall be unlawful for any vehicle, except an emergency vehicle, maintenance equipment, construction equipment including contractor's and state-owned equipment when operating within a marked construction zone, or a vehicle operated by a commercial vehicle inspector of the Department of Public Safety, to use such crossover. Vehicles owned and operated by elderly and needy persons under contract with the commissioner of transportation pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/160.282">160.282</a> for maintenance services on highway rest stop and tourist centers outside the seven-county metropolitan area as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/473.121">473.121</a>, may also use these crossovers while those persons are proceeding to or from work in the rest area or tourist center if authorized by the commissioner, and the vehicle carries on its roof a distinctive flag designed and issued by the commissioner. For the purposes of this clause "emergency vehicle" includes a tow truck or towing vehicle if it is on the way to the location of an accident or a disabled vehicle.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner of transportation may by order, and any public authority may by ordinance, with respect to any controlled-access highway under their jurisdictions prohibit or regulate the use of any such highway by pedestrians, bicycles, or other nonmotorized traffic, or by motorized bicycles, or by any class or kind of traffic which is found to be incompatible with the normal and safe flow of traffic.</p>
          <p>(d) The commissioner of transportation or the public authority adopting any such prohibitory rules shall erect and maintain official signs on the controlled-access highway on which such rules are applicable and when so erected no person shall disobey the restrictions stated on such signs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.305.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Backing.</span></h2>
          <p>Except for a driver of an authorized emergency vehicle in the course of performing duties, no driver of a vehicle shall back the same upon the roadway or shoulder of any controlled-access highway.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.305.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Petty misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who violates the provisions of this section or any order or ordinance promulgated or enacted by the commissioner of transportation or a public authority pursuant thereto is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.305.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/439/#laws.0.1.0">1959 c 439 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/0/72/#laws.0.1.0">1961 c 72 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/236/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 236 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.9.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/406/#laws.0.39.0">1974 c 406 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/166/#laws.0.7.0">1976 c 166 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/214/#laws.0.9.0">1977 c 214 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/494/#laws.0.2.0">1978 c 494 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/533/#laws.0.12.0">1980 c 533 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/112/#laws.0.5.0">1991 c 112 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/186/#laws.0.119.0">1995 c 186 s 119</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/312/#laws.11.9.0">2014 c 312 art 11 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.63.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 63</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">BUS USE OF SHOULDERS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.306">
        <h1 class="shn">169.306 USE OF SHOULDERS BY BUSES.</h1>
        <p>(a) A road authority, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/160.02#stat.160.02.25">160.02, subdivision 25</a>, is authorized to permit transit buses and Metro Mobility buses use of a shoulder, as designated by the road authority, of a freeway or expressway, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/160.02">160.02</a>, in Minnesota.</p>
        <p>(b) If a road authority permits the use of a freeway or expressway shoulder by transit buses, the road authority shall permit the use on that shoulder of a bus (1) with a seating capacity of 40 passengers or more operated by a motor carrier of passengers, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/221.012#stat.221.012.26">221.012, subdivision 26</a>, while operating in intrastate commerce or (2) providing regular route transit service, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/174.22#stat.174.22.8">174.22, subdivision 8</a>, or Metro Mobility services, and operated by or under contract with the Metropolitan Council, a local transit authority, or a transit authority created by the legislature. Drivers of these buses must have adequate training in the requirements of paragraph (c), as determined by the commissioner.</p>
        <p>(c) Buses authorized to use the shoulder under this section may be operated on the shoulder only when main-line traffic speeds are less than 35 miles per hour, except as provided for in paragraph (f). Drivers of buses being operated on the shoulder may not exceed the speed of main-line traffic by more than 15 miles per hour and may never exceed 35 miles per hour, except as provided for in paragraph (f). Drivers of buses being operated on the shoulder must yield to merging, entering, and exiting traffic and must yield to other vehicles on the shoulder. Buses operated on the shoulder must be registered with the Department of Transportation.</p>
        <p>(d) For the purposes of this section, the term "Metro Mobility bus" means a motor vehicle of not less than 20 feet in length engaged in providing special transportation services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/473.386">473.386</a> that is:</p>
        <p>(1) operated by or under contract with a public or private entity receiving financial assistance to provide transit services from the Metropolitan Council or the commissioner of transportation; and</p>
        <p>(2) authorized by a road authority to use freeway or expressway shoulders.</p>
        <p>(e) This section does not apply to the operation of buses on dynamic shoulder lanes.</p>
        <p>(f) The commissioner may authorize different operating conditions and maximum speeds, not to exceed the posted speed limit, based upon an engineering study and recommendation by the road authority. The engineering study must be conducted by the road authority and must conform with the manual and specifications adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06#stat.169.06.1">169.06, subdivision 1</a>, and applicable state and federal standards. The road authority shall consult the public transit operator before recommending operating conditions different from those authorized by law.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.306.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/364/#laws.0.10.0">2002 c 364 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/51/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 51 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/306/#laws.0.5.0">2008 c 306 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/351/#laws.0.31.0">2010 c 351 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/287/#laws.4.21.0">2012 c 287 art 4 s 21</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">OTHER TRAFFIC RULES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.31">
        <h1 class="shn">169.31 STOP AT SIDEWALK.</h1>
        <p>The driver of a vehicle within a business or residence district emerging from an alley, driveway, or building shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to driving onto a sidewalk or into the sidewalk area and shall yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian and all other traffic on the sidewalk.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.31.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-216</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.66.0">1937 c 464 s 66</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/739/#laws.0.13.0">1978 c 739 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.315">
        <h1 class="shn">169.315 OPENING AND CLOSING VEHICLE DOOR.</h1>
        <p>No person shall open any door on a motor vehicle unless and until it is reasonably safe to do so and can be done without interfering with the movement of other traffic. No person shall allow any door on the side of a vehicle adjacent to moving traffic to remain open for a period of time longer than necessary to load or unload passengers.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.315.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/739/#laws.0.14.0">1978 c 739 s 14</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">STOPPING, PARKING PROVISIONS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.32">
        <h1 class="shn">169.32 STOPPING, STANDING, AND PARKING.</h1>
        <p>(a) Upon any highway outside of a business or residence district no person shall stop, park, or leave standing any vehicle, whether attended or unattended, upon the paved or improved or main-traveled part of the highway when it is practical to stop, park, or so leave such vehicle off such part of said highway, but in every event a clear and unobstructed width of at least 20 feet of such part of the highway opposite such standing vehicle shall be left for the free passage of other vehicles and a clear view of such stopped vehicle be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.</p>
        <p>(b) This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or improved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such a manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.</p>
        <p>(c) This section shall not apply to the driver of a school bus stopped for the purpose of receiving or discharging any school child or school children provided the school bus is equipped and identified as provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.441">169.441</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.442#stat.169.442.1">169.442, subdivision 1</a>, and is displaying the flashing red lamps and stop arm required therein.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.32.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-217</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.67.0">1937 c 464 s 67</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/146/#laws.0.3.0">1969 c 146 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.17.0">1991 c 277 s 17</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.33">
        <h1 class="shn">169.33 POLICE MAY MOVE VEHICLE.</h1>
        <p>(a) When any police officer finds a vehicle standing upon a highway in violation of any of the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.32">169.32</a>, such officer is hereby authorized to move such vehicle, or require the driver or other person in charge of the vehicle to move the same, to a position off the paved or improved or main-traveled part of such highway.</p>
        <p>(b) When any police officer finds a vehicle unattended upon any street or highway or upon any bridge or causeway or in any tunnel where such vehicle constitutes an obstruction to traffic, such officer is hereby authorized to provide for the removal of such vehicle and remove the same to the nearest convenient garage or other place of safety.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.33.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-218</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.68.0">1937 c 464 s 68</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.12.0">1939 c 430 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.34">
        <h1 class="shn">169.34 PROHIBITIONS; STOPPING, PARKING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.34.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Prohibitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) A person must not stop, stand, or park a vehicle, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or traffic-control device, in any of the following places:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) on a sidewalk;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) in front of a public or private driveway;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) within an intersection;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) within ten feet of a fire hydrant;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) on a crosswalk;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) within 30 feet upon the approach to any flashing beacon, stop sign, or traffic-control signal located at the side of a roadway;</p>
          <p class="in">(8) within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing;</p>
          <p class="in">(9) within 20 feet of the driveway entrance to any fire station and on the side of a street opposite the entrance to any fire station within 75 feet of said entrance when properly signposted;</p>
          <p class="in">(10) alongside or opposite any street excavation or obstruction when such stopping, standing, or parking would obstruct traffic;</p>
          <p class="in">(11) on the roadway side of any vehicle stopped or parked at the edge or curb of a street;</p>
          <p class="in">(12) upon any bridge or other elevated structure upon a highway or within a highway tunnel, except as otherwise provided by ordinance;</p>
          <p>(13) within a bicycle lane, except when posted signs permit parking; or</p>
          <p class="in">(14) at any place where official signs prohibit stopping.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) A person must not move a vehicle not owned by the person into any prohibited area or away from a curb such distance as is unlawful.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) A person must not, for camping purposes, leave or park a travel trailer on or within the limits of any highway or on any highway right-of-way, except where signs are erected designating the place as a campsite.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) A person must not stop or park a vehicle on a street or highway when directed or ordered to proceed by any peace officer invested by law with authority to direct, control, or regulate traffic.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.34.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Violation; penalty for owner or lessee.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) If a motor vehicle is stopped, standing, or parked in violation of subdivision 1, the owner of the vehicle, or for a leased motor vehicle the lessee of the vehicle, is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) The owner or lessee may not be fined under paragraph (a) if (1) another person is convicted for, or pleads guilty to, that violation, or (2) the motor vehicle was stolen at the time of the violation.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) Paragraph (a) does not apply to a lessor of a motor vehicle if the lessor keeps a record of the name and address of the lessee.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) Paragraph (a) does not prohibit or limit the prosecution of a motor vehicle operator who violates subdivision 1.</p>
          <p class="in">(e) A violation under paragraph (a) does not constitute grounds for revocation or suspension of the owner's or lessee's driver's license.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.34.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-219</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.69.0">1937 c 464 s 69</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/1/38/#laws.0.1.0">Ex1937 c 38 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.13.0">1939 c 430 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/342/#laws.0.16.0">1989 c 342 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/287/#laws.1.46.0">2008 c 287 art 1 s 46</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/127/#laws.0.35.0">2013 c 127 s 35</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.64.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 64</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/104/#laws.1.36.0">2024 c 104 art 1 s 36</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.342">
        <h1 class="shn">169.342 GOOD SAMARITAN; EXCEPTION TO STOPPING AND PARKING.</h1>
        <p>(a) A person who stops or parks that person's motor vehicle on any highway or street for the sole purpose of aiding another motorist who signals for assistance by raising the hood of the vehicle or displaying a flag, flare or similar signal is not in violation of any law, ordinance, or rule prohibiting the stopping or parking of a motor vehicle, and no peace officer shall issue a traffic ticket therefor if:</p>
        <p>(1) the motorist in distress is not already being given aid or assistance;</p>
        <p>(2) the person takes reasonable safety precautions in stopping and parking the vehicle, and conforms with other laws regulating the stopping and parking of vehicles;</p>
        <p>(3) the person is not in violation of traffic laws or rules other than the prohibition against stopping and parking; and</p>
        <p>(4) the person promptly leaves the scene if directed to leave by a peace officer.</p>
        <p>(b) This section does not apply to any person who stops or parks a vehicle next to an unattended vehicle.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.342.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/167/#laws.0.1.0">1977 c 167 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.345">
        <h1 class="shn">169.345 PARKING PRIVILEGE FOR PHYSICALLY DISABLED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.345.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope of privilege.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A vehicle described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a>, subdivision 1, paragraph (a), that prominently displays the certificate authorized by this section or that bears the disability plate or plates issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a> may be parked by or solely for the benefit of a physically disabled person:</p>
          <p>(1) in a designated parking space for disabled persons, as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.346">169.346</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) in a metered parking space without obligation to pay the meter fee and without time restrictions unless time restrictions are separately posted on official signs; and</p>
          <p>(3) without time restrictions in a nonmetered space where parking is otherwise allowed for passenger vehicles but restricted to a maximum period of time and that does not specifically prohibit the exercise of disabled parking privileges in that space.</p>
          <p class="bl">A person may park the vehicle for a physically disabled person in a parking space described in clause (1) or (2) only when actually transporting the physically disabled person for the sole benefit of that person and when the parking space is within a reasonable distance from the drop-off point.</p>
          <p>(b) For purposes of this subdivision, a certificate is prominently displayed if it is displayed so that it may be viewed from the front and rear of the motor vehicle by hanging it from the rearview mirror attached to the front windshield of the motor vehicle or, in the case of a motorcycle or a motorized bicycle, is secured to the vehicle. If there is no rearview mirror or if the certificate holder's disability precludes placing the certificate on the mirror, the certificate must be displayed on the dashboard of the vehicle. No part of the certificate may be obscured.</p>
          <p>(c) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), clauses (1), (2), and (3), this section does not permit parking in areas prohibited by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.32">169.32</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.34">169.34</a>, in designated no parking spaces, or in parking spaces reserved for specified purposes or vehicles.
