A local governmental unit may, by ordinance, prohibit parking on any street or highway to create a fire lane, or to accommodate heavy traffic during morning and afternoon rush hours and these ordinances also apply to physically disabled persons.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.345.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For the purpose of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a> and this section, the following terms have the meanings given them in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) "Health professional" means a licensed physician, licensed physician assistant, advanced practice registered nurse, licensed physical therapist, or licensed chiropractor.</p>
          <p>(c) "Long-term certificate" means a certificate issued for a period greater than 12 months but not greater than 71 months.</p>
          <p>(d) "Organization certificate" means a certificate issued to an entity other than a natural person for a period of three years.</p>
          <p>(e) "Permit" refers to a permit that is issued for a period of 30 days, in lieu of the certificate referred to in subdivision 3, while the application is being processed.</p>
          <p>(f) "Physically disabled person" means a person who:</p>
          <p>(1) because of disability cannot walk without significant risk of falling;</p>
          <p>(2) because of disability cannot walk 200 feet without stopping to rest;</p>
          <p>(3) because of disability cannot walk without the aid of another person, a walker, a cane, crutches, braces, a prosthetic device, or a wheelchair;</p>
          <p>(4) is restricted by a respiratory disease to such an extent that the person's forced (respiratory) expiratory volume for one second, when measured by spirometry, is less than one liter;</p>
          <p>(5) has an arterial oxygen tension (PaO<sub>2</sub>) of less than 60 mm/Hg on room air at rest;</p>
          <p>(6) uses portable oxygen;</p>
          <p>(7) has a cardiac condition to the extent that the person's functional limitations are classified in severity as class III or class IV according to standards set by the American Heart Association;</p>
          <p>(8) has lost an arm or a leg and does not have or cannot use an artificial limb;</p>
          <p>(9) has a disability that would be aggravated by walking 200 feet under normal environmental conditions to an extent that would be life threatening; or</p>
          <p>(10) is legally blind.</p>
          <p>(g) A pregnant person experiencing any of the conditions described in paragraph (f) is eligible for parking privileges pursuant to this section.</p>
          <p>(h) "Short-term certificate" means a certificate issued for a period greater than six months but not greater than 12 months.</p>
          <p>(i) "Six-year certificate" means a certificate issued for a period of six years.</p>
          <p>(j) "Temporary certificate" means a certificate issued for a period not greater than six months.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.345.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Health professional's medical statement.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall develop a format for the medical statement. The medical statement must be signed by a health professional who certifies that the applicant is a physically disabled person as defined in subdivision 2. The commissioner may request additional information from the health professional if needed to verify the applicant's eligibility. The medical statement that the applicant is a physically disabled person must specify whether the disability is permanent or temporary and, if temporary, the opinion of the health professional as to the duration of the disability. A health professional who fraudulently certifies to the commissioner that a person is a physically disabled person as defined in subdivision 2, and that the person is entitled to the disability plates authorized by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a> or to the certificate authorized by this section, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is subject to a fine of $500.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner may waive the requirement of providing a statement of a health professional if the applicant has previously filed with the commissioner a statement of a health professional certifying that the applicant has a permanent physical disability.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.345.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Identifying certificate.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall issue (1) immediately, a permit valid for 30 days if the person is eligible for the certificate issued under this section and (2) an identifying certificate for a vehicle described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a>, subdivision 1, paragraph (a), when a physically disabled applicant submits proof of physical disability under subdivision 2a. The commissioner shall design separate certificates for persons with permanent and temporary disabilities that can be readily distinguished from each other from outside a vehicle at a distance of 25 feet or, in the case of a motorcycle or a motorized bicycle, can be readily secured to the motorcycle or motorized bicycle. An applicant may be issued up to two certificates if the applicant has not been issued disability plates under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The operator of a vehicle displaying a certificate has the parking privileges provided in subdivision 1 only while the vehicle is actually parked while transporting a physically disabled person.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner shall cancel all certificates issued to an applicant who fails to comply with the requirements of this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.345.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Organization certificates.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An organization providing transportation to one or more physically disabled persons may apply to the commissioner for one or more organization certificates for motor vehicles owned or operated on behalf of the organization.</p>
          <p>(b) The organization shall submit a written statement of intent to the commissioner signed by an officer of the organization. The statement must:</p>
          <p>(1) indicate the number of certificates requested;</p>
          <p>(2) state that all issued certificates must be used solely for the benefit of physically disabled persons;</p>
          <p>(3) state that the organization shall report lost or stolen certificates to the commissioner within 24 hours of first discovery; and</p>
          <p>(4) state that the organization shall immediately notify the commissioner of any misuse or suspected misuse of any certificate issued to the organization.</p>
          <p>(c) An organization shall include with the application a description of the internal controls to be used to ensure the proper use of certificates and to account for all issued certificates. The controls must include:</p>
          <p>(1) maintenance of a current list of the make, model, and plate number of all motor vehicles in which a certificate issued to the organization will be used; and</p>
          <p>(2) maintenance of a current list of the name and driver's license number of all individuals authorized to operate the motor vehicle in which certificates issued to the organization will be used.</p>
          <p>(d) When the commissioner is satisfied that an organization will use a certificate to transport physically disabled persons, the commissioner shall issue without charge (1) immediately, a permit valid for 30 days if the organization is eligible for a certificate and (2) an organization certificate for the motor vehicle.</p>
          <p>(e) The certificate issued to an organization transporting physically disabled persons must be renewed every third year. On original application and renewal, the organization must present evidence that each certificate issued continues to be used exclusively to transport physically disabled persons.</p>
          <p>(f) The commissioner shall cancel all certificates issued to an applicant who fails to comply with the requirements of this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.345.3b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3b.<span class="headnote">Certificate design, format, information.</span></h2>
          <p>A certificate must be made of plastic or similar durable material and must bear its expiration date prominently on both sides. A certificate issued to a temporarily disabled person must display the date of expiration of the duration of the disability, as determined under subdivision 3 or 3a. Each applicant must be provided a summary of the parking privileges and restrictions that apply to each motor vehicle for which the certificate is used.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.345.3c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3c.<span class="headnote">Fees; organization, temporary, and short-term certificates.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may charge a fee of $5 for issuance of each organization certificate, each temporary certificate, and each short-term certificate and a fee of $5 for a duplicate to replace a lost, stolen, or damaged organization, temporary, or short-term certificate. The commissioner shall not issue more than three duplicate certificates for lost, stolen, or canceled certificates within any six-year period without the approval of the Minnesota State Council on Disability.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.345.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Unauthorized use or noncompliance; cancellation; misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If a peace officer, authorized parking enforcement employee or agent of a statutory or home rule charter city or town, representative of the Minnesota State Council on Disability, or an authorized agent of a citizen enforcement program under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.346#stat.169.346.4">169.346, subdivision 4</a>, finds that a certificate, permit, or disability plate is being improperly used, or the applicant is no longer eligible, the officer, municipal employee, representative, or agent shall report the violation or situation to the commissioner. The commissioner may cancel the certificate, permit, or disability plates issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a> on determining that:</p>
          <p>(1) the certificate, permit, or plates were used improperly;</p>
          <p>(2) the certificate, permit, or plates were fraudulently obtained;</p>
          <p>(3) the certificate, permit, or plates were issued in error;</p>
          <p>(4) the person who was issued the certificate, permit, or plates is deceased;</p>
          <p>(5) the person who was issued the certificate, permit, or plates no longer maintains a Minnesota address; or</p>
          <p>(6) the person or organization has failed to comply with the requirements of this section.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who uses a certificate, permit, or disability plates in violation of this section is guilty of a misdemeanor and is subject to a fine of $500.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.345.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/389/#laws.0.2.0">1967 c 389 s 2</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="section" id="stat.169.346">
        <h1 class="shn">169.346 DISABILITY PARKING AREAS; CRITERIA, ENFORCEMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.346.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Disability parking space prohibitions.</span></h2>
          <p>A person shall not:</p>
          <p>(1) park a motor vehicle in or obstruct access to a parking space or associated access aisle designated and reserved for the physically disabled, on either private or public property;</p>
          <p>(2) park a motor vehicle in or obstruct access to an area designated by a local governmental unit as a transfer zone for disabled persons;</p>
          <p>(3) alter a certificate;</p>
          <p>(4) exercise the parking privilege provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.345">169.345</a>, unless:</p>
          <p>(i) that person is a physically disabled person as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.345#stat.169.345.2">169.345, subdivision 2</a>, or the person is transporting or parking a motor vehicle for a physically disabled person; and</p>
          <p>(ii) the motor vehicle visibly displays one of the following: a disability plate issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a>, a certificate issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.345">169.345</a>, a permit valid for 30 days issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.345">169.345</a>, or an equivalent certificate, insignia, or plate issued by another state, a foreign country, or one of its political subdivisions; or</p>
          <p>(5) park a motor vehicle in an area used as a regular route transit stopping point where a transit vehicle that is accessible to the physically disabled regularly stops and a sign that bears the international symbol of access in white on blue is posted. A sign posted under this clause may display other information relating to the regular route transit service. For purposes of this clause, an area used as a regular route transit stopping point consists of the 80 feet immediately preceding the sign described in this clause.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.346.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Disability parking when designated spaces occupied or unavailable.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event the designated disability parking spaces are either occupied or unavailable, a vehicle bearing a valid disability parking certificate issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.345">169.345</a> or license plates for physically disabled persons under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a> may park at an angle and occupy two standard parking spaces.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.346.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Disability parking space signs.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Parking spaces reserved for physically disabled persons must be designated and identified by the posting of signs incorporating the international symbol of access in white on blue and indicating that violators are subject to a fine of up to $200. These parking spaces are reserved for disabled persons with motor vehicles displaying the required certificate, plates, permit valid for 30 days, or insignia.</p>
          <p>(b) For purposes of this subdivision, a parking space that is clearly identified as reserved for physically disabled persons by a permanently posted sign that does not meet all design standards, is considered designated and reserved for physically disabled persons. A sign posted for the purpose of this section must be visible from inside a motor vehicle parked in the space, be kept clear of snow or other obstructions which block its visibility, and be nonmovable.</p>
          <p>(c) By August 1, 2024, the Minnesota Council on Disability must select and propose a statewide uniform disability parking space sign that is consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act. The selected and proposed sign must not display any variation of the word "handicapped." As part of selecting and proposing a statewide uniform disability parking space sign, the Minnesota Council on Disability may encourage owners or managers of property to replace existing disability parking space signs at the owner's earliest opportunity once the sign is made available for distribution.</p>
          <p>(d) Beginning on August 1, 2025, an applicable owner or manager of property on which a disability parking sign may be located must install and display the new uniform disability parking sign required in paragraph (c) at:</p>
          <p>(1) newly created on-site parking facilities; and</p>
          <p>(2) existing on-site parking facilities when the manager or owner replaces existing disability parking space signs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.346.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Parking space free of obstruction; penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>The owner or manager of the property on which the designated parking space is located must ensure that the parking space and associated access aisle are kept free of obstruction. If the owner or manager does not have the parking space properly posted or knowingly allows the parking space or access aisle to be blocked by plowed snow, merchandise, or similar obstructions, the owner or manager is guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to a fine of up to $500.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.346.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor; enforcement.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor and must be fined not less than $100 and not more than $200. This subdivision must be enforced in the same manner as parking ordinances or regulations in the governmental subdivision in which the violation occurs. Law enforcement officers may tag motor vehicles parked on either private or public property in violation of subdivision 1. Parking enforcement employees or agents of statutory or home rule charter cities or towns may tag or otherwise issue citations for motor vehicles parked on public property in violation of subdivision 1. If a holder of a disability certificate or disability plates allows a person who is not otherwise eligible to use the certificate or plates, then the holder is not eligible to be issued or to use a disability certificate or plates for 12 months after the date of violation. Except when the permit or certificate is expired by, or is otherwise invalid for, more than 90 days, a physically disabled person, or a person parking a motor vehicle for a disabled person, who is charged with violating subdivision 1 because the person parked in a parking space for physically disabled persons without the required certificate, license plates, or permit must not be convicted if the person (1) produces in court or before the court appearance the required certificate, permit, or evidence that the person has been issued plates under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.021">168.021</a>, (2) surrenders the expired permit or certificate, and (3) demonstrates entitlement to the certificate, plates, or permit at the time of arrest or tagging. To be valid, the certificate or permit must show that it is owned by the same person that owned the expired certificate or permit displayed at the time the tag was issued. The registered vehicle owner is subject to the provisions of this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.346.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Local ordinance; citizen enforcement program.</span></h2>
          <p>A statutory or home rule charter city may, by ordinance, establish a program to enforce the parking restrictions of this section or any similar local ordinance, relating to parking spaces for the physically disabled, by using citizen volunteers to issue citations to violators. The ordinance shall contain a process for training program participants in the requirements of the law, the method of issuing citations, and other related matters. Program participants who satisfy the training requirements of the ordinance are authorized to issue citations for violations of this section and are exempt from any other training or licensure requirements imposed on law enforcement officers by chapter 626.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.346.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Local ordinance; long-term parking.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A statutory or home rule charter city may enact an ordinance establishing a permit program for long-term disability parking. If a city enacts the ordinance, a permit program for long-term disability parking must establish as a minimum:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) a limitation on disability parking of a maximum of four hours during the hours of enforcement, on one-hour, 90-minute, and two-hour parking meters;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) a requirement for city parking lots and ramps to provide a 50 percent discount on monthly fees for contracted parkers with disabilities or a 50 percent reduction in the hourly rate for parkers with disabilities, with appropriate vehicle identification, who park in designated disability parking spaces; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) issuance of a special needs permit to an employed person with severe disability for an all-day, on-street parking permit that will accommodate the person's access needs.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.346.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/205/#laws.0.1.0">1977 c 205 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/31/#laws.0.3.0">1979 c 31 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/277/#laws.0.5.0">1979 c 277 s 5</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/24/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 24 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/355/#laws.0.8.0">1987 c 355 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/482/#laws.0.2.0">1990 c 482 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/497/#laws.0.12.0">1990 c 497 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/301/#laws.0.5.0">1991 c 301 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/424/#laws.0.1.0">1992 c 424 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/83/#laws.0.3.0">1993 c 83 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/98/#laws.0.6.0">1993 c 98 s 6</a>-8; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/130/#laws.0.1.0">1993 c 130 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/495/#laws.0.1.0">1994 c 495 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/238/#laws.2.19.0">1999 c 238 art 2 s 19</a>,20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/64/#laws.0.8.0">2005 c 64 s 8</a>-11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/272/#laws.0.1.0">2008 c 272 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/30/#laws.0.2.0">2011 c 30 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/127/#laws.0.36.0">2013 c 127 s 36</a>,37; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.5.26.0">2023 c 68 art 5 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.3.59.0">2024 c 127 art 3 s 59</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.35">
        <h1 class="shn">169.35 PARKING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.35.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Parallel to curb.</span></h2>
          <p>Except where angle parking is permitted by local ordinance, each vehicle stopped or parked upon a two-way roadway where there is an adjacent curb shall be so stopped or parked with the right-hand wheels of the vehicle parallel with and within 12 inches of the right-hand curb, provided, that such exception shall only apply to a state trunk highway after approval by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.35.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Where no curb.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon streets and highways not having a curb each vehicle stopped or parked shall be stopped or parked parallel with and to the right of the paved or improved or main-traveled part of the street or highway.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.35.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">One-way roadway.</span></h2>
          <p>Local authorities with respect to streets and highways under their jurisdiction and with the consent of the commissioner with respect to state trunk highways may by ordinance permit parking of vehicles with the left hand wheels adjacent to and within 12 inches of the left hand curb of a one-way roadway.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.35.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-220</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.70.0">1937 c 464 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/1/38/#laws.0.1.0">Ex1937 c 38 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.14.0">1939 c 430 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.21.0">1947 c 428 s 21</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.36"><b>169.36</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/255/#laws.0.21.0">2014 c 255 s 21</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">OTHER TRAFFIC RULES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.37">
        <h1 class="shn">169.37 OBSTRUCTING VIEW OF DRIVER.</h1>
        <p>No person shall drive a vehicle when it is so loaded, or when there are in the front seat such number of persons, exceeding three, as to obstruct the view of the driver to the front or sides of the vehicle or as to interfere with the driver's control over the driving mechanism of the vehicle.</p>
        <p>No passenger in a vehicle or streetcar shall ride in such position as to interfere with the driver's view ahead or to the sides, or to interfere with the driver's control over the driving mechanism of the vehicle or streetcar.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.37.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-222</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.72.0">1937 c 464 s 72</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.38"><b>169.38</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/24/#laws.0.5.0">2001 c 24 s 5</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.39"><b>169.39</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/255/#laws.0.21.0">2014 c 255 s 21</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.40">
        <h1 class="shn">169.40 FIRE TRUCK; FIRE STATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.40.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Following fire truck; parking at fire scene.</span></h2>
          <p>The driver of any vehicle other than one on official business shall not follow any fire apparatus traveling in response to a fire alarm closer than 500 feet, or drive into or park such vehicle within the block where a fire apparatus has stopped in answer to a fire alarm.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.40.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Fire station entrance.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall drive a vehicle within 50 feet of the driveway entrance to any fire station while a fire apparatus is being driven into the fire station unless on official business.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.40.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-225</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.75.0">1937 c 464 s 75</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/281/#laws.0.1.0">1967 c 281 s 1</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.41">
        <h1 class="shn">169.41 CROSSING FIRE HOSE.</h1>
        <p>No streetcar or vehicle shall be driven over any unprotected hose of a fire department when laid down on any street, private driveway, or streetcar track, to be used at any fire or alarm of fire, without the consent of the fire department official in command.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.41.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-226</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.76.0">1937 c 464 s 76</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.42">
        <h1 class="shn">169.42 LITTERING; DROPPING OBJECT ON VEHICLE; MISDEMEANOR.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.42.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Objects on highway.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall throw, deposit, place, or dump, or cause to be thrown, deposited, placed, or dumped upon any street or highway or upon any public or privately owned land adjacent thereto without the owner's consent any snow, ice, glass bottle, glass, nails, tacks, wire, cans, garbage, swill, papers, ashes, cigarette filters, debris from fireworks, refuse, carcass of any dead animal, offal, trash or rubbish or any other form of offensive matter, or any other substance likely to injure any person, animal, or vehicle upon any such street or highway.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.42.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>MS 1969 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.49.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 49</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.42.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Dropping dangerous object on highway.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who drops, or permits to be dropped or thrown, upon any highway any of the material specified in subdivision 1, shall immediately remove the same or cause it to be removed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.42.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Removing object; responsibility.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person removing a wrecked or damaged vehicle from a highway shall remove any glass or other injurious substance dropped upon the highway from such vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.42.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Dropping object on vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall drop or hurl any destructive or injurious material or object at or upon any motor vehicle upon any highway or the occupants thereof.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.42.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who violates the provisions of this section is guilty of a misdemeanor. The record of any conviction of or plea of guilty under this section of a person operating a motor vehicle shall be immediately forwarded to the Department of Public Safety for inclusion upon that offender's driving record. Any second or subsequent offense under this section shall require a minimum fine in the amount of $400. Any judge may, for any violation of this section, order the offender to pick up litter along any public highway or road for four to eight hours under the direction of the Department of Transportation, with the option of a jail sentence being imposed.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.42.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-227</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.77.0">1937 c 464 s 77</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/663/#laws.0.1.0">1951 c 663 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/104/#laws.0.1.0">1967 c 104 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/299/#laws.0.1.0">1973 c 299 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/166/#laws.0.7.0">1976 c 166 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/533/#laws.0.13.0">1980 c 533 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/359/#laws.0.11.0">1983 c 359 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/138/#laws.0.1.0">1991 c 138 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/28/#laws.1.17.0">2003 c 28 art 1 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.65.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 65</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.421">
        <h1 class="shn">169.421 CIVIL LIABILITY FOR LITTERING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.421.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Finding.</span></h2>
          <p>The legislature finds that the cost of removal and disposal of solid waste, including litter, from vehicles is an onerous burden upon the public, and that the criminal law is not always adequate in dealing with the problem. This requires the imposition of civil liability as provided in this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.421.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "owner" as to a vehicle means the owner of the vehicle, but in the case of a leased vehicle means the lessee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.421.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Civil liability imposed.</span></h2>
          <p>If any solid waste, including litter, glass, nails, tacks, wire, cans, bottles, garbage, papers, refuse, trash, cigarette filters, debris from fireworks, or any form of offensive matter is thrown, deposited, placed, or dumped from a vehicle upon any street or highway, public land, or upon private land without the consent of the owner of the land, a violation of this subdivision occurs and civil liability is imposed upon the owner of the vehicle. The driver and passengers riding in a vehicle are constituted as the agents of the owner of the vehicle for purposes of this subdivision. It is a defense to any action brought pursuant to this section that the vehicle was stolen. This section is not applicable to the owner of a vehicle transporting persons for hire or transporting school children.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.421.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Civil penalty; damages.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates this section is subject to the civil penalties for littering and an action for damages as specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115A.99">115A.99</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.421.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Procedures.</span></h2>
          <p>A civil action may be commenced as is any civil action or by the issuance of a citation to the owner of the vehicle by any law enforcement officer who has reason to believe that a violation has occurred. Actions commenced by the issuance of a citation by a law enforcement officer shall be tried by the prosecuting authority responsible for misdemeanor prosecutions in the jurisdiction where a violation occurs. Any damages recovered in an action brought by a public agency shall be deposited in the treasury of the jurisdiction trying the action and distributed as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/484.90">484.90</a>. Any district court may establish a separate civil calendar for cases brought under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.421.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Relationship to criminal law; election of remedy.</span></h2>
          <p>If an act is a violation of this section and of a statute or ordinance providing a criminal penalty, a public agency elects its remedy by commencing either an action under this section or a criminal prosecution, and the commencement of one type of action by a public agency is a bar to its bringing of the other.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.421.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Payment.</span></h2>
          <p>Any district court may establish a schedule of costs and civil damages, and procedures for payment, in cases brought by a public agency under which the defendant may consent to default judgment and make payment according to the schedule without making a personal appearance in court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.421.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Citation.</span></h2>
          <p>This section may be cited as the "Civil Litter Act."</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.421.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/235/#laws.0.1.0">1979 c 235 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/138/#laws.0.2.0">1991 c 138 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/412/#laws.0.3.0">1994 c 412 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/254/#laws.2.14.0">1998 c 254 art 2 s 14</a>,15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/28/#laws.1.18.0">2003 c 28 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/277/#laws.1.22.0">2008 c 277 art 1 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.43">
        <h1 class="shn">169.43 SWINGING GATE ON TRUCK.</h1>
        <p>(a) No truck shall be operated on any highway with gate, loading rack, or partition carried in any manner on any part of the exterior of the truck, unless the top and bottom of such gate, loading rack or partition is securely attached to the truck, so as to prevent swinging or becoming loose.</p>
        <p>(b) No truck shall be driven or parked on any highway with tailgate or tailboard hanging down or projecting from the vehicle except while such vehicle is being loaded or unloaded, and except when a load on the tailboard renders impossible the closing of the tailboard.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.43.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-228</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-229</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.78.0">1937 c 464 s 78</a>,79; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.22.0">1947 c 428 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/263/#laws.0.0.0">1949 c 263</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/320/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 320 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">SCHOOL BUS SAFETY</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.435">
        <h1 class="shn">169.435 OFFICE OF PUPIL TRANSPORTATION SAFETY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.435.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Responsibility; Department of Public Safety.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The Department of Public Safety has the primary responsibility for school transportation safety. The Office of Pupil Transportation Safety is created as a section under the Division of State Patrol. The commissioner shall designate a director of pupil transportation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.435.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Expired]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.435.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Pupil transportation safety director.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> The duties of the pupil transportation safety director include:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) overseeing all department activities related to school bus safety;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) assisting in the development, interpretation, and implementation of laws and policies relating to school bus safety, in consultation with a stakeholder group consisting of, but not limited to, representatives of the school board association, school superintendents, private bus contractors, directors of transportation, school bus employees or their exclusive bargaining representatives, and parent organizations;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) supervising preparation of the School Bus Inspection Manual;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) in conjunction with the Department of Education and the stakeholder group described in clause (2), assisting school districts in developing and implementing comprehensive transportation policies and establishing best practices for private contracts;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) developing and maintaining a consistent record-keeping system to document school bus inspections, out-of-service school transportation vehicles, driver turnover rate, and driver files; and</p>
          <p class="in">(6) conducting periodic audits of selected school districts to determine compliance with federal law and state statute concerning (i) school bus driver requirements and driver employee background and license checks, including controlled substance and alcohol testing requirements; and (ii) duty to report violations to the commissioner of public safety. Audit results must be documented and retained by the Office of Pupil Transportation Safety, and any statutory violations documented in the audit must be reported to the commissioners of public safety and education.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.435.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Staff.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">In addition to the pupil transportation safety director, who must be a state trooper, the Office of Pupil Transportation Safety must be staffed by a minimum of:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) three state troopers, each of whom must be assigned to the metropolitan area, northern Minnesota, or southern Minnesota; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) 15 school bus vehicle inspectors, one of whom must be designated chief inspector. The school bus vehicle inspectors shall perform annual and spot inspections of school buses and Head Start buses as required by law.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.435.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.13.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.16.13.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 16 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.6.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.12.17.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 12 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.36.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 36</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.44"><b>169.44</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.18.0">1991 c 277 s 18</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.441">
        <h1 class="shn">169.441 SCHOOL BUS IDENTIFICATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.441.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Identification and signal requirements, generally.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.441">169.441</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.448">169.448</a>, school bus means a motor vehicle that is outwardly equipped and identified as a school bus. A motor vehicle that satisfies the identification requirements of this section and the signal equipment requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.442">169.442</a> is considered outwardly equipped and identified as a school bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.441.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.43.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 43</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.441.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Head Start bus; color; identification.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A Head Start bus is exempt from the color requirements of this chapter.</p>
          <p>(b) A type A, B, C, or D Head Start bus must bear on its front and rear a plainly visible sign containing the words "Head Start bus" in letters at least eight inches in height.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.441.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sign on bus; application of other law.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.443#stat.169.443.2">169.443, subdivision 2</a>; and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.444">169.444, subdivisions 1, 4, and 5</a>, apply only if the school bus bears on its front and rear a plainly visible sign containing the words "school bus" in letters at least eight inches in height.</p>
          <p>(b) Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.443#stat.169.443.8">169.443, subdivision 8</a>, a school bus sign must be removed or covered when the vehicle is being used as other than a school bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.441.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.10.14.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 10 s 14</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.441.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/137/#laws.0.9.0">2012 c 137 s 9</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.441.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.3.0">1991 c 277 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/516/#laws.0.1.0">1992 c 516 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/603/#laws.0.4.0">1994 c 603 s 4</a>,5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.15.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.16.13.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 16 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/398/#laws.0.55.0">1996 c 398 s 55</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.10.13.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 10 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/102/#laws.0.3.0">2013 c 102 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.442">
        <h1 class="shn">169.442 SCHOOL BUS SIGNALS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.442.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Signals required.</span></h2>
          <p>A type A, B, C, or D school bus must be equipped with at least one stop-signal arm, prewarning flashing amber signals, and flashing red signals.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.442.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.43.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 43</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.442.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.43.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 43</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.442.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Optional warning system.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to equipment required under subdivision 1, and notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.64">169.64</a>, a school bus may be equipped with a driver-activated, exterior student-control, warning system. The driver shall activate this system when the use of the stop-signal arm and flashing red signals is required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.443#stat.169.443.1">169.443, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.442.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">White strobe lamps on certain buses transporting children.</span></h2>
          <p> A school bus or a Head Start bus may be equipped with a flashing strobe lamp under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.64#stat.169.64.8">169.64, subdivision 8</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.442.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Supplemental warning system.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to the signals required under subdivision 1, a type A, B, C, or D school bus may be equipped with a supplemental warning system under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4503#stat.169.4503.31">169.4503, subdivision 31</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.442.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.4.0">1991 c 277 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/603/#laws.0.6.0">1994 c 603 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.16.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.19.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 19</a>,20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.96.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 96</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/3/#laws.3.54.0">1Sp2017 c 3 art 3 s 54</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.46.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 46</a>,47</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.443">
        <h1 class="shn">169.443 SAFETY OF SCHOOL CHILDREN; BUS DRIVER'S DUTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.443.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Using bus signals.</span></h2>
          <p>A driver of a school bus shall activate the prewarning flashing amber signals of the bus before stopping to load or unload school children. The driver shall activate and continuously operate the amber signals for a distance of at least 100 feet before stopping in a speed zone of 35 miles per hour or less and at least 300 feet before stopping in a speed zone of more than 35 miles per hour. On stopping for this purpose, the driver shall extend the stop-signal arm system and activate the flashing red signals. The driver shall not retract the stop-signal arm system nor extinguish the flashing red signals until loading or unloading is completed, students are seated, and children who must cross the roadway are safely across.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.443.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Use of stop-signal arm.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The stop-signal arm system of a school bus must be used in conjunction with the flashing red signals only when the school bus is stopped on a street or highway to load or unload school children.</p>
          <p>(b) A local authority, including the governing body of an Indian tribe, may by ordinance require that a school bus activate the stop-signal arm system and flashing red signals while stopped to unload school children at a location other than a location on a street or highway. The ordinance must designate each location where the requirement is imposed. The requirement is effective only if the local authority has erected signs at or near the location to provide adequate notice that other vehicles are required to obey section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.444#stat.169.444.1">169.444, subdivision 1</a>, when those signals are activated.</p>
          <p>(c) A school bus driver is prohibited from loading or unloading passengers in a designated right-turn lane or in a lane immediately adjacent to a designated right-turn lane unless:</p>
          <p>(1) a school bus stop designated by the district transportation safety director is located in the right-turn lane;</p>
          <p>(2) the driver stops the bus at the extreme right side of the right-turn lane; and</p>
          <p>(3) the driver activates the prewarning flashing amber signals, flashing red signals, and stop-signal arm, unless the school board or its designee, based on safety considerations, provides written direction to the driver not to do so.</p>
          <p class="bl">After loading or unloading passengers, the school bus driver may re-enter the right-hand lane of traffic without turning right. The school bus must indicate the intent to enter the right-hand lane of traffic by activating a flashing left turn signal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.443.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">When signals not used.</span></h2>
          <p>School bus drivers shall not activate the prewarning flashing amber signals or flashing red signals and shall not use the stop arm signal:</p>
          <p>(1) in special school bus loading areas where the bus is entirely off the traveled portion of the roadway and where no other motor vehicle traffic is moving or is likely to be moving within 20 feet of the bus;</p>
          <p>(2) when directed not to do so, in writing, by the local school board;</p>
          <p>(3) when a school bus is being used on a street or highway for purposes other than the actual transportation of school children to or from school or a school-approved activity, except as provided in subdivision 8;</p>
          <p>(4) at railroad grade crossings;</p>
          <p>(5) when operating the bus under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4475">169.4475</a>; and</p>
          <p>(6) when loading and unloading people at designated school bus stops where people are not required to cross the street or highway, while the bus is completely off the traveled portion of a roadway that has adequate shoulders. The driver shall drive the bus completely off the traveled portion of this roadway before loading or unloading people. A school bus stop is designated under this clause if the transportation director of the school district in which the bus stop is located, in consultation with the road authority, certifies the integrity of the shoulder and the safety of the location for loading and unloading people. Each designated school bus stop must be documented and approved by the school board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.443.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Street crossings.</span></h2>
          <p>Where school children must cross a roadway before getting on or after getting off the school bus, the driver of the school bus or a school bus patrol may supervise the crossing, using the standard school patrol flag or signal as approved and prescribed by the commissioner of public safety. Before moving the school bus, the driver of the bus shall visually determine that all children have crossed the roadway and that those who are to do so have boarded the school bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.443.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Moving bus after children unloaded.</span></h2>
          <p>When children are getting off a school bus or Head Start bus, the driver shall visually determine that they are a safe distance from the bus before moving the bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.443.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Type III vehicles.</span></h2>
          <p>The driver of a type III vehicle shall load or unload school children or Head Start passengers only from the right-hand side of the vehicle, provided that on a one-way street the driver shall load or unload school children or Head Start passengers only from the curb side of the vehicle. When loading or unloading school children or Head Start passengers, the driver shall activate the vehicle's four-way hazard lights described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.59#stat.169.59.4">169.59, subdivision 4</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.443.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates this section is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.443.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Use for recreational or educational activity.</span></h2>
          <p>A school bus that transports over regular routes and on regular schedules persons age 18 or under to and from a regularly scheduled recreational or educational activity must comply with subdivisions 1 and 7. Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.441#stat.169.441.3">169.441, subdivision 3</a>, a school bus may provide such transportation only if (1) the "school bus" sign is plainly visible; (2) the school bus has a valid certificate of inspection under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.451">169.451</a>; (3) the driver of the school bus possesses a driver's license with a valid school bus endorsement under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.10">171.10</a>; and (4) the entity that organizes the recreational or educational activity, or the contractor who provides the school buses to the entity, consults with the superintendent of the school district in which the activity is located or the superintendent's designee on the safety of the regular routes used.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.443.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Personal cellular phone call prohibition.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) As used in this subdivision, "school bus" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.011#stat.169.011.71">169.011, subdivision 71</a>. In addition, the term includes type III vehicles as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.011#stat.169.011.71">169.011, subdivision 71</a>, when driven by employees or agents of school districts.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) A school bus driver may not operate a school bus while communicating over, or otherwise operating, a cellular phone for personal reasons, whether handheld or hands free, when the vehicle is in motion or a part of traffic.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.443.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.5.0">1991 c 277 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/516/#laws.0.2.0">1992 c 516 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/78/#laws.0.1.0">1993 c 78 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/465/#laws.1.25.0">1994 c 465 art 1 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/603/#laws.0.7.0">1994 c 603 s 7</a>,8; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.17.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.7.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/426/#laws.0.25.0">2000 c 426 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.21.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 21</a>,22; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/146/#laws.8.4.0">2007 c 146 art 8 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/271/#laws.0.1.0">2008 c 271 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.96.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 96</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/96/#laws.8.3.0">2009 c 96 art 8 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/102/#laws.0.4.0">2013 c 102 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/127/#laws.0.38.0">2013 c 127 s 38</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/3/#laws.3.55.0">1Sp2017 c 3 art 3 s 55</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.48.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 48</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.444">
        <h1 class="shn">169.444 SAFETY OF SCHOOL CHILDREN; DUTIES OF OTHER DRIVERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.444.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Children getting on or off school bus.</span></h2>
          <p>When a school bus is stopped on a street or highway, or other location where signs have been erected under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.443#stat.169.443.2">169.443, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (b), and is displaying an extended stop-signal arm and flashing red lights, the driver of a vehicle approaching the bus shall stop the vehicle at least 20 feet away from the bus. The vehicle driver shall not allow the vehicle to move until the school bus stop-signal arm is retracted and the red lights are no longer flashing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.444.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Passing on right.</span></h2>
          <p>No person may pass or attempt to pass a school bus in a motor vehicle on the right-hand, passenger-door side of the bus when the school bus is displaying the prewarning flashing amber signals as required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.443#stat.169.443.1">169.443, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.444.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Violations by drivers; penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who fails to stop a vehicle or to keep it stopped, as required in subdivision 1, or who violates subdivision 1a, is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than $500.</p>
          <p>(b) A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if the person fails to stop a motor vehicle or to keep it stopped, as required in subdivision 1, or who violates subdivision 1a, and commits either or both of the following acts:</p>
          <p>(1) passes or attempts to pass the school bus in a motor vehicle on the right-hand, passenger-door side of the bus; or</p>
          <p>(2) passes or attempts to pass the school bus in a motor vehicle when a school child is outside of and on the street or highway used by the school bus or on the adjacent sidewalk.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.444.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Prosecutor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The attorney in the jurisdiction in which the violation occurred who is responsible for prosecution of misdemeanor violations of this section shall also be responsible for prosecution of gross misdemeanor violations of this section.</p>
          <p>(b) When an attorney responsible for prosecuting gross misdemeanors under this section requests criminal history information relating to prior convictions under this section from a court, the court must furnish the information without charge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.444.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Exception for separated roadway.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person driving a vehicle on a street or highway with separated roadways is not required to stop the vehicle when approaching or meeting a school bus that is on a different roadway.</p>
          <p>(b) "Separated roadway" means a road that is separated from a parallel road by a physical barrier, raised median, or depressed median.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.444.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Cause for arrest.</span></h2>
          <p>A peace officer may arrest the driver of a motor vehicle if the peace officer has probable cause to believe that the driver has operated the vehicle in violation of subdivision 1 or 1a within the past four hours.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.444.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Violation; penalty for owner or lessee.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If a motor vehicle is operated in violation of subdivision 1 or 1a, the owner of the vehicle, or for a leased motor vehicle the lessee of the vehicle, is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) The owner or lessee may not be fined under paragraph (a) if (1) another person is convicted for that violation, or (2) the motor vehicle was stolen at the time of the violation.</p>
          <p>(c) Paragraph (a) does not apply to a lessor of a motor vehicle if the lessor keeps a record of the name and address of the lessee.</p>
          <p>(d) Paragraph (a) does not prohibit or limit the prosecution of a motor vehicle operator for violating subdivision 1 or 1a.</p>
          <p>(e) A violation under paragraph (a) does not constitute grounds for revocation or suspension of the owner's or lessee's driver's license.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.444.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Evidentiary presumption.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) There is a rebuttable presumption that signals described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.442">169.442</a> were in working order and operable when a violation of subdivision 1, 1a, 2, or 5 was allegedly committed, if the signals of the applicable school bus were inspected and visually found to be in working order and operable within 12 hours preceding the incident giving rise to the violation.</p>
          <p>(b) There is a rebuttable presumption that a motor vehicle outwardly equipped and identified as a school bus satisfies all of the identification and equipment requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.441">169.441</a> when a violation of subdivision 1, 1a, 2, or 5 was allegedly committed, if the applicable school bus bears a current inspection certificate issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.451">169.451</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.444.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Scheduling cases.</span></h2>
          <p>When necessary or desirable to ensure that a school bus driver who witnessed or otherwise can provide relevant information concerning a violation of this section is available to be present at a court proceeding held to determine an alleged violation of this section, the court administrator shall schedule the proceeding to be held between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.444.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.6.0">1991 c 277 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/78/#laws.0.2.0">1993 c 78 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.2.32.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 2 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/159/#laws.2.24.0">1997 c 159 art 2 s 24</a>-28; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/3/#laws.3.56.0">1Sp2017 c 3 art 3 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/104/#laws.1.37.0">2024 c 104 art 1 s 37</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.445">
        <h1 class="shn">169.445 COOPERATION WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.445.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Cooperation of school authorities.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of public safety shall ensure that local authorities having jurisdiction over school buses shall cooperate with law enforcement and judicial authorities in reporting and prosecuting violators of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.443">169.443</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.444">169.444</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.445.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/137/#laws.0.9.0">2012 c 137 s 9</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.445.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.43.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 43</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.445.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.7.0">1991 c 277 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.18.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 18</a>,19</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.446">
        <h1 class="shn">169.446 SAFETY OF SCHOOL CHILDREN; TRAINING AND EDUCATION RULES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.446.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Peace officer training.</span></h2>
          <p>The Board of Peace Officer Standards and Training shall include sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.441">169.441</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.448">169.448</a> and the enforcement of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.443">169.443</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.444">169.444</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.447">169.447</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.448">169.448</a> in the instruction for the professional peace officer education program. The board shall notify the chief law enforcement officer of each law enforcement agency in the state of these sections.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.446.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Driver training programs.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner of public safety shall adopt rules requiring a minimum of 30 minutes of thorough instruction concerning section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.444">169.444</a> for persons enrolled in driver training programs offered at public, private and parochial schools, and commercial driver training schools. The instruction must encompass at least the responsibilities of drivers, the content and requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.444">169.444</a>, and the penalties for violating that section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.446.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.97.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 97</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.446.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.8.0">1991 c 277 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.20.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.37.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 37</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.447">
        <h1 class="shn">169.447 SCHOOL BUS AND HEAD START BUS SAFETY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.447.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Passenger seating.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The number of pupils or other authorized passengers transported in a school bus or Head Start bus must not be more than the number of pupils or passengers that can be fully seated. Seating capacity must be adjusted according to each passenger's individual physical size, but not more than the manufacturers' rated seating capacity.</p>
          <p>(b) No person shall stand in the school bus or Head Start bus when the bus is in motion.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.447.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Driver seat belt.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> School buses and Head Start buses must be equipped with driver seat belts and seat belt assemblies of the type described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.685#stat.169.685.3">169.685, subdivision 3</a>. A properly adjusted and fastened seat belt, including both the shoulder and lap belt when the vehicle is so equipped, shall be worn by the driver.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.447.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Passenger lap and shoulder belts.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) In addition to the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4501#stat.169.4501.1">169.4501, subdivision 1</a>, a school bus may be equipped with an approved lap belt or an approved lap and shoulder belt installed for each passenger seating position on the bus. The design and installation of lap belts and lap and shoulder belts required under this paragraph must meet the standards of the commissioner established under paragraph (b).</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner shall consider all concerns necessary to properly integrate lap belts or lap and shoulder belts into the current compartmentalization safety system and prescribe standards for the design and installation of lap and shoulder belts required under paragraph (a). The standards are not subject to chapter 14 and are specifically not subject to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.386">14.386</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) This subdivision does not apply to specially equipped school buses under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4504">169.4504</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) A passenger on a school bus equipped with lap belts or lap and shoulder belts must use these lap belts or lap and shoulder belts unless the passenger, or if the passenger is a minor, the passenger's parent or guardian, has notified the school district in writing that the passenger does not intend to wear the lap belt or lap and shoulder belt.</p>
          <p>(e) In an action for personal injury or wrongful death against a school district, a school bus operator under contract with a school district, or any agent or employee of a school district or operator, or against a volunteer, no such person or entity shall be held liable solely because the injured party was not wearing a safety belt; provided, however, that nothing contained herein shall be construed to grant immunity from liability for failure to:</p>
          <p>(1) maintain in operating order any equipment required by statute, rule, or school district policy; or</p>
          <p>(2) comply with an applicable statute, rule, or school district policy.</p>
          <p>(f) In an action for personal injury or wrongful death, a school district, a school bus contract operator, any agent or employee of a school district or operator, or a volunteer is not liable for failing to assist any child with the adjustment, fastening, unfastening, or other use of the lap belt or lap and shoulder belt.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.447.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.43.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 43</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.447.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Aisle and exit.</span></h2>
          <p>The driver of a school bus or Head Start bus shall keep the aisle and emergency exit of a school bus or Head Start bus unobstructed at all times when children are being transported.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.447.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Trailer behind school bus.</span></h2>
          <p>A school bus may pull a trailer, as defined by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.011#stat.169.011.86">169.011, subdivision 86</a>, only when traveling to or from cocurricular or extracurricular activities, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/123B.49">123B.49</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.447.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.34.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.447.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.9.0">1991 c 277 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/603/#laws.0.9.0">1994 c 603 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.21.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.8.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/397/#laws.11.3.0">1998 c 397 art 11 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/489/#laws.6.28.0">2000 c 489 art 6 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/146/#laws.8.5.0">2007 c 146 art 8 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/127/#laws.0.39.0">2013 c 127 s 39</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.4475">
        <h1 class="shn">169.4475 SPECIAL EVENT SCHOOL BUS USE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4475.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Temporary use authority.</span></h2>
