          <p>A pupil transport entity that meets the requirements of this section may operate a school bus for which the entity has paid registration tax under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.18">168.013, subdivision 18</a>, to provide transportation that is not pupil transportation without reregistration of the bus, issuance of new plates, or payment of additional taxes and fees under chapter 168.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4475.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>A pupil transport entity may operate a school bus under this section if:</p>
          <p>(1) the transportation is performed under an agreement with a tax exempt entity under section 501(c) of the Internal Revenue Code, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/289A.02">289A.02</a>, subdivision 7, solely to transport participants in conjunction with a special event of up to two days organized or substantially sponsored by the tax exempt entity; and</p>
          <p>(2) the pupil transportation entity meets the requirements of a motor carrier of passengers under chapter 221, including but not limited to use of a temporary vehicle identification card under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/221.132">221.132</a> for the school bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4475.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">School bus equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.448#stat.169.448.1">169.448, subdivision 1</a>, a school bus operated under this section may:</p>
          <p>(1) be painted national school bus glossy yellow; and</p>
          <p>(2) be equipped with a stop-signal arm, prewarning flashing amber signals, and flashing red signals.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.4475.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/102/#laws.0.5.0">2013 c 102 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.448">
        <h1 class="shn">169.448 OTHER BUSES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.448.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Restrictions on appearance; misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A bus that is not used as a school bus must not be operated on a street or highway unless it is painted a color significantly different than national school bus glossy yellow.</p>
          <p>(b) A bus that is not used as a school bus or Head Start bus may not be operated if it is equipped with school bus or Head Start bus-related equipment and printing.</p>
          <p>(c) A violation of this subdivision is a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(d) This subdivision does not apply to a school bus owned by or under contract to a school district operated as a charter or leased bus.</p>
          <p>(e) This subdivision does not apply to a school bus operated by a licensed child care provider if:</p>
          <p>(1) the stop-signal arm is removed;</p>
          <p>(2) the lighting systems for prewarning flashing amber signals, flashing red signals, and supplemental warnings under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4503#stat.169.4503.31">169.4503, subdivision 31</a>, are deactivated;</p>
          <p>(3) the school bus is identified as a "child care bus" in letters at least eight inches high on the front and rear top of the bus;</p>
          <p>(4) the name, address, and telephone number of the owner or operator of the bus is identified on each front door of the bus in letters not less than three inches high; and</p>
          <p>(5) the conditions under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.02#stat.171.02.2a">171.02, subdivision 2a</a>, paragraphs (a) to (j) and (l), have been met.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.448.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">School motor coach.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A school district may not acquire a motor coach for transportation purposes.</p>
          <p>(b) A motor coach acquired by a school district before March 26, 1986, may be used by it only to transport students participating in school activities, their instructors, and supporting personnel to and from school activities. A motor coach may not be outwardly equipped and identified as a school bus. A motor coach operated under this subdivision is not a school bus for purposes of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/123B.92">123B.92</a>. The commissioner of education shall implement rules governing the equipment, identification, operation, inspection, and certification of motor coaches operated under this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(c) After January 1, 1998, a school district may not own or operate a motor coach for any purpose.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.448.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Head Start vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding subdivision 1, a vehicle used to transport students under Public Law 99-425, the Head Start Act, may be equipped as a school bus or Head Start bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.448.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Day activity center buses.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding subdivision 1, a vehicle used to transport adults to and from a day activity center may be equipped with prewarning flashing amber signals and a stop-signal arm, and the operator of the vehicle may activate this equipment, under the following circumstances:</p>
          <p>(1) the operator possesses a commercial driver's license with a school bus endorsement;</p>
          <p>(2) the vehicle is engaged in picking up or dropping off adults at locations predesignated by the day activity center that owns or leases the bus;</p>
          <p>(3) the vehicle is identified as a "day activity center bus" in letters at least eight inches high on the front and rear top of the bus; and</p>
          <p>(4) the name, address, and telephone number of the owner and operator of the bus is identified on each front door of the bus in letters not less than three inches high.</p>
          <p>The provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.444">169.444</a> relating to duties of care of a motorist to a school bus, and violations thereof, apply to a vehicle described in this section when the vehicle is operated in conformity with this subdivision. The provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.443">169.443</a> relating to bus driver's duties apply to a vehicle described in this section except those that by their nature have no application.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.448.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.10.0">1991 c 277 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/603/#laws.0.10.0">1994 c 603 s 10</a>,11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/398/#laws.0.56.0">1996 c 398 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/397/#laws.11.3.0">1998 c 397 art 11 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/398/#laws.5.55.0">1998 c 398 art 5 s 55</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/489/#laws.6.29.0">2000 c 489 art 6 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/97/#laws.0.2.0">2001 c 97 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/130/#laws.0.12.0">2003 c 130 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/19/#laws.2.28.0">1Sp2003 c 19 art 2 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/6/#laws.3.47.0">1Sp2005 c 6 art 3 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/277/#laws.1.23.0">2008 c 277 art 1 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.49.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 49</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.449">
        <h1 class="shn">169.449 SCHOOL BUS OPERATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.449.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Rules.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of public safety shall adopt rules governing the operation of school buses used for transportation of school children, when owned or operated by a school or privately owned and operated under a contract with a school. Each school, its officers and employees, and each person employed under the contract is subject to these rules.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.449.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Enforcement.</span></h2>
          <p>The operation of a school bus on the public streets or highways in violation of rules concerning the operation of school buses adopted by the commissioner under subdivision 1 is a misdemeanor. The State Patrol shall enforce rules adopted under subdivision 1 when a school bus is operated on a public street or highway.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.449.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.22.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.12.18.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 12 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/3/#laws.3.57.0">1Sp2017 c 3 art 3 s 57</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.45"><b>169.45</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.43.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 43</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.4501">
        <h1 class="shn">169.4501 SCHOOL BUS EQUIPMENT STANDARDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4501.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">National standards adopted.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Except as provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4502">169.4502 </a>and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4503">169.4503</a>, the construction, design, equipment, and color of types A, B, C, D school buses and multifunction school activity buses used for the transportation of school children shall meet the requirements of the "bus body and chassis specifications" in the most recent edition of the "National School Transportation Specifications and Procedures" adopted by the National Congress on School Transportation. Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4504">169.4504</a>, the construction, design, and equipment of types A, B, C, D school buses and multifunction school activity buses used for the transportation of students with disabilities also shall meet the requirements of the "specially equipped school bus specifications" in the National School Transportation Specifications and Procedures. The "bus body and chassis specifications" and "specially equipped school bus specifications" sections of the most recent edition of the "National School Transportation Specifications and Procedures," adopted by the National Congress on School Transportation, are incorporated by reference in this chapter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4501.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The standards adopted in this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4502">169.4502 </a>and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4503">169.4503</a>, govern the construction, design, equipment, and color of school buses used for the transportation of school children, when owned or leased and operated by a school or privately owned or leased and operated under a contract with a school. Each school, its officers and employees, and each person employed under the contract is subject to these standards.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) The standards apply to school buses manufactured after August 1 of the year following a year in which a revised edition of the National School Transportation Specifications and Procedures is adopted. Buses complying with the standards when manufactured need not comply with standards established later except as specifically provided for by law.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) A school bus manufactured on or before the date provided by paragraph (b) must conform to the Minnesota standards in effect on the date the vehicle was manufactured except as specifically provided for in law.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) A new bus body may be remounted on a used chassis provided that the remounted vehicle meets state and federal standards for new buses which are current at the time of the remounting. Permission must be obtained from the commissioner of public safety before the remounting is done. A used bus body may not be remounted on a new or used chassis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4501.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Inspection manual.</span></h2>
          <p>The Department of Public Safety shall develop a School Bus Inspection Manual based on the national standards adopted in subdivision 1 and Minnesota standards adopted in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4502">169.4502</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4504">169.4504</a>. The Minnesota State Patrol shall use the manual as the basis for inspecting buses as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.451">169.451</a>. The Department of Public Safety has no rulemaking authority to alter the standards upon which school buses are inspected.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4501.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Variance.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of public safety may grant a variance to any of the school bus standards to accommodate testing of new equipment related to school buses. A variance from the standards must be for the sole purpose of testing and evaluating new equipment for increased safety, efficiency, and economy of pupil transportation. The variance expires 18 months from the date on which it is granted unless the commissioner specifies an earlier expiration date.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.4501.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.23.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.9.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 9</a>,10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.12.19.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 12 s 19</a>,20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.23.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 23</a>,24; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/146/#laws.8.6.0">2007 c 146 art 8 s 6</a>,7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/96/#laws.8.4.0">2009 c 96 art 8 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/137/#laws.0.1.0">2012 c 137 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/3/#laws.3.58.0">1Sp2017 c 3 art 3 s 58</a>,59</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.4502">
        <h1 class="shn">169.4502 ADDITIONAL MINNESOTA SCHOOL BUS CHASSIS STANDARDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Relation to national standards.</span></h2>
          <p>The bus chassis standards contained in this section are required in addition to those required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4501">169.4501</a>. When a Minnesota standard contained in this section conflicts with a national standard adopted in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4501">169.4501</a>, the Minnesota standard contained in this section is controlling.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Brakes.</span></h2>
          <p>The braking system must meet federal motor vehicle safety standards in effect at the time of manufacture.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Certification.</span></h2>
          <p>A chassis manufacturer shall certify that the product meets Minnesota standards. All buses with a certified manufacturing date prior to April 1, 1977, shall not be recertified as a school bus after January 1, 1996.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Color of fenders, hood, and grill.</span></h2>
          <p>Fenders may be painted black. The hood may be painted nonreflective black or nonreflective yellow. The grill may be manufacturer's standard color or chrome.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>MS 2016 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/3/#laws.3.144.0">1Sp2017 c 3 art 3 s 144</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.34.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.34.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Trailer hitch.</span></h2>
          <p>Installation of a trailer hitch is permitted. A hitch shall be flush mounted.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.34.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Horn.</span></h2>
          <p>A bus shall be equipped with a horn in good working order and capable of emitting sound audible under normal conditions from a distance of not less than 200 feet.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Tire and rim.</span></h2>
          <p>The use of multipiece rims or tube-type tires is not permitted on school buses manufactured after October 31, 2004. Radial and bias-ply tires shall not be used on the same axle. Front tire tread depth shall not be less than 4/32 inch in any major tire tread groove. Rear tire tread shall not be less than 2/32 inch. Tires must be measured in three locations around the tire, in two adjoining grooves. No recapped tires shall be used on the front wheels. Recapped tires are permitted on the rear wheels.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Transmission gear shift display.</span></h2>
          <p>The transmission shifting pattern must be permanently displayed in the driver's full view.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.34.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.34.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4502.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/146/#laws.8.15.0">2007 c 146 art 8 s 15</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.4502.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.36.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 36</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.2.33.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 2 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.11.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 11</a>-17; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.25.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/146/#laws.8.8.0">2007 c 146 art 8 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.4503">
        <h1 class="shn">169.4503 ADDITIONAL MINNESOTA SCHOOL BUS BODY STANDARDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Relation to national standards.</span></h2>
          <p>The bus body standards contained in this section are required in addition to those required by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4501">169.4501</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4502">169.4502</a>. When a Minnesota standard contained in this section conflicts with a national standard adopted in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4501">169.4501</a>, the Minnesota standard contained in this section is controlling.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Back-up warning alarm.</span></h2>
          <p>An automatic audible back-up alarm may be installed. A spring-loaded button in the driver's compartment that will temporarily disable the back-up alarm is allowed for usage in school bus overnight parking lots and repair facilities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.34.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Certification.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon request, a body manufacturer or school bus dealer must provide preliminary certification to the Department of Public Safety that the product meets Minnesota standards.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Colors.</span></h2>
          <p>Fenderettes may be black. The beltline may be painted yellow over black or black over yellow. The rub rails adjacent to the beltline may be black or yellow. All other rub rails must be black. The area around the lenses of alternately flashing signal lamps extending outward from the edge of the lamp three inches, plus or minus one-quarter inch, to the sides and top and at least one inch to the bottom, must be black. Visors or hoods, black in color, with a minimum of four inches may be provided.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Communications.</span></h2>
          <p>All buses manufactured after January 1, 1995, shall have a two-way voice communications system.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Floor construction.</span></h2>
          <p>The metal floor must be covered with plywood. The plywood must be five-ply nominal five-eighths inches thick, and must equal or exceed properties of exterior-type softwood plywood, grade C-D, as specified in the standard issued by the United States Department of Commerce. All of the plywood's exposed edges must be sealed. Type A-I buses must be equipped with nominal one-half inch thick plywood or an equivalent material that meets the requirements of this subdivision. Equivalent material may be used to replace plywood, provided it has insulation R-value, deterioration, sound abatement, and moisture resistance properties that are equal to or exceed the properties of the plywood it is replacing. The floor must be level from front to back, and side to side, except in wheel housing, toe board, and driver's seat platform areas.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.34.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.34.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.34.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.10a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10a.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.34.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.34.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.34.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Identification.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Each bus must, in the beltline, identify the school district serviced, or company name, or owner of the bus. Numbers necessary for identification must appear on the sides and rear of the bus. Symbols or letters may be used on the outside of the bus near the entrance door for student identification. A manufacturer's nameplate or logo may be placed on the bus.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) All type A, B, C, and D buses sold must display lettering "Unlawful to pass when red lights are flashing" on the rear of the bus. The lettering must be in two-inch black letters on school bus yellow background. This message must be displayed directly below the upper window of the rear door. On rear engine buses, it must be centered at approximately the same location. Only signs and lettering approved or required by state law are permitted to be displayed.</p>
          <p>(c) The requirements of paragraph (b) do not apply to a type A, B, C, or D school bus that is equipped with a changeable electronic message sign on the rear of the bus that:</p>
          <p>(1) displays one or more of the messages: "Caution / stopping," "Unlawful to pass," "Stop / do not pass," or similar messages approved by the commissioner;</p>
          <p>(2) displays messages in conjunction with bus operation and activation of prewarning flashing amber signals, flashing red signals, or stop-signal arm, as appropriate; and</p>
          <p>(3) is a supplemental warning system under subdivision 31.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Insulation.</span></h2>
          <p> Thermal insulation is required. It shall be fire-resistant, UL approved, with minimum R-value of 5.5. Insulation shall be installed so as to prevent sagging.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Interior speakers.</span></h2>
          <p>Interior speakers, except in the driver's compartment, must not protrude more than one-half inch from the mounting surface.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Lamps and signals.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If installed, a white flashing strobe shall be of a double flash type. No roof hatch can be mounted behind the strobe light.</p>
          <p>(b) All lamps on the exterior of the vehicle must conform with and be installed as required by federal motor vehicle safety standard number 108, Code of Federal Regulations, title 49, part 571.</p>
          <p>(c) A type A, B, C, or D school bus manufactured for use in Minnesota after December 31, 1994, may not be equipped with red turn-signal lenses on the rear of the bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/146/#laws.8.15.0">2007 c 146 art 8 s 15</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.18">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/146/#laws.8.15.0">2007 c 146 art 8 s 15</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.19">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.<span class="headnote">Rub rail.</span></h2>
          <p>There shall be one rub rail at the base of the skirt of the bus on all type A, excluding van conversions, B, C, and D buses.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.20">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20.<span class="headnote">Seat and crash barriers.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> All restraining barriers and passenger seats shall be covered with a material that has fire retardant or fire block characteristics.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.21">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 21.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.34.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.22">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 22.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.34.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.23">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 23.<span class="headnote">Windows.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Windshield, entrance, and rear emergency exit doors must be of approved safety glass. Laminated or tempered glass (AS-2 or AS-3) is permitted in all other windows. All glass shall be federally approved and marked as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.74">169.74</a>. The windshield may be of uniform tint throughout or may have a horizontal gradient band starting slightly above the line of vision and gradually decreasing in light transmission to 20 percent or less at the top of the windshield.</p>
          <p>(b) The use of tinted glass, as approved by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.71">169.71</a>, is permitted on side windows and rear windows except for the entrance door and the window to the left of the driver. The window to the left of the driver and the upper service door windows must be thermal glass. Regardless of a bus's date of manufacture, the window immediately behind the entrance door does not need to be made of thermal glass. The window to the left of the driver for type A buses need not be thermal glass.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.24">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 24.<span class="headnote">Wiring.</span></h2>
          <p>If a master cutoff switch is used, it shall not be wired as to kill power to the electric brake system.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.25">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 25.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.34.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.26">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 26.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/146/#laws.8.15.0">2007 c 146 art 8 s 15</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.27">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 27.</h2>
          <p>MS 2012 [Expired, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/96/#laws.8.6.0">2009 c 96 art 8 s 6</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.28">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 28.<span class="headnote">Crossing control arm.</span></h2>
          <p>All buses manufactured for use in Minnesota after January 1, 2013, shall be equipped with a crossing control arm mounted at the right front corner of the front bumper. The crossing control arm shall be automatically activated whenever the bus is stopped with the flashing red signals in use.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.29">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 29.<span class="headnote">Auxiliary fans.</span></h2>
          <p>Additional auxiliary fans are required for school buses manufactured on or after December 31, 2012, and shall meet the following requirements:</p>
          <p>(a) Fans for the left and right sides of the windshield shall be placed in a location where they can be adjusted for maximum effectiveness and where they do not obstruct vision to any mirror. Type A buses may be equipped with one fan.</p>
          <p>(b) Fans shall be a minimum of six inches in diameter.</p>
          <p>(c) Fan blades shall be covered with a protective cage. Each fan shall be controlled by a separate switch.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.30">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 30.<span class="headnote">Video or mobile surveillance systems.</span></h2>
          <p>Camera heads for video or mobile surveillance may be mounted in the driver compartment area, midbus, or on a rear interior bulkhead in the student passenger area. For buses manufactured or retrofitted with a surveillance system after December 31, 2012, cameras mounted midbus must be parallel to a seat back, must not have any sharp edges, must not extend outward more than 3-1/2 inches, and must be located within 24 inches of the top of the side window of the bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4503.31">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 31.<span class="headnote">Supplemental warning system.</span></h2>
          <p> Type A, B, C, or D school buses may be equipped with a supplemental warning system.</p>
          <p>A supplemental warning system must:</p>
          <p>(1) use amber and red signal colors;</p>
          <p>(2) use supplemental amber warning lights activated only in conjunction with activated overhead amber warning lights and supplemental red warning lights activated only in conjunction with activated overhead red flashing lights;</p>
          <p>(3) be wired so the supplemental warning system is automatically activated in conjunction with activation of prewarning flashing amber signals, stop-signal arm, and flashing red signals;</p>
          <p>(4) be programmed to flash at a rate of 60 to 120 flashes per minute by either:</p>
          <p>(i) using a randomized flash pattern; or</p>
          <p>(ii) alternating with the corresponding overhead light; and</p>
          <p>(5) use lights installed in pairs and mounted on the same level and placed as wide as practicable on the body above the bumper level.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.4503.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.37.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.2.34.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 2 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.18.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 18</a>-27; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.1.45.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 1 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/294/#laws.2.26.0">2004 c 294 art 2 s 26</a>-30; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/146/#laws.8.9.0">2007 c 146 art 8 s 9</a>,10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/96/#laws.8.5.0">2009 c 96 art 8 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/137/#laws.0.3.0">2012 c 137 s 3</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/3/#laws.3.60.0">1Sp2017 c 3 art 3 s 60</a>-64; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.50.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 50</a>-52; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/104/#laws.1.38.0">2024 c 104 art 1 s 38</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.4504">
        <h1 class="shn">169.4504 ADDITIONAL STANDARDS FOR SPECIALLY EQUIPPED BUS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4504.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Relation to national standards.</span></h2>
          <p>The specially equipped school bus standards contained in this section are required in addition to those required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4501">169.4501</a>. When a Minnesota standard contained in this section conflicts with a national standard adopted in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4501">169.4501</a>, the Minnesota standard contained in this section is controlling.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4504.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Communications.</span></h2>
          <p>All vehicles used to transport disabled students shall be equipped with a two-way communication system.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4504.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Restraining devices.</span></h2>
          <p>Special restraining devices such as shoulder harnesses, lap belts, and chest restraint systems may be installed to the seats if the devices do not require the alteration in any form of the seat, seat cushion, framework, or related seat components. The restraints must be for the sole purpose of restraining students with disabilities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4504.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Securement system for mobile seating.</span></h2>
          <p>Wheelchair securement devices must comply with all requirements for wheelchair securement systems contained in federal regulation in effect on the later of the date the bus was manufactured or the date that a wheelchair securement system was added to the bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4504.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Aisle width.</span></h2>
          <p>All school buses equipped with a power lift shall provide at least a 12-inch aisle leading from wheelchair position to at least one emergency door and the lift area.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4504.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Securement and restraint system.</span></h2>
          <p>The securement and restraint system must be located and installed so that when an occupied wheelchair or other mobility aid is secured, the installation meets the requirements of the applicable federal motor vehicle safety standard.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.4504.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.38.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 38</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/412/#laws.2.15.0">1996 c 412 art 2 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.28.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 28</a>,29</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.451">
        <h1 class="shn">169.451 INSPECTING SCHOOL AND HEAD START BUSES; RULES; MISDEMEANOR.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.451.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Annual requirement.</span></h2>
          <p>The Minnesota State Patrol shall inspect every school bus and every Head Start bus annually to ascertain whether its construction, design, equipment, and color comply with all provisions of law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.451.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Inspection certificate.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as provided in subdivision 2a, no person shall drive, or no owner shall knowingly permit or cause to be driven, any school bus or Head Start bus unless there is displayed thereon a certificate issued by the commissioner of public safety stating that, in the month specified on the certificate, a member of the Minnesota State Patrol inspected the bus and found that on the date of inspection the bus complied with the applicable provisions of state law relating to construction, design, equipment, and color. The certificate is valid for 12 months after the month specified on the certificate.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.451.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Interim inspection; certificate.</span></h2>
          <p>In lieu of the certificate required in subdivision 2, a new or used school bus being sold by a dealer in this state may display an interim inspection certificate. The school bus dealer completing the preregistration certificate required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.102">168.102</a> may inspect the bus to determine if the bus complies with the applicable provisions of state law relating to construction, design, equipment, and color. If the bus complies with the applicable provisions of state law, the dealer may affix the interim inspection certificate to the school bus, indicating that on the date of the inspection, the bus complied with the applicable provisions of state law relating to construction, design, equipment, and color. The interim certificate must include the date of the inspection and must be valid until the owner's next scheduled annual inspection, but must not be valid for more than 12 months following the month of the initial inspection. The commissioner must provide the prescribed interim inspection certificates at no cost to the dealer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.451.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Inspection criteria.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner of public safety must inspect school buses in accordance with the School Bus Inspection Manual as prescribed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4501#stat.169.4501.3">169.4501, subdivision 3</a>. Upon completion of an inspection, the commissioner must provide a printed or electronic vehicle examination report to the carrier or school district.</p>
          <p>(b) A school bus displaying a defect as defined in the "School Bus Recommended Out-of-Service Criteria" in the most recent edition of the "National School Transportation Specification and Procedures" adopted by the National Congress on School Transportation is deemed unsafe for student transportation. A member of the State Patrol must affix a rejection sticker to the lower left corner of the windshield. A person may remove the rejection sticker only upon authorization from a member of the State Patrol who has determined that all defects have been corrected. Pending reinspection and certification of the vehicle by a member of the State Patrol, a bus bearing a rejection sticker may be used to transport students for up to 30 days provided the defects have been corrected and the vehicle examination report is signed by the owner or a designee certifying that all defects have been corrected. The signed report must be carried in the first aid kit on the bus.</p>
          <p>(c) A school bus that has had an inspection completed in which no out-of-service defects were identified has passed the inspection and a member of the State Patrol must affix an inspection certificate to the lower left corner of the windshield. All defects identified must be repaired within 14 days of the inspection. The person completing the repairs must sign and date the inspection report indicating the repairs were made. The inspection report must be retained at the principal place of business of the carrier or school district for 12 months following the inspection and must be available for review by a representative of the commissioner of public safety.</p>
          <p>(d) A defect discovered during an inspection that was identified by a member of the State Patrol during a previous inspection but has not been corrected results in a failed inspection. A member of the State Patrol must affix a rejection sticker to the lower left corner of the windshield.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.451.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Violations; penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The State Patrol must enforce subdivisions 2 to 3.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who operates a school bus without a valid inspection certificate issued pursuant to subdivision 2 or an interim inspection certificate issued pursuant to subdivision 2a is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(c) A person who operates, or an owner who knowingly permits the operation of, a school bus displaying a rejection sticker issued in accordance with subdivision 3, paragraph (b), and has not fulfilled all the requirements specified in subdivision 3, paragraph (b), is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.451.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Random spot inspection.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to the annual inspection, the Minnesota State Patrol has authority to conduct random, unannounced spot inspections of any school bus or Head Start bus being operated within the state to ascertain whether it is in compliance with provisions of law, including the Minnesota school bus equipment standards in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4501">169.4501</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4504">169.4504</a>, subject to the procedures approved by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.451.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Member of the State Patrol.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, a member of the State Patrol includes an employee of the Department of Public Safety described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299D.06">299D.06</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.451.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/327/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 327 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/80/#laws.0.1.0">1973 c 80 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/332/#laws.0.3.0">1974 c 332 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/37/#laws.0.2.0">1981 c 37 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/357/#laws.0.61.0">1981 c 357 s 61</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/216/#laws.1.28.0">1983 c 216 art 1 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.12.0">1991 c 277 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/603/#laws.0.12.0">1994 c 603 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.2.35.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 2 s 35</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/398/#laws.6.31.0">1998 c 398 art 6 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/100/#laws.0.8.0">2020 c 100 s 8</a>-10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/5/#laws.4.61.0">1Sp2021 c 5 art 4 s 61</a>,62; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.5.27.0">2023 c 68 art 5 s 27</a>-29</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.4511">
        <h1 class="shn">169.4511 SCHOOL BUS ACCIDENT AND SUBSEQUENT OPERATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4511.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Postcrash inspection.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A peace officer responding to an accident involving a school bus or Head Start bus must immediately notify the State Patrol if the accident results in:</p>
          <p>(1) a fatality;</p>
          <p>(2) bodily injury to a person who, as a result of the injury, immediately receives medical treatment away from the scene of the accident; or</p>
          <p>(3) one or more motor vehicles incurring disabling damage as a result of the accident, requiring a motor vehicle to be transported away from the scene by tow truck or other motor vehicle.</p>
          <p>(b) No person shall drive or knowingly permit or cause to be driven, for the purpose of transporting students, any school bus or Head Start bus after such an accident unless:</p>
          <p>(1) the vehicle has been inspected by the Minnesota State Patrol and the State Patrol has determined that the vehicle may safely be operated; or</p>
          <p>(2) a waiver has been granted under subdivision 2.</p>
          <p>(c) A violation of this section is a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4511.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Waiver.</span></h2>
          <p>A state trooper or designee of the Minnesota State Patrol called to the scene of an accident by a responding peace officer under subdivision 1 may waive the inspection requirement of subdivision 1 if the trooper or State Patrol designee determines that a postcrash inspection is not needed or cannot be accomplished without unreasonable delay. The trooper or State Patrol designee granting a waiver must provide to the driver of the school bus for which the waiver is granted a written statement that the inspection has been waived. The written statement must include the incident report number assigned to the accident by the State Patrol.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.4511.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.2.36.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 2 s 36</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/113/#laws.0.1.0">2009 c 113 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.452"><b>169.452</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/398/#laws.6.38.0">1998 c 398 art 6 s 38</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.454">
        <h1 class="shn">169.454 TYPE III VEHICLE STANDARDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Standards.</span></h2>
          <p>This section applies to type III vehicles used for the transportation of school children when owned and operated by a school district or privately owned and operated. All related equipment provided on the vehicle must comply with federal motor vehicle safety standards where applicable. If no federal standard applies, equipment must be manufacture's standard.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Age of vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>Vehicles model year 2007 or older must not be used as type III vehicles to transport school children, except those vehicles that are manufactured to meet the structural requirements of federal motor vehicle safety standard 222, Code of Federal Regulations, title 49, part 571.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Color.</span></h2>
          <p>Vehicles must be painted a color other than national school bus yellow.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Fire extinguisher.</span></h2>
          <p>A minimum of one 10BC rated dry chemical type fire extinguisher is required. The extinguisher must be mounted in a bracket, and must be located in the driver's compartment and be readily accessible to the driver and passengers. A pressure indicator is required and must be easily read without removing the extinguisher from its mounted position.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">First aid kit and body fluids cleanup kit.</span></h2>
          <p>A minimum of a ten-unit first aid kit, and a body fluids cleanup kit is required. They must be contained in removable, moisture- and dust-proof containers mounted in an accessible place within the driver's compartment and must be marked to indicate their identity and location.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Identification.</span></h2>
          <p>The vehicle must not have the words "school bus" in any location on the exterior of the vehicle, or in any interior location visible to a motorist.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Lamps and signals.</span></h2>
          <p>Installation and use of the eight-lamp warning system is prohibited.</p>
          <p>All lamps on the exterior of the vehicle must conform with and be installed as required by federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 108, Code of Federal Regulations, title 49, part 571.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Stop-signal arm.</span></h2>
          <p>Installation and use of a stop-signal arm is prohibited.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Mirrors.</span></h2>
          <p>The interior clear rearview mirror must afford a good view of pupils and roadway to the rear. Two exterior clear rearview mirrors must be provided, one to the left and one to the right of the driver. Each mirror must be firmly supported and adjustable to give the driver clear view past the left rear and the right rear of the bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/137/#laws.0.9.0">2012 c 137 s 9</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.12.34.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 12 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Option.</span></h2>
          <p>Type III vehicles may carry fire extinguisher, first aid kit, and warning triangles in the trunk or trunk area of the vehicle, if a label in the driver and front passenger area clearly indicates the location of these items.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.454.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Exemption.</span></h2>
          <p>When a vehicle otherwise qualifying as a type III vehicle under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.011#stat.169.011.71">169.011, subdivision 71</a>, whether owned and operated by a school district or privately owned and operated, is used to transport school children in a nonscheduled situation, it shall be exempt from the vehicle requirements of this section and the licensing requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.321">171.321</a>, if the vehicle is properly registered and insured and operated by an employee or agent of a school district with a valid driver's license.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.454.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.25.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.2.38.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 2 s 38</a>,39; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.1.46.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 1 s 46</a>,47; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.96.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 96</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/96/#laws.8.7.0">2009 c 96 art 8 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/127/#laws.0.40.0">2013 c 127 s 40</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.5.30.0">2023 c 68 art 5 s 30</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.4581">
        <h1 class="shn">169.4581 CRIMINAL CONDUCT ON SCHOOL BUS.</h1>
        <p> Each local law enforcement agency shall adopt a written policy regarding procedures for responding to criminal incidents on school buses. In adopting a policy, each law enforcement agency shall consult with local school officials, with representatives of private companies that contract with school districts to provide transportation, and with parents of students. The policy must recognize that responding to reports of criminal conduct on school buses is the responsibility of law enforcement officials.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.4581.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.26.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/25/#laws.0.81.0">2023 c 25 s 81</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.4582">
        <h1 class="shn">169.4582 REPORTABLE OFFENSE ON SCHOOL BUS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4582.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Reportable offense; definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Reportable offense" means misbehavior causing an immediate and substantial danger to self or surrounding persons or property under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/121A.45">121A.45</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.4582.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duty to report; school official.</span></h2>
          <p>Consistent with the school bus safety policy under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/123B.91#stat.123B.91.1">123B.91, subdivision 1</a>, the school principal, the school transportation safety director, or other designated school official shall immediately report to the local law enforcement agency having jurisdiction where the misbehavior occurred and to the school superintendent if the reporting school official knows or has reason to believe that a student has committed a reportable offense on a school bus or in a bus loading or unloading area. The reporting school official shall issue a report to the commissioner of public safety concerning the incident upon request of the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.4582.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/647/#laws.12.27.0">1994 c 647 art 12 s 27</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/397/#laws.11.3.0">1998 c 397 art 11 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/137/#laws.0.8.0">2012 c 137 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">VEHICLE EQUIPMENT, SAFETY</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.46">
        <h1 class="shn">169.46 HITCHING BEHIND VEHICLE.</h1>
        <p>No person shall hitch a toboggan, hand sled, bicycle, or other similar device onto any motor vehicle or streetcar while being used on a highway.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.46.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-232</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.82.0">1937 c 464 s 82</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/24/#laws.0.3.0">2001 c 24 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.467">
        <h1 class="shn">169.467 MOTOR VEHICLE SAFETY STANDARDS; DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.467.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.467">169.467</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.469">169.469</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.467.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Motor vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>"Motor vehicle" means any vehicle driven or drawn by mechanical power manufactured primarily for use on the public streets, roads and highways, except any vehicle operated exclusively on a rail or rails.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.467.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">New motor vehicle; new vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>"New motor vehicle" or "new vehicle" means a motor vehicle as defined herein heretofore unregistered.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.467.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">New item of motor vehicle equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>"New item of motor vehicle equipment" or "new equipment" means any option, device, accessory or other equipment in the possession of a retail merchant including an automobile dealer prior to its initial retail sale designed to be attached to a motor vehicle as a part thereof or to be used in conjunction therewith.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.467.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Motor vehicle safety standard.</span></h2>
          <p>"Motor vehicle safety standard" means a minimum standard for motor vehicle performance, or motor vehicle equipment performance which is practicable, which meets the need for motor vehicle safety and which provides objective criteria.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.467.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/21/#laws.0.1.0">1974 c 21 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.468">
        <h1 class="shn">169.468 VEHICLE SAFETY RULES; FEDERAL SAFETY STANDARDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.468.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Federal motor vehicle safety standards.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of public safety, pursuant to the Administrative Procedure Act, may adopt and enforce rules in substantial conformity with federal motor vehicle safety standards established by the United States Secretary of Transportation pursuant to the national Traffic and Motor Vehicle Safety Act of 1966 (Public Law 89-563) with respect to any new motor vehicle or new item of motor vehicle equipment applicable to the same aspect of performance of such new vehicle or new equipment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.468.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Other safety standards; fee for testing and approval.</span></h2>
          <p>In the absence of a motor vehicle safety standard adopted pursuant to the national Traffic and Motor Vehicle Safety Act of 1966 or if any such standard is not applicable to new vehicles or new equipment manufactured and first sold in the state of Minnesota, the commissioner of public safety may require new vehicles and specific types of new equipment to be tested and approved for compliance with the requirements of this chapter, or any rule adopted pursuant to this chapter. The commissioner shall approve or disapprove of the vehicle or equipment within a reasonable time after it is submitted. Approval may be based upon a certificate of approval or test report furnished to the commissioner by the American Association of Motor Vehicle Administrators. If such new vehicle or new equipment does not conform to the provisions of this chapter, or to such rules adopted by the commissioner of public safety, no person shall sell, offer for sale, or use any such new vehicle or new equipment. The commissioner of public safety is authorized to set and collect a reasonable fee from the manufacturer or distributor for the testing and approval of all new vehicles and specific types of new equipment upon which approval is required under this section. Such fee may be sufficient in amount to reimburse the Department of Public Safety for all costs connected with such test and approval. The commissioner shall waive the fee for any approval based on a certificate of approval or test report furnished by the American Association of Motor Vehicle Administrators.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.468.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Conflicts of laws.</span></h2>
          <p>A federal motor vehicle safety standard adopted by the commissioner of public safety which conflicts with an equipment provision of this chapter, applicable to the same aspect of performance, shall supersede, on its effective date, the conflicting equipment provision of this chapter, with respect to new motor vehicles.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.468.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who violates the provisions of this section is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.468.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/21/#laws.0.2.0">1974 c 21 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/494/#laws.0.3.0">1978 c 494 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.66.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 66</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.469">
        <h1 class="shn">169.469 INJUNCTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.469.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authority of district court.</span></h2>
          <p>The district courts of this state have the authority to restrain or enjoin a violation or threatened violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.468">169.468</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.469.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Injunctive power of attorney general.</span></h2>
          <p>Whenever it appears to the satisfaction of the attorney general that any party has sold or offered for sale or is selling or offering for sale any such new motor vehicle or new item of motor vehicle equipment in violation of this section, the attorney general may, in the name of the state, seek injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction against any such violation or threatened violation.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.469.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/21/#laws.0.3.0">1974 c 21 s 3</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.47">
        <h1 class="shn">169.47 UNSAFE EQUIPMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.47.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor; exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) It is unlawful and punishable as hereinafter provided for any person to drive or for the owner to cause or knowingly permit to be driven on any highway any vehicle or combination of vehicles which is in such unsafe condition as to endanger any person, or which does not contain those parts or is not at all times equipped with such lamps and other equipment in proper condition and adjustment as required in this chapter, or which is equipped in any manner in violation of this chapter, or for any person to do any act forbidden or fail to perform any act required under this chapter.</p>
          <p>(b) The provisions of this chapter with respect to equipment on vehicles do not apply to implements of husbandry, road machinery, or road rollers except as otherwise provided in this chapter.</p>
          <p>(c) For purposes of this section, a specialized vehicle resembling a low-slung trailer having a short bed or platform shall be deemed to be an implement of husbandry when such vehicle is used exclusively to transport implements of husbandry, provided, however, that no such vehicle shall operate on the highway before sunrise or after sunset unless proper lighting is affixed to the implement being drawn.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.47.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/494/#laws.0.6.0">1978 c 494 s 6</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.47.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-233</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.83.0">1937 c 464 s 83</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.16.0">1939 c 430 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/256/#laws.0.1.0">1969 c 256 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.11.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/730/#laws.0.1.0">1973 c 730 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/187/#laws.0.5.0">1993 c 187 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/600/#laws.0.2.0">1994 c 600 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.471">
        <h1 class="shn">169.471 TELEVISION; HEADPHONES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.471.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Television screen in vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">No television screen shall be installed or used in any motor vehicle where images from the screen are visible to the driver while operating the motor vehicle except:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) video screens installed in law enforcement vehicles;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) closed-circuit video systems used exclusively to aid the driver's visibility to the front, rear, or sides of the vehicle; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) video screens installed as part of a vehicle control system or used in intelligent vehicle highway applications.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.471.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Use of headphones in vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> (a) No person, while operating a motor vehicle, shall wear headphones or earphones that are used in both ears simultaneously for purposes of receiving or listening to broadcasts or reproductions from radios, tape decks, or other sound-producing or transmitting devices.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Paragraph (a) does not prohibit:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the use of a hearing aid device by a person who needs the device;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the use of a communication headset by a firefighter while operating a fire department emergency vehicle in response to an emergency; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the use of a communication headset by an emergency medical services person while operating an ambulance subject to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144E.101">144E.101</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.471.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/78/#laws.0.1.0">1949 c 78 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.12.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/460/#laws.0.1.0">1974 c 460 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/26/#laws.0.4.0">1993 c 26 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/131/#laws.0.2.0">1999 c 131 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/208/#laws.0.1.0">2006 c 208 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/287/#laws.1.47.0">2008 c 287 art 1 s 47</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.475">
        <h1 class="shn">169.475 USE OF WIRELESS COMMUNICATIONS DEVICE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.475.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "Electronic message" means a self-contained piece of digital communication that is designed or intended to be transmitted between physical devices. An electronic message includes, but is not limited to: email; a text message; an instant message; a command or request to access a web page; a voice mail message; a transmitted image; transmitted video content, including through video calling; transmitted gaming data; and other data transmitted using a commonly recognized electronic communications protocol. An electronic message does not include: voice or audio data transmitted as a result of making a phone call; data transmitted between a motor vehicle and a wireless communications device located in the vehicle; data transmitted by a two-way radio, citizens band radio, or amateur radio used in accordance with Federal Communications Commission rules and regulations; or data transmitted automatically without direct initiation by a person.</p>
          <p>(c) "Voice-activated or hands-free mode" means an attachment, accessory, wirelessly paired or tethered capability, application, wireless connection, or built-in feature of a wireless communications device or a motor vehicle that allows the person to use verbal or single touch commands to:</p>
          <p>(1) activate or deactivate the device; and</p>
          <p>(2) activate or deactivate a function or software application of the device.</p>
          <p class="bl">Voice-activated or hands-free mode does not include typing or scrolling on a device.</p>
          <p>(d) For purposes of this section, a motor vehicle is not in motion or a part of traffic if the vehicle is lawfully stopped, is in a location that is not designed or ordinarily used for vehicular travel, and is not obstructing traffic.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.475.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibition on use; penalty.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Except as provided in subdivision 3, when a motor vehicle is in motion or a part of traffic, the person operating the vehicle upon a street or highway is prohibited from:</p>
          <p>(1) holding a wireless communications device with one or both hands; or</p>
          <p class="in">(2) using a wireless communications device to:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) initiate, compose, send, retrieve, or read an electronic message;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) engage in a cellular phone call, including initiating a call, talking or listening, and participating in video calling; and</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) access the following types of content stored on the device: video content, audio content, images, games, or software applications.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates paragraph (a) a second or subsequent time must pay a fine of $275.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.475.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The prohibitions in subdivision 2 do not apply if a person uses a wireless communications device:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) solely in a voice-activated or hands-free mode to (i) initiate or participate in a cellular phone call, provided that the person does not hold the device with one or both hands; or (ii) initiate, compose, send, or listen to an electronic message;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) to view or operate a global positioning system or navigation system in a manner that does not require the driver to type while the vehicle is in motion or a part of traffic, provided that the person does not hold the device with one or both hands;</p>
          <p>(3) to listen to audio-based content in a manner that does not require the driver to scroll or type while the vehicle is in motion or a part of traffic, provided that the person does not hold the device with one or both hands;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) to obtain emergency assistance to (i) report a traffic accident, medical emergency, or serious traffic hazard, or (ii) prevent a crime about to be committed;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) in the reasonable belief that a person's life or safety is in immediate danger; or</p>
          <p class="in">(6) in an authorized emergency vehicle while in the performance of official duties.</p>
          <p>(b) The exception in paragraph (a), clause (1), does not apply to accessing nonnavigation video content, engaging in video calling, engaging in live-streaming, accessing gaming data, or reading electronic messages.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.475.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
