        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.38.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 38</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/75/#laws.2.22.0">2015 c 75 art 2 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/11/#laws.0.2.0">2019 c 11 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.4.50.0">2023 c 68 art 4 s 50</a>,51</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.48">
        <h1 class="shn">169.48 VEHICLE LIGHTING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.48.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Lights to be displayed.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Every vehicle upon a highway within this state:</p>
          <p>(1) at any time from sunset to sunrise;</p>
          <p>(2) at any time when it is raining, snowing, sleeting, or hailing; and</p>
          <p>(3) at any other time when visibility is impaired by weather, smoke, fog or other conditions or there is not sufficient light to render clearly discernible persons and vehicles on the highway at a distance of 500 feet ahead;</p>
          <p class="bl">shall display lighted headlamps, lighted tail lamps, and illuminating devices, as hereinafter, respectively, required for different classes of vehicles, subject to exceptions with respect to parked vehicles and law enforcement vehicles, as hereinafter stated. In addition to the other requirements of this paragraph, every school bus transporting children upon a highway within this state, at any time from a half hour before sunrise to a half hour after sunset, shall display lighted headlamps, lighted tail lamps, and illuminating devices as required by this paragraph, except that the operator shall use the lowermost distribution of light specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.60">169.60</a> unless conditions warrant otherwise.</p>
          <p>(b) When requirement is hereinafter declared as to the distance from which certain lamps and devices shall render objects visible or within which such lamps or devices shall be visible, these provisions shall apply during the time stated in this section upon a straight level unlighted highway under normal atmospheric conditions unless a different time or condition is expressly stated and unless otherwise specified the location of lamps and devices shall refer to the center of such lamps or devices. Parking lamps shall not be used in lieu of headlamps to satisfy the requirements of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.48.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Certain violations; negligence.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.96">169.96</a>, a violation of subdivision 1, paragraph (a), clause (2), is not negligence per se or prima facie evidence of negligence.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.48.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-234</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.84.0">1937 c 464 s 84</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/218/#laws.0.1.0">1967 c 218 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/134/#laws.0.1.0">1974 c 134 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/482/#laws.0.1.0">1990 c 482 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/555/#laws.0.8.0">1990 c 555 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/45/#laws.0.1.0">2003 c 45 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.49">
        <h1 class="shn">169.49 HEADLAMPS.</h1>
        <p>(a) Every motor vehicle other than a motorcycle must be equipped with at least two headlamps, including at least one on each side of the front of the motor vehicle. Headlamps must comply with the requirements and limitations set forth in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.47">169.47</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.66">169.66</a>.</p>
        <p>(b) Every motorcycle must be equipped with at least one and not more than four headlamps, which must comply with the requirements and limitations of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.47">169.47</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.66">169.66</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.49.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-235</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.85.0">1937 c 464 s 85</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1957/0/754/#laws.0.1.0">1957 c 754 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/75/#laws.2.23.0">2015 c 75 art 2 s 23</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.50">
        <h1 class="shn">169.50 REAR LAMPS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.50.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Requirements; exception.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Every motor vehicle and every vehicle that is being drawn at the end of a train of vehicles must be equipped with at least one tail lamp, exhibiting a red light plainly visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear.</p>
          <p>(b) Every motor vehicle, other than a truck-tractor, and every vehicle that is being drawn at the end of a train of vehicles, registered in this state and manufactured or assembled after January 1, 1960, must be equipped with at least two tail lamps mounted on the rear and on the same level and as widely spaced laterally as practicable. When lighted, the tail lamps must comply with the provisions of this section.</p>
          <p>(c) An implement of husbandry being towed by a motor vehicle at a speed of not more than 30 miles per hour, displaying a slow-moving vehicle emblem, and complying with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.55#stat.169.55.2">169.55, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), clause (4), is not subject to the requirements of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.50.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">License plates.</span></h2>
          <p>Either such rear lamp or separate lamp shall be so constructed and placed as to illuminate with a white light the rear registration plate and render it legible from a distance of 50 feet to the rear. Any rear lamp or rear lamps, together with any separate lamp for illuminating the rear registration plate, shall be so wired as to be lighted whenever the headlamps or auxiliary driving lamps are lighted.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.50.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reflectors.</span></h2>
          <p>On and after January 1, 1960, each new motor vehicle, trailer, or semitrailer, hereafter sold and each such vehicle hereafter operated on a highway, shall carry at the rear either as a part of the rear lamp, or separately, at least two reflectors. The reflectors shall be of a type approved by the commissioner of public safety and shall be mounted as close as is practicable to the extreme edges of the vehicle at a height not more than 60, nor less than 20 inches above the surface upon which the vehicle stands. Each such reflector shall be so designed and maintained as to be visible at night from all distances within 300 to 50 feet from the vehicle, except that on a commercial vehicle the reflectors shall be visible from all distances within 500 to 50 feet from the vehicle, when directly in front of a motor vehicle displaying lawfully lighted headlamps.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.50.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-236</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.86.0">1937 c 464 s 86</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.25.0">1947 c 428 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1953/0/201/#laws.0.1.0">1953 c 201 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1957/0/754/#laws.0.2.0">1957 c 754 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/215/#laws.0.1.0">1959 c 215 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/521/#laws.0.6.0">1959 c 521 s 6</a>,7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.15.0">1971 c 491 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/43/#laws.0.1.0">2001 c 43 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/10/#laws.1.29.0">2005 c 10 art 1 s 29</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.51">
        <h1 class="shn">169.51 CLEARANCE AND MARKER LAMPS.</h1>
        <p>(a) Every motor vehicle or motor-drawn vehicle designed or used for the transportation of property, or for the transportation of passengers for compensation, shall display lighted lamps, as required in this section.</p>
        <p>(b) Every such vehicle having a width, including load thereon, at any part in excess of 80 inches shall be equipped with four clearance lamps, two located on the front at opposite sides and not more than six inches from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle or load, displaying a white or amber light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle, and two located on the rear on opposite sides not more than six inches from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle or load, displaying a red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear of the vehicle. The front clearance lamps shall be located at a height of not less than 24 inches above the headlamp centers. The rear clearance lamps shall be in addition to the red rear lamp hereinbefore required.</p>
        <p>(c) Every such vehicle or combination of such vehicles which exceeds 30 feet in overall length shall be equipped with at least four side marker lamps, one on each side near the front and one on each side near the rear. Such lamps shall be at a height of not less than 24 inches above the surface upon which the vehicle stands. The lamps near the front shall display a white or amber light and lamps near the rear shall display a red light, each visible from a distance of 500 feet to the side of the vehicle on which it is located. If the clearance lamps on the right and left sides of the vehicle, as hereinbefore required, display lights visible from a distance of 500 feet at right angles to the right and left side, respectively, of the vehicle, they shall be deemed to meet the requirements as to marker lamps, provided an additional marker lamp, white or amber, is displayed approximately midway between the above specified marker lamps.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.51.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-237</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.87.0">1937 c 464 s 87</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.515">
        <h1 class="shn">169.515 LIGHTS ON GRANT PROGRAM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.515.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "high poverty area" means a census tract as reported in the most recently completed decennial census published by the United States Bureau of the Census that has a poverty area rate of at least 20 percent or in which the median family income does not exceed 80 percent of the greater of the statewide or metropolitan median family income.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.515.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Grant program established.</span></h2>
          <p>The Lights On grant program is established under this section to provide drivers on Minnesota roads with vouchers of up to $250 to use at participating auto repair shops to repair or replace broken or malfunctioning lighting equipment required under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.49">169.49</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.51">169.51</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.515.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Eligibility.</span></h2>
          <p>Counties, cities, towns, the State Patrol, and local law enforcement agencies, including law enforcement agencies of a federally recognized Tribe, as defined in United States Code, title 25, section 5304(e), are eligible to apply for grants under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.515.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner of public safety must develop application materials and procedures for the Lights On grant program.</p>
          <p>(b) The application must describe the type or types of intended vouchers, the amount of money requested, and any other information deemed necessary by the commissioner.</p>
          <p>(c) Applicants must submit an application under this section in the form and manner prescribed by the commissioner.</p>
          <p>(d) Applicants must describe how grant money will be used to provide and distribute vouchers to drivers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.515.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Use of grant award.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Applicants must keep records of vouchers distributed and records of all expenses associated with awarded grant money.</p>
          <p>(b) Applicants must not use awarded grant money for administrative costs. A nonstate organization that contracts with the commissioner to operate the program must not retain any of the grant money for administrative costs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.515.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Vouchers.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An applicant must not distribute more than one voucher per motor vehicle in a 90-day period.</p>
          <p>(b) A voucher that is distributed to a driver must contain the following information:</p>
          <p>(1) the motor vehicle license plate number;</p>
          <p>(2) the date of issuance; and</p>
          <p>(3) the badge number of the peace officer distributing the voucher.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.515.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Grant criteria.</span></h2>
          <p>Preference for grant awards must be given to applicants whose proposals provide resources and vouchers to individuals residing in geographic areas that (1) have higher crash rates or higher numbers of tickets issued for broken or malfunctioning lighting equipment, or (2) are high poverty areas.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.515.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) By February 1 each year, grant recipients must submit a report to the commissioner itemizing all expenditures made using grant money during the previous calendar year, the purpose of each expenditure, and the disposition of each contact made with drivers with malfunctioning or broken lighting equipment. The report must be in the form and manner prescribed by the commissioner.</p>
          <p>(b) By March 15 each year, the commissioner must submit a report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over transportation policy and finance. The report must list, for the previous calendar year:</p>
          <p>(1) the participating grant recipients and the total number and dollar amount of vouchers that each grant recipient distributed; and</p>
          <p>(2) the participating auto repair shops and the total number and dollar amount of vouchers that each received.</p>
          <p class="bl">Grant recipients and any program organization contracted by the commissioner must provide information as requested by the commissioner to complete the report required under this paragraph.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.515.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.3.60.0">2024 c 127 art 3 s 60</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.52">
        <h1 class="shn">169.52 PROJECTING LOAD; LIGHT OR FLAG.</h1>
        <p>When the load upon any vehicle extends to the rear four feet or more beyond the bed or body of such vehicle there shall be displayed at the extreme rear end of the load, at the times when lighted lamps on vehicles are required in this chapter, a red light or lantern plainly visible from a distance of at least 500 feet to the sides and rear. The light or lantern required under this section shall be in addition to the rear light required upon every vehicle. At any time when no lights are required there shall be displayed at the extreme rear end of such load a red, yellow or orange flag or cloth not less than 16 inches square.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.52.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-238</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.88.0">1937 c 464 s 88</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/56/#laws.0.1.0">1973 c 56 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.522">
        <h1 class="shn">169.522 SLOW-MOVING VEHICLE, SIGN REQUIRED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.522.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Displaying emblem; rules.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) All animal-drawn vehicles, motorized golf carts when operated on designated roadways pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.045">169.045</a>, implements of husbandry, and other machinery, including all road construction machinery, which are designed for operation at a speed of 30 miles per hour or less, must display a triangular slow-moving vehicle emblem, except (1) when being used in actual construction and maintenance work and traveling within the limits of a construction area marked in accordance with the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, as set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06">169.06</a>, or (2) for a towed implement of husbandry that is empty and that is not self-propelled, in which case it may be towed at lawful speeds greater than 30 miles per hour without removing the slow-moving vehicle emblem. The emblem must consist of a fluorescent or illuminated red-orange triangle with a dark red reflective border and be mounted so as to be visible from a distance of not less than 600 feet to the rear. When a primary power unit towing an implement of husbandry or other machinery displays a slow-moving vehicle emblem visible from a distance of 600 feet to the rear, it is not necessary to display a similar emblem on the secondary unit. All slow-moving vehicle emblems sold in this state must be so designed that when properly mounted they are visible from a distance of not less than 600 feet to the rear when directly in front of lawful lower beam of headlamps on a motor vehicle. The commissioner of public safety shall adopt standards and specifications for the design and position of mounting the slow-moving vehicle emblem. Such standards and specifications must be adopted by rule in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act.</p>
          <p>(b) An alternate slow-moving vehicle emblem consisting of a dull black triangle with a white reflective border may be used after obtaining a permit from the commissioner under rules of the commissioner. A person with a permit to use an alternate slow-moving vehicle emblem must:</p>
          <p>(1) carry in the vehicle a regular slow-moving vehicle emblem and display the emblem when operating a vehicle between sunset and sunrise, and at any other time when visibility is impaired by weather, smoke, fog, or other conditions; and</p>
          <p>(2) permanently affix to the rear of the slow-moving vehicle at least 72 square inches of reflective tape that reflects the color red.</p>
          <p>(c) In addition to the emblem requirement under this subdivision, an animal-drawn vehicle must comply with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.58#stat.169.58.6">169.58, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.522.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibition on use.</span></h2>
          <p>The use of this emblem is restricted to the slow-moving vehicles specified in subdivision 1 and its use on any other type of vehicle or stationary object on the highway is prohibited.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.522.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Display required.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall sell, lease, rent, or operate any slow-moving vehicle, as defined in subdivision 1, except motorized golf carts and except those units designed to be completely mounted on a primary power unit, which is manufactured or assembled on or after July 1, 1967, unless the vehicle is equipped with a slow-moving vehicle emblem-mounting device as specified in subdivision 1. Provided however, a slow-moving vehicle must not be operated without such slow-moving vehicle emblem.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.522.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/309/#laws.0.1.0">1967 c 309 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.16.0">1971 c 491 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/57/#laws.0.1.0">1974 c 57 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/549/#laws.0.3.0">1982 c 549 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/101/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 101 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/187/#laws.0.6.0">1993 c 187 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/600/#laws.0.3.0">1994 c 600 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/143/#laws.0.14.0">1997 c 143 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/6/#laws.3.48.0">1Sp2005 c 6 art 3 s 48</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/5/#laws.4.63.0">1Sp2021 c 5 art 4 s 63</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.53">
        <h1 class="shn">169.53 LIGHTS FOR PARKED VEHICLES.</h1>
        <p>When a vehicle is parked or stopped upon a highway or shoulder adjacent thereto during the times when lighted lamps on vehicles are required, it shall be equipped with one or more lamps which shall exhibit a white or amber light on the roadway side visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle and a red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear, except that local authorities may provide by ordinance that no lights need be displayed upon a vehicle when stopped or parked in accordance with local parking regulations upon a highway where there is sufficient light to clearly reveal any person or object within a distance of 500 feet upon the highway. Any lighted headlamps upon a parked vehicle shall be depressed or dimmed.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.53.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-239</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.89.0">1937 c 464 s 89</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.26.0">1947 c 428 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/96/#laws.0.1.0">1959 c 96 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.54"><b>169.54</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/132/#laws.0.1.0">1951 c 132 s 1</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.541">
        <h1 class="shn">169.541 LIGHTING EXEMPTION FOR LAW ENFORCEMENT; STANDARDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.541.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Exemption.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/84.87">84.87</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/84.928">84.928</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/86B.511">86B.511</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.48">169.48</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.65">169.65</a>, relating to lighting of vehicles and watercraft, do not apply to a licensed peace officer, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (c), while operating a motor vehicle or watercraft owned, leased, or otherwise the property of the state or a political subdivision, in the performance of the officer's law enforcement duties if the officer's conduct is reasonable and is consistent with the standards adopted under subdivision 2, and if the officer reasonably believes that operating the vehicle without lights is necessary under the circumstances to investigate a criminal violation or suspected criminal violation of state laws, rules, or orders or local laws, ordinances, or regulations.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.541.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">POST Board standards.</span></h2>
          <p>The Peace Officer Standards and Training Board shall adopt standards governing situations in which licensed peace officers as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (c), may operate a vehicle or watercraft without lights as provided in subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.541.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/391/#laws.10.3.0">1990 c 391 art 10 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/555/#laws.0.9.0">1990 c 555 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.67.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 67</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.55">
        <h1 class="shn">169.55 LIGHTS ON ALL VEHICLES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.55.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Lights or reflectors required.</span></h2>
          <p>At the times when lighted lamps on vehicles are required each vehicle including an animal-drawn vehicle and any vehicle specifically excepted in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.47">169.47</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.79">169.79</a>, with respect to equipment and not previously required to be equipped with lamps, must be equipped with one or more lighted lamps or lanterns projecting a white light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle and with a lamp or lantern exhibiting a red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear, except that reflectors meeting the maximum requirements of this chapter may be used in lieu of the lights required in this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.55.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Implement of husbandry.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) At the times when lighted lamps on vehicles are required:</p>
          <p>(1) every self-propelled implement of husbandry must be equipped with at least one lamp displaying a white light to the front, and at least one lamp displaying a red light to the rear;</p>
          <p>(2) every self-propelled implement of husbandry must also display two red reflectors visible to the rear;</p>
          <p>(3) every combination of a self-propelled and towed implement of husbandry must be equipped with at least one lamp mounted to indicate as nearly as practicable the extreme left projection of the combination and displaying a white or amber light to the front and a red or amber light to the rear of the self-propelled implement of husbandry; and</p>
          <p>(4) the last unit of every combination of implements of husbandry must display two red reflectors visible to the rear.</p>
          <p>(b) The reflectors must be of the type approved for use upon commercial vehicles. The reflectors must be mounted as close as practicable to the extreme edges of the implement of husbandry. The reflectors must be reflex reflectors that are visible at night from all distances within 600 feet to 100 feet when directly in front of lawful lower beams of headlamps.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.55.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Implement of husbandry; hazard warning lights.</span></h2>
          <p>No person may operate a self-propelled implement of husbandry manufactured after January 1, 1970, on a highway unless the implement of husbandry displays vehicular hazard warning lights visible to the front and rear in normal sunlight.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.55.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-241</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.91.0">1937 c 464 s 91</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.27.0">1947 c 428 s 27</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/574/#laws.0.0.0">1949 c 574</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/410/#laws.0.1.0">1959 c 410 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/185/#laws.0.2.0">1979 c 185 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/44/#laws.0.1.0">1981 c 44 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/187/#laws.0.7.0">1993 c 187 s 7</a>,8; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/238/#laws.2.21.0">1999 c 238 art 2 s 21</a>,93; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/479/#laws.1.12.0">2000 c 479 art 1 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.53.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 53</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.56">
        <h1 class="shn">169.56 AUXILIARY LIGHTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.56.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Spotlight.</span></h2>
          <p>Any motor vehicle may be equipped with not to exceed two spot lamps and every lighted spot lamp shall be so aimed and used upon approaching another vehicle that no part of the high-intensity portion of the beam will be directed on the road surface to the left of the center of the vehicle, nor more than 100 feet ahead of the vehicle upon which such lamps are mounted.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.56.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Fog light.</span></h2>
          <p>Any motor vehicle may be equipped with not to exceed two fog lamps mounted on the front at a height not less than 12 inches nor more than 30 inches above the level surface upon which the vehicle stands and so aimed that when the vehicle is not loaded none of the high-intensity portion of the light to the left of the center of the vehicle shall at a distance of 25 feet ahead project higher than a level of four inches below the level of the center of the lamp from which it comes. Lighted fog lamps meeting the above requirements may be used with lower headlamp beams as specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.60">169.60</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.56.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Auxiliary low-beam light.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as provided in subdivision 5, any motor vehicle may be equipped with not to exceed two auxiliary low-beam lamps mounted on the front at a height of not less than 24 inches nor more than 42 inches above the level surface upon which the vehicle stands. The provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.60">169.60</a> shall apply to any combination of headlamps and auxiliary low-beam lamps.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.56.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Auxiliary driving light.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as provided in subdivision 5, any motor vehicle may be equipped with not to exceed two auxiliary driving lamps mounted on the front at a height not less than 16 inches nor more than 42 inches above the level surface upon which the vehicle stands. The provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.60">169.60</a> shall apply to any combination of headlamps and auxiliary driving lamps.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.56.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exception for light obstructed by snowplow blade.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The auxiliary lamps permitted in subdivision 3 may be mounted more than 42 inches high on any truck equipped with a snowplow blade that obstructs the required headlights. The lights may not be illuminated when a snowplow blade is not mounted on the vehicle.</p>
          <p>(b) No other vehicle may be operated on a public highway unless the auxiliary lamps permitted in subdivisions 3 and 4 comply with the height requirements or are completely covered with an opaque material.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.56.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Motorcycle ground light.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.64#stat.169.64.4a">169.64, subdivision 4a</a>, a motorcycle may be equipped with white ground lights mounted under the motorcycle if:</p>
          <p>(1) the bulbs or strips are not visible to operators of other vehicles; and</p>
          <p>(2) the lights are aimed so as to project a steady, nonflashing beam not more than six feet in radius directly onto the roadway and illuminate an area around the motorcycle.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.56.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-242</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.92.0">1937 c 464 s 92</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/207/#laws.0.2.0">1945 c 207 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/521/#laws.0.5.0">1959 c 521 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/26/#laws.0.5.0">1993 c 26 s 5</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/600/#laws.0.4.0">1994 c 600 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/104/#laws.1.39.0">2024 c 104 art 1 s 39</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.57">
        <h1 class="shn">169.57 VEHICLE SIGNALS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.57.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Stoplights.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any vehicle may be equipped and when required under this chapter, shall be equipped with at least two stop lamps on the rear which shall emit a red or yellow light and which shall be actuated upon application of the service (foot) brake and which may, but need not be, incorporated with the tail lamps and which shall be plainly visible and understandable from a distance of 100 feet to the rear during normal sunlight and at night.</p>
          <p>(b) No person shall sell or offer for sale or operate on the highways any motor vehicle registered in this state and manufactured or assembled after January 1, 1960, unless it is equipped with at least two stop lamps meeting the requirements of this subdivision, except that a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or truck-tractor manufactured or assembled after said date shall be equipped with at least one stop lamp meeting the requirements of this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.57.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Turn signal.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any vehicle may be equipped, and when required under this chapter shall be equipped, with a lamp or lamps or mechanical signal device of such color as may be approved by the commissioner of public safety and capable of clearly indicating any intention to turn either to the right or to the left and shall be visible and understandable during both daytime and nighttime from a distance of 100 feet both to the front and rear.</p>
          <p>(b) It is unlawful for any person to sell or offer for sale any new motor vehicle, excepting motorcycles, motor scooters, and bicycles with motor attached, unless it is equipped with turn signals meeting the requirements of this chapter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.57.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Maintenance.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) When a vehicle is equipped with stop lamps or signal lamps, the lamps must at all times be maintained in good working condition.</p>
          <p>(b) All mechanical signal devices must be self-illumined when in use at the times when lighted lamps on vehicles are required.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.57.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Alteration of stop lamp prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>On a vehicle that must be equipped with a single center high-mounted stop lamp under federal motor vehicle safety standards, and on any other vehicle equipped with a similar stop lamp, a person may not alter the stop lamp by the addition of an overlay or other device, or install a replacement lens, if the alteration or installation alters or obscures any portion of the lamp or affects the intensity of light emitted.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.57.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-243</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.93.0">1937 c 464 s 93</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/207/#laws.0.3.0">1945 c 207 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.28.0">1947 c 428 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/90/#laws.0.2.0">1949 c 90 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/521/#laws.0.8.0">1959 c 521 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/328/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 328 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/383/#laws.0.13.0">1987 c 383 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.54.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 54</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.68.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 68</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.58">
        <h1 class="shn">169.58 IDENTIFICATION LAMPS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.58.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Wide or long vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>Any vehicle or combination of vehicles having a width including load thereon at any part in excess of 80 inches or which exceeds 30 feet in overall length may be equipped with identification lamps on the front displaying three amber or white lights and identification lamps on the rear displaying three red lights, and when so equipped the lights in each such group shall be evenly spaced not less than 6 nor more than 12 inches apart, along a horizontal line as near to the top of the vehicle as practicable, and these lights shall be visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front and rear, respectively, of the vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.58.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Red lamp; permit for volunteer emergency responders.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon obtaining a permit from the commissioner of public safety, any motor vehicles operated by an active member of a volunteer fire department authorized by or contracting with any city, town, or township in this state, an emergency medical first responder, or an ambulance crew member may be equipped with a lamp emitting a red light to the front of such vehicle. The lens of such lamp shall be not more than three inches in diameter. Such lamp shall be lighted only when the member of the volunteer fire department, ambulance crew member, or emergency medical first responder is responding to an emergency call in connection with duties as a volunteer firefighter, ambulance crew member, or responder. The commissioner of public safety is hereby authorized to issue permits on applications of a member of a volunteer fire department properly certified to by the chief of said volunteer fire department, and on applications for emergency medical first responders or ambulance crew members. The commissioner of public safety must be notified immediately upon the termination of membership in a volunteer fire department or when an ambulance or permitted emergency medical first responder ceases operations.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.58.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Volunteer ambulance driver.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of public safety, upon application therefor, may issue a permit to any certificated volunteer ambulance driver authorizing the driver to equip any privately owned motor vehicle operated by the driver with a lamp emitting a red light to the front of the vehicle. The lamps shall conform to specifications adopted by the commissioner. The lamp shall be lighted only when the driver is proceeding to the location of an ambulance in response to an emergency call. The application shall be in the form prescribed by the commissioner and shall contain verification satisfactory to the commissioner of the applicant's status as a certificated volunteer ambulance driver. Any permit issued shall expire immediately upon termination of the permittee's employment as a volunteer ambulance driver.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.58.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Lighted sign on vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>A vehicle engaged in deliveries to residences may display a lighting device mounted on the vehicle, which may project a red light to the front if the sign projects one or more additional colors to the front.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.58.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Transportation network company vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this subdivision, the definitions in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/65B.472#stat.65B.472.1">65B.472, subdivision 1</a>, apply except that "transportation network company vehicle" has the meaning given to "personal vehicle" in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/65B.472">65B.472</a>, subdivision 1, paragraph (c).</p>
          <p>(b) A transportation network company vehicle may be equipped with no more than two removable, interior-mounted, trade dress identifying devices as provided by the transportation network company that are designed to assist riders in identifying and communicating with drivers. The identifying device may be illuminated and emit a steady beam of solid colored light in any direction when the driver is logged into the digital network. The identifying device must not: (1) display the colors red, amber, or blue; (2) project a flashing, oscillating, alternating, or rotating light; or (3) project a glaring or dazzling light.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.58.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Animal-drawn vehicles.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An animal-drawn vehicle must be equipped with an identification lamp or lamps that indicate the vehicle's presence and are visible from a distance of at least 500 feet from both the front and the rear. The lighting requirement under this subdivision may be met using a lamp powered by energy generated from the vehicle's movement.</p>
          <p>(b) This subdivision does not apply to an animal-drawn vehicle that: (1) operates exclusively between the hours of sunrise and sunset and never during periods of reduced visibility, inclement weather, or insufficient light; or (2) never operates on a public roadway.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.58.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-244</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.94.0">1937 c 464 s 94</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/207/#laws.0.4.0">1945 c 207 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/349/#laws.0.0.0">1949 c 349</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.17.0">1971 c 491 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/123/#laws.5.7.0">1973 c 123 art 5 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/429/#laws.0.63.0">1977 c 429 s 63</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/404/#laws.0.1.0">1980 c 404 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/112/#laws.0.2.0">1991 c 112 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/238/#laws.2.22.0">1999 c 238 art 2 s 22</a>,93; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/479/#laws.1.12.0">2000 c 479 art 1 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.55.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 55</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/5/#laws.4.64.0">1Sp2021 c 5 art 4 s 64</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.59">
        <h1 class="shn">169.59 WARNING LIGHTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.59.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Fender lights.</span></h2>
          <p>Any vehicle may be equipped with not more than two side cowl or fender lamps, one on each side which shall emit a white light without glare.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.59.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Running board light.</span></h2>
          <p>Any vehicle may be equipped with not more than one running board courtesy lamp on each side thereof, which shall emit a white or yellow light without glare.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.59.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Backup light.</span></h2>
          <p>Any vehicle may be equipped with not more than two backup lamps, either separately or in combination with another lamp, and not more than two rear cornering lamps, except that the lamps must not be continuously lighted when the vehicle is in forward motion, nor shall it project a glaring light.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.59.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Flashing warning light.</span></h2>
          <p>Any vehicle may be equipped with lamps which may be used for the purpose of warning the operators of other vehicles of the presence of a vehicular traffic hazard requiring the exercise of unusual care in approaching, overtaking, or passing, and when so equipped may display such warning in addition to any other warning signals required by this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.50#stat.169.50.1">169.50, subdivision 1</a> or 3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.56#stat.169.56.1">169.56, subdivision 1</a>, 2, 3, or 4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.57#stat.169.57.1">169.57, subdivision 1</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.64#stat.169.64.3">169.64, subdivision 3</a>. The lamps used to display such warnings to the front shall be mounted at the same level and as widely spaced laterally as practicable, and shall display simultaneous flashing white or amber lights, or any shade of color between white and amber. The lamps used to display such warnings to the rear shall be mounted at the same level and as widely spaced laterally as practicable, and shall show simultaneously flashing amber or red lights, or any shade of color between amber and red. Instead of a pair of lamps that flash simultaneously, either one or two strobe lights or rotating beacon lights with an amber or yellow lens may be used both to the front and rear of the vehicle. These warning lights shall be visible from a distance of not less than 500 feet under normal atmospheric conditions at night.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.59.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-245</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.95.0">1937 c 464 s 95</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/521/#laws.0.9.0">1959 c 521 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/549/#laws.0.30.0">1984 c 549 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/456/#laws.0.21.0">1996 c 456 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/10/#laws.1.30.0">2005 c 10 art 1 s 30</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.60">
        <h1 class="shn">169.60 DISTRIBUTION OF LIGHT.</h1>
        <p>Except as hereinafter provided, the headlamps, the auxiliary low-beam lamps, or the auxiliary driving lamps, or combinations thereof, on motor vehicles shall be so arranged that the driver may select at will between distributions of light projected to different elevations, subject to the following requirements and limitations:</p>
        <p>(a) There shall be an uppermost distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed and of such intensity as to reveal persons and vehicles at a distance of at least 350 feet ahead for all conditions of loading.</p>
        <p>(b) There shall be a lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a distance of at least 100 feet ahead; and on a straight level road under any condition of loading none of the high-intensity portion of the beam shall be directed to strike the eyes of an approaching driver.</p>
        <p>(c) All road-lighting equipment manufactured and installed on and after January 1, 1938, shall be so arranged that when any beam is used which is not in conformity with paragraph (b), means shall be provided for indicating to the driver when such beams are being used.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.60.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-246</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.96.0">1937 c 464 s 96</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/1/38/#laws.0.1.0">Ex1937 c 38 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1955/0/53/#laws.0.1.0">1955 c 53 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/26/#laws.0.8.0">1993 c 26 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.61">
        <h1 class="shn">169.61 COMPOSITE BEAM.</h1>
        <p>(a) When a motor vehicle is being operated on a highway or shoulder adjacent thereto during the times when lighted lamps on vehicles are required in this chapter, the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam, directed high enough and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a safe distance in advance of the vehicle, subject to the following requirements and limitations.</p>
        <p>(b) When the driver of a vehicle approaches a vehicle within 1,000 feet, such driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver.</p>
        <p>(c) When the driver of a vehicle follows another vehicle within 200 feet to the rear, except when engaged in the act of overtaking and passing, such driver shall use a distribution of light permissible under this chapter other than the uppermost distribution of light specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.60">169.60</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.61.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-247</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.97.0">1937 c 464 s 97</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/207/#laws.0.5.0">1945 c 207 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1953/0/330/#laws.0.1.0">1953 c 330 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1955/0/52/#laws.0.1.0">1955 c 52 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.62">
        <h1 class="shn">169.62 CERTAIN LIGHTS PERMITTED ON OLD MOTOR VEHICLES.</h1>
        <p>Headlamps arranged to provide a single distribution of light not supplemented by auxiliary driving lamps shall be permitted on motor vehicles manufactured and sold prior to January 1, 1938, in lieu of multiple-beam road-lighting equipment herein specified if the single distribution of light complies with the following requirements and limitations:</p>
        <p>(a) The headlamps shall be so aimed that when the vehicle is fully loaded none of the high-intensity portion of the lamp beam rises above a horizontal plane passing through the headlamp centers parallel to the level surface upon which the vehicle stands, and in no case higher than 42 inches above the level on which the vehicle stands at a distance of 75 and more feet ahead.</p>
        <p>(b) The intensity shall be sufficient to reveal persons and vehicles at a distance of at least 200 feet.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.62.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-248</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.98.0">1937 c 464 s 98</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.63">
        <h1 class="shn">169.63 NUMBER OF LAMPS.</h1>
        <p>(a) At all times when lighted lamps on vehicles are required in this chapter, at least two lighted headlamps shall be displayed, one on each side at the front of every motor vehicle, other than a motorcycle; provided, that under adverse weather conditions two lighted auxiliary lamps, one on each side at the front of the vehicle, may be used in lieu of two lighted headlamps, except when such vehicle is parked subject to the rules governing lights on parked vehicles.</p>
        <p>(b) When a motor vehicle equipped with headlamps, as herein required, is also equipped with any auxiliary lamps, spot lamps or any other lamps on the front thereof projecting a beam of intensity greater than 300-candle power, not more than a total of four of any such lamps on the front of a vehicle shall be lighted at any one time when upon a highway.</p>
        <p>(c) The maximum beam candle power from any combination of lamps used at any time for road lighting shall not exceed that authorized by the commissioner of public safety.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.63.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-249</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.99.0">1937 c 464 s 99</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.18.0">1939 c 430 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.18.0">1971 c 491 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.64">
        <h1 class="shn">169.64 PROHIBITED LIGHTS; EXCEPTIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Bright light.</span></h2>
          <p>Any lighted lamp or illuminating device upon a motor vehicle, other than a headlamp, a spot lamp, or an auxiliary driving lamp, which projects a beam of light of an intensity greater than 300-candle power, shall be so directed that no part of the beam will strike the level of the roadway on which the vehicle stands at a distance of more than 75 feet from the vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Colored light.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Unless otherwise authorized by the commissioner of public safety, no vehicle shall be equipped, nor shall any person drive or move any vehicle or equipment upon any highway with any lamp or device displaying a red light or any colored light other than those required or permitted in this chapter.</p>
          <p>(b) A vehicle manufactured for use as an emergency vehicle may display and use colored lights that are not otherwise required or permitted in this chapter, provided that the vehicle is owned and operated according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.10">168.10</a>, is owned and operated solely as a collector's item and not for general transportation purposes, and is registered under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.10#stat.168.10.1a">168.10, subdivision 1a</a>, 1b, 1c, 1d, 1g, or 1h. A person may not activate the colored lights authorized under this paragraph on streets or highways except as part of a parade or other special event.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Flashing lights; glaring lights.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Flashing lights are prohibited, except:</p>
          <p>(1) on an authorized emergency vehicle, school bus, bicycle as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.222#stat.169.222.6">169.222, subdivision 6</a>, road maintenance equipment, tow truck or towing vehicle as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168B.16">168B.16</a>, service vehicle, farm tractor, self-propelled farm equipment, rural mail carrier vehicle, or funeral home vehicle;</p>
          <p>(2) on any vehicle as a means of indicating a right or left turn, or the presence of a vehicular traffic hazard requiring unusual care in approaching, overtaking, or passing; or</p>
          <p>(3) as otherwise provided in this section.</p>
          <p>(b) All flashing warning lights must be of the type authorized by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.59#stat.169.59.4">169.59, subdivision 4</a>, unless otherwise permitted or required in this chapter.</p>
          <p>(c) A stop lamp or signal lamp is prohibited from projecting a glaring or dazzling light, except for:</p>
          <p>(1) strobe lamps as provided under subdivision 8 or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.59#stat.169.59.4">169.59, subdivision 4</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) a school bus equipped with a supplemental warning system under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4503">169.4503</a>, subdivision 31.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Blue light.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraphs (b) to (d), blue lights are prohibited on all vehicles except road maintenance equipment and snow removal equipment operated by or under contract to the state or a political subdivision thereof.</p>
          <p>(b) Authorized emergency vehicles may display flashing blue lights to the rear of the vehicle as a warning signal in combination with other lights permitted or required by this chapter. In addition, authorized emergency vehicles may display, mounted on the passenger side only, flashing blue lights to the front of the vehicle as a warning signal in combination with other lights permitted or required by this chapter.</p>
          <p>(c) A motorcycle may display a blue light of up to one-inch diameter as part of the motorcycle's rear brake light.</p>
          <p>(d) A motor vehicle may display a blue light of up to one-inch diameter as part of the vehicle's rear brake light if:</p>
          <p>(1) the vehicle is a collector vehicle, as described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.10">168.10</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) the vehicle is eligible to display a collector plate under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.10">168.10</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">White light.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) It is unlawful to project a white light at the rear of a vehicle while traveling on any street or highway, except:</p>
          <p>(1) for a vehicle moving in reverse;</p>
          <p>(2) for a school bus equipped with a supplemental warning system under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.4503#stat.169.4503.31">169.4503, subdivision 31</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) for a strobe lamp as provided under subdivision 8;</p>
          <p>(4) as required for license plate illumination under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.50#stat.169.50.2">169.50, subdivision 2</a>;</p>
          <p>(5) as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.59#stat.169.59.4">169.59, subdivision 4</a>; and</p>
          <p>(6) as otherwise provided in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) A lighting device mounted on top of a vehicle engaged in deliveries to residences may project a white light to the rear if the sign projects one or more additional colors to the rear.</p>
          <p>(c) An authorized emergency vehicle may display an oscillating, alternating, or rotating white light used in connection with an oscillating, alternating, or rotating red light when responding to emergency calls.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>MS 2010 [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168B.16">168B.16</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Flashing amber light.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any service vehicle may be equipped with a flashing amber lamp of a type approved by the commissioner of public safety.</p>
          <p>(b) A service vehicle shall not display the lighted lamp authorized under paragraph (a) when traveling upon the highway or at any other time except at the scene of a disabled vehicle or while engaged in snow removal or road maintenance.</p>
          <p>(c) A self-propelled implement of husbandry may display the lighted lamp authorized under paragraph (a) at any time.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/277/#laws.0.18.0">1991 c 277 s 18</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Strobe lamp.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, a vehicle may be equipped with a 360-degree flashing strobe lamp that emits a white light with a flash rate of 60 to 120 flashes a minute, and the lamp may be used as provided in this subdivision, if the vehicle is:</p>
          <p>(1) a school bus that is subject to and complies with the equipment requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.442#stat.169.442.1">169.442, subdivision 1</a>, or a Head Start bus. The lamp must operate from a separate switch containing an indicator lamp to show when the strobe lamp is in use; or</p>
          <p>(2) a road maintenance vehicle owned or under contract to the Department of Transportation or a road authority of a county, home rule or statutory city, or town, but the strobe lamp may only be operated while the vehicle is actually engaged in snow removal during daylight hours.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, a vehicle may be equipped with a 360-degree flashing strobe lamp that emits an amber light with a flash rate of 60 to 120 flashes a minute, and the lamp may be used as provided in this subdivision, if the vehicle is a rural mail carrier vehicle, provided that the strobe lamp is mounted at the highest practicable point on the vehicle. The strobe lamp may only be operated while the vehicle is actually engaged during daylight hours in the delivery of mail to residents on a rural mail route.</p>
          <p>(c) A strobe lamp authorized by this subdivision must be of a double flash type certified to the commissioner of public safety by the manufacturer as being weatherproof and having an effective light output that meets or exceeds the most recent version of SAE International standard J845, Class 2, or a subsequent standard.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Warning lamp on vehicles collecting solid waste or recycling.</span></h2>
          <p>A solid waste vehicle or recycling vehicle may be equipped with a single amber warning lamp that meets the most current SAE International standard for authorized maintenance and service vehicles, Class 2. The lamp may be operated only when the collection vehicle is in the process of collecting solid waste or recycling and is either:</p>
          <p>(1) stopped at an establishment where solid waste or recycling is to be collected; or</p>
          <p>(2) traveling at a speed that is at least ten miles per hour below the posted speed limit and moving between establishments where solid waste or recycling is to be collected.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.64.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Cover for lamp or reflector.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), it is prohibited for any person to:</p>
          <p>(1) equip a motor vehicle with any equipment or material that covers a headlamp, tail lamp, or reflector; or</p>
          <p>(2) operate a motor vehicle fitted with or otherwise having equipment or material that covers a headlamp, tail lamp, or reflector.</p>
          <p>(b) Paragraph (a) does not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) any manufacturer's original equipment or material;</p>
          <p>(2) any equipment or material that is clear and colorless; or</p>
          <p>(3) the covering for auxiliary lights required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.56">169.56</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.64.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-250</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.100.0">1937 c 464 s 100</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.29.0">1947 c 428 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/53/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 53 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.19.0">1971 c 491 s 19</a>,20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/104/#laws.0.2.0">1976 c 104 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/35/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 35 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/293/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 293 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/316/#laws.0.2.0">2002 c 316 s 2</a>;
