      <div class="section" id="stat.169.65">
        <h1 class="shn">169.65 SPECIFICATIONS FOR LIGHTING AND OTHER DEVICES.</h1>
        <p>(a) The commissioner of public safety is hereby authorized and required to adopt and enforce standard specifications as to the amount, color and direction of light to be emitted or reflected by lighting devices and as to the general construction and mounting on the vehicle for compliance with the requirements and limitations of this chapter.</p>
        <p>(b) No person shall have for sale, sell, or offer for sale for use upon or as a part of the equipment of a vehicle, trailer or semitrailer, or use upon any such vehicle, any headlamp, auxiliary driving lamp, rear lamp, signal lamp, spot lamp, clearance lamp, marker lamp or reflector, or parts of any of the foregoing, unless of a type which has been submitted to and approved by the commissioner of public safety.</p>
        <p>(c) No person shall have for sale, sell, or offer for sale for use upon or as a part of the equipment of a vehicle, trailer or semitrailer, or bicycle, or use upon any such vehicle, any lamp or device mentioned in this section, which has been approved by the commissioner of public safety unless such lamp or device bears thereon the trademark or name and model designation all permanently marked under which it is approved so as to be legible when installed.</p>
        <p>(d) No person shall use upon any vehicle, trailer or semitrailer or bicycle any lamps mentioned in this section unless such lamps are equipped with bulbs of a type approved by the commissioner of public safety, having a rated candle power, and are mounted and adjusted as to focus and aim in accordance with instructions of the commissioner of public safety.</p>
        <p>(e) The commissioner of public safety is hereby authorized to approve or disapprove lighting devices.</p>
        <p>(f) The commissioner of public safety is hereby required to approve or disapprove any lighting device, of a type on which approval is specifically required in this chapter, within a reasonable time after such device has been submitted.</p>
        <p>(g) The commissioner of public safety is further authorized to set up a procedure which shall be followed when any device is submitted for approval.</p>
        <p>(h) The commissioner of public safety is authorized to set and collect a reasonable fee for the testing and approval of all types of devices upon which approval is required in this chapter. Such fee may be sufficient in amount to reimburse the Department of Public Safety for all costs connected with such test and approval.</p>
        <p>(i) The commissioner of public safety, upon approving any such lamp or device, shall issue to the applicant a certificate of approval, together with any instructions determined by the commissioner of public safety.</p>
        <p>(j) The commissioner of public safety shall publish lists of all lamps and devices by name and type which have been approved by the commissioner of public safety, together with instructions as to the permissible candlepower rating of the bulbs which the commissioner of public safety has determined for use therein and such other instructions as to adjustment as the commissioner of public safety may deem necessary. No person shall sell for use or use on any vehicle any reconverted lamp or any device redesigned for a use other than for which it was originally approved unless authorized by the commissioner of public safety.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.65.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-251</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-252</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-253</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.101.0">1937 c 464 s 101</a>-103; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/207/#laws.0.6.0">1945 c 207 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.21.0">1971 c 491 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/494/#laws.0.4.0">1978 c 494 s 4</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.66">
        <h1 class="shn">169.66 HEARING ON SPECIFICATIONS.</h1>
        <p>(a) With reason to believe that an approved device which is being sold commercially does not comply with the requirements of this chapter, the commissioner of public safety may, after giving 30 days' previous notice to the person holding the certificate of approval for such device in this state, conduct a hearing upon the question of compliance of the approved device. After the hearing the commissioner of public safety shall determine whether the approved device meets the requirements of this chapter. If it does not meet the requirements of this chapter, the commissioner of public safety shall give notice to the person holding the certificate of approval for such device in this state.</p>
        <p>(b) If, at the expiration of 90 days after such notice, the person holding the certificate of approval for such device has failed to satisfy the commissioner of public safety that the approved device as thereafter to be sold meets the requirements of this chapter, the commissioner of public safety shall suspend or revoke the approval issued therefor until or unless such device is resubmitted to and retested by an authorized testing agency and is found to meet the requirements of this chapter, and may require that all such devices sold since the notification following the hearing be replaced with devices that do comply with the requirements of this chapter. The commissioner of public safety may at the time of the retest purchase in the open market and submit to the testing agency one or more sets of such approved devices, and if such device upon such retest fails to meet the requirements of this chapter, the commissioner of public safety may refuse to renew the certificate of approval of such device.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.66.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-254</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.104.0">1937 c 464 s 104</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.22.0">1971 c 491 s 22</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.67">
        <h1 class="shn">169.67 BRAKES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.67.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Motor vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>Every motor vehicle, other than a motorcycle, when operated upon a highway, shall be equipped with brakes adequate to control the movement of and to stop and hold such vehicle, including two separate means of applying the brakes, each of which means shall be effective to apply the brakes to at least two wheels. If these two separate means of applying the brakes are connected in any way, they shall be so constructed that failure of any one part of the operating mechanism shall not leave the motor vehicle without brakes on at least two wheels.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.67.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Motorcycle and bicycle.</span></h2>
          <p>Every motorcycle, and bicycle with motor attached, when operated upon a highway, shall be equipped with at least one brake, which may be operated by hand or foot.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.67.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Trailer, semitrailer.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) No trailer or semitrailer with a gross vehicle weight of 3,000 or more pounds, or a gross weight that exceeds the empty weight of the towing vehicle, may be drawn on a highway unless it is equipped with brakes that are adequate to control the movement of and to stop and hold the trailer or semitrailer. A surge brake on a trailer or semitrailer meets the requirement of this paragraph for brakes adequate to stop and hold the trailer or semitrailer.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) No trailer or semitrailer with a gross vehicle weight of more than 3,000 pounds may be drawn on a highway unless it is equipped with brakes that are so constructed that they are adequate to stop and hold the trailer or semitrailer whenever it becomes detached from the towing vehicle.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) Except as provided in paragraph (d), paragraph (a) does not apply to:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) a towed custom service vehicle drawn by a motor vehicle that is equipped with brakes that meet the standards of subdivision 5, provided that such a towed custom service vehicle that exceeds 30,000 pounds gross weight may not be drawn at a speed of more than 45 miles per hour;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) a motor vehicle drawn by another motor vehicle that is equipped with brakes that meet the standards of subdivision 5; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) a disabled vehicle while being towed to a place of repair.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) Vehicles described in paragraph (c), clause (2), may be operated without complying with paragraph (a) only if the trailer or semitrailer does not exceed the following gross weights:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) 3,000 pounds while being drawn by a vehicle registered as a passenger automobile, other than a pickup truck as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.26">168.002, subdivision 26</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) 12,000 pounds while being drawn by any other motor vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.67.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Service brakes on wheels; exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) All motor vehicles, trailers, and semitrailers manufactured after June 30, 1988, must be equipped with foot brakes on all wheels.</p>
          <p>(b) Paragraph (a) does not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) a mobile crane that is not operated at a speed of more than 45 miles per hour and is capable of stopping within the performance standards of subdivision 5;</p>
          <p>(2) a motorcycle;</p>
          <p>(3) a trailer or semitrailer with a gross weight of less than 3,000 pounds;</p>
          <p>(4) a swivel-type third wheel on a travel trailer; and</p>
          <p>(5) a temporary auxiliary axle attached to a motor vehicle during a period of vehicle weight restrictions for the purpose of relieving the weight on another axle, if the combined gross weight on the temporary axle and the axle being relieved does not exceed 18,000 pounds and the motor vehicle meets all brake requirements under this section.</p>
          <p>(c) Paragraph (a) does not require brakes on the front wheels of a vehicle having three or more axles and manufactured before July 1, 1988, if the brakes on the other wheels of the vehicle meet the standards of subdivision 5.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.67.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Performance standards.</span></h2>
          <p>Every motor vehicle or combination of vehicles, at all times and under all conditions of loading, upon application of the service (foot) brake, shall be capable of (1) developing a braking force that is not less than the percentage of its gross weight tabulated herein for its classification, (2) decelerating in a stop from not more than 20 miles per hour at not less than the feet per second per second tabulated herein for its classification, and (3) stopping from a speed of 20 miles per hour in not more than the distance tabulated herein for its classification, such distance to be measured from the point at which movement of the service brake pedal or control begins. Tests for deceleration and stopping distance shall be made on a substantially level (not to exceed plus or minus one percent grade), dry, smooth, hard surface that is free from loose material.</p>
          <table>

        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-255</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-256</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.105.0">1937 c 464 s 105</a>,106; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/1/38/#laws.0.2.0">Ex1937 c 38 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.19.0">1939 c 430 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/207/#laws.0.7.0">1945 c 207 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1953/0/423/#laws.0.1.0">1953 c 423 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1955/0/452/#laws.0.1.0">1955 c 452 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/277/#laws.0.1.0">1959 c 277 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/0/89/#laws.0.1.0">1961 c 89 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/747/#laws.0.1.0">1963 c 747 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/272/#laws.0.1.0">1967 c 272 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/205/#laws.0.1.0">1976 c 205 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/636/#laws.0.8.0">1988 c 636 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/342/#laws.0.17.0">1989 c 342 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/416/#laws.0.2.0">1990 c 416 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/581/#laws.0.12.0">1992 c 581 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/187/#laws.0.10.0">1993 c 187 s 10</a>-12; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/120/#laws.0.2.0">1995 c 120 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.2.44.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 2 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.39.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/382/#laws.0.40.0">2010 c 382 s 40</a></p>

      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.672"><b>169.672</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/549/#laws.0.34.0">1984 c 549 s 34</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.68">
        <h1 class="shn">169.68 HORN, SIREN.</h1>
        <p>(a) Every motor vehicle when operated upon a highway must be equipped with a horn in good working order and capable of emitting sound audible under normal conditions from a distance of not less than 200 feet. However, the horn or other warning device must not emit an unreasonably loud or harsh sound or a whistle. The driver of a motor vehicle shall, when reasonably necessary to insure safe operation, give audible warning with the horn, but shall not otherwise use the horn when upon a highway.</p>
        <p>(b) A vehicle must not be equipped with, and a person shall not use upon a vehicle, any siren, whistle, or bell, except as otherwise permitted in this section.</p>
        <p>(c) It is permissible, but not required, for any commercial vehicle to be equipped with a theft alarm signal device, so arranged that it cannot be used by the driver as an ordinary warning signal.</p>
        <p>(d) All authorized emergency vehicles must be equipped with a siren capable of emitting sound audible under normal conditions from a distance of not less than 500 feet and of a type conforming to the federal certification standards for sirens, as determined by the General Services Administration. However, the siren must not be used except when the vehicle is operated in response to an emergency call or in the immediate pursuit of an actual or suspected violator of the law, in which latter events the driver of the vehicle shall sound the siren when necessary to warn pedestrians and other drivers of the vehicle's approach.</p>
        <p>(e) It is permissible, but not required, for a bicycle to be equipped with a horn or bell designed to alert motor vehicles, other bicycles, and pedestrians of the bicycle's presence.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.68.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-257</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.107.0">1937 c 464 s 107</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.24.0">1971 c 491 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/426/#laws.0.26.0">2000 c 426 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/127/#laws.0.41.0">2013 c 127 s 41</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.684">
        <h1 class="shn">169.684 SEAT BELT; DECLARATION OF POLICY.</h1>
        <p>It is the policy of this state that enactment of a mandatory automobile seat belt usage law is intended to be compatible with support for federal safety standards requiring automatic crash protection and should not be used in any manner to rescind federal automatic crash protection system requirements for new vehicles.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.684.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/310/#laws.0.2.0">1986 c 310 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.685">
        <h1 class="shn">169.685 SEAT BELT; PASSENGER RESTRAINT SYSTEM FOR CHILDREN.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.685.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Requirement; exemptions.</span></h2>
          <p>After January 1, 1964, all new motor vehicles, not exempt from Minnesota license fees, other than a bus, school bus, motorcycle, motorized bicycle, farm tractor, road tractor, and truck, sold or offered for sale or registered in Minnesota shall be equipped to permit the installation of seat belts in the front seat thereof.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.685.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Required after registration.</span></h2>
          <p>Within 30 days after the registration of such motor vehicle, it shall be equipped with seat belts installed for use in the left front and right front seats thereof.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.685.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Standards.</span></h2>
          <p>The specifications and requirements for seat belts or seat belt assemblies shall conform with the minimum standards for seat belts or seat belt assemblies heretofore adopted by the Society of Automotive Engineers and in effect on January 1, 1963.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.685.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Booster seat" means a child passenger restraint system that meets applicable federal motor vehicle safety standards and is designed to provide belt-positioning that elevates a child to be properly seated with a safety belt.</p>
          <p>(c) "Child passenger restraint system" means a device that:</p>
          <p>(1) meets applicable federal motor vehicle safety standards of the United States Department of Transportation and complies with any other applicable federal regulations;</p>
          <p>(2) is designed to restrain, seat, or position children; and</p>
          <p>(3) is appropriate to the age of the child being restrained.</p>
          <p class="bl">Child passenger restraint system includes a booster seat.</p>
          <p>(d) "Properly restrained" means restrained or secured according to the instructions of both the motor vehicle manufacturer and the child passenger restraint system manufacturer.</p>
          <p>(e) "Secured with a safety belt" means restrained or secured by a seat belt that (1) meets applicable federal motor vehicle safety standards, and (2) is properly adjusted and fastened, including both the shoulder and lap straps when equipped in the vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.685.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Admissibility into evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), proof of the use or failure to use seat belts or a child passenger restraint system as described in subdivision 4a, or proof of the installation or failure of installation of seat belts or a child passenger restraint system as described in subdivision 4a is not admissible in evidence in any litigation involving personal injuries or property damage resulting from the use or operation of any motor vehicle.</p>
          <p>(b) Paragraph (a) does not affect the right of a person to bring an action for damages arising out of an incident that involves a defectively designed, manufactured, installed, or operating seat belt or child passenger restraint system. Paragraph (a) does not prohibit the introduction of evidence pertaining to the use of a seat belt or child passenger restraint system in an action described in this paragraph.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.685.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Child passenger restraint systems.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (c), every driver in this state who transports a child or children under the age of 18 years in a motor vehicle that is in motion or a part of traffic and is required under federal motor vehicle safety standards to be equipped with a safety belt or lower anchors and tethers for children in a passenger seating position must have the child or children secured as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) a child who is younger than two years of age must be properly restrained in a rear-facing child passenger restraint system with an internal harness, until the child reaches the weight or height limit of the child passenger restraint system;</p>
          <p>(2) a child who is at least two years of age and exceeds the rear-facing weight or height limit of the child passenger restraint system must be properly restrained in a forward-facing child passenger restraint system with an internal harness, until the child reaches the weight or height limit of the child passenger restraint system;</p>
          <p>(3) a child who is at least four years of age and exceeds the weight or height limit of the forward-facing child passenger restraint system must be properly restrained in a booster seat and secured with a safety belt;</p>
          <p>(4) a child who is at least nine years of age or exceeds the weight or height limit of the child passenger restraint system or the booster seat must be secured with a safety belt adjusted and fastened around the child's body to fit correctly. The safety belt fits correctly when the child sits all the way back against the vehicle seat, the child's knees bend over the edge of the vehicle seat, the lap strap fits snugly across the child's thighs and lower hips and not the child's abdomen, and the shoulder strap snugly crosses the center of the child's chest and not the child's neck;</p>
          <p>(5) a child who is younger than 13 years of age must be transported in the rear seat of a motor vehicle, when available, and must be properly restrained in a child passenger restraint system or booster seat or secured with a safety belt; and</p>
          <p>(6) a child who, because of age or weight, can be placed in more than one category under this paragraph must be placed in the more protective category, where clause (1) provides for the most protective and clause (5) provides for the least protective.</p>
          <p>(b) The driver of a motor vehicle transporting a child who is younger than six years of age or weighs less than 60 pounds must transport the child in a rear seat if:</p>
          <p>(1) the vehicle is equipped with a passenger side air bag supplemental restraint system;</p>
          <p>(2) the air bag system is activated; and</p>
          <p>(3) a rear seat is available.</p>
          <p>(c) When the number of children in the motor vehicle under 13 years of age exceeds the number of age- or size-appropriate child passenger restraint systems and safety belts available in the motor vehicle, the unrestrained children must be seated in a rear seat, if rear seats are available.</p>
          <p>(d) The weight and height limits of a child passenger restraint system under this subdivision are as established by the child passenger restraint system manufacturer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.685.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Violation; petty misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any motor vehicle operator who violates subdivision 4a is guilty of a petty misdemeanor and may be sentenced to pay a fine of not more than $50. The fine may be waived or the amount reduced if the motor vehicle operator produces evidence that within 14 days after the date of the violation a child passenger restraint system meeting federal motor vehicle safety standards was purchased or obtained for the exclusive use of the operator.</p>
          <p>(b) At the time of issuance of a citation under this subdivision, a peace officer may provide to the violator information on obtaining a free or low-cost child passenger restraint system.</p>
          <p>(c) The fines collected for violations of this subdivision must be deposited in the Minnesota child passenger restraint and education account.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.685.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) This section does not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) a person transporting a child in an emergency medical vehicle while in the performance of official duties and when the physical or medical needs of the child make the use of a child passenger restraint system unreasonable or when a child passenger restraint system is not available;</p>
          <p>(2) a peace officer transporting a child while in the performance of official duties and when a child passenger restraint system is not available, provided that a seat belt must be substituted;</p>
          <p>(3) a person while operating a motor vehicle for hire, including a taxi, airport limousine, and bus, but excluding a rented, leased, or borrowed motor vehicle; and</p>
          <p>(4) a person while operating a school bus that has a gross vehicle weight rating of greater than 10,000 pounds.</p>
          <p>(b) A child passenger restraint system is not required for a child who cannot, in the judgment of a licensed physician, be safely transported in a child passenger restraint system because of a medical condition, body size, or physical disability. A motor vehicle operator claiming exemption for a child under this paragraph must possess a typewritten statement from the physician stating that the child cannot be safely transported in a child passenger restraint system. The statement must give the name and birth date of the child, be dated within the previous six months, and be made on the physician's letterhead or contain the physician's name, address, and telephone number. A person charged with violating subdivision 5 may not be convicted if the person produces the physician's statement in court or in the office of the arresting officer.</p>
          <p>(c) A person offering a motor vehicle for rent or lease shall provide a child passenger restraint device to a customer renting or leasing the motor vehicle who requests the device. A reasonable rent or fee may be charged for use of the child passenger restraint device.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.685.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Appropriation; special account.</span></h2>
          <p>The Minnesota child passenger restraint and education account is created in the special revenue fund, consisting of fines collected under subdivision 5 and other money appropriated or donated. The money in the account is annually appropriated to the commissioner of public safety to be used to provide child passenger restraint systems to families in financial need, school districts and child care providers that provide for the transportation of pupils to and from school using type III vehicles or school buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 pounds or less, and to provide an educational program on the need for and proper use of child passenger restraint systems. Information on the commissioner's activities and expenditure of funds under this section must be available upon request.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.685.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/93/#laws.0.1.0">1963 c 93 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/227/#laws.0.2.0">1979 c 227 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/37/#laws.0.2.0">1981 c 37 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/56/#laws.0.1.0">1981 c 56 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/261/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 261 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/73/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 73 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/415/#laws.0.1.0">1988 c 415 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/74/#laws.0.1.0">1993 c 74 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/635/#laws.1.14.0">1994 c 635 art 1 s 14</a>,15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/106/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 106 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/82/#laws.0.1.0">2009 c 82 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/356/#laws.0.2.0">2010 c 356 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/287/#laws.4.23.0">2012 c 287 art 4 s 23</a>,24; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/255/#laws.0.18.0">2014 c 255 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/104/#laws.1.40.0">2024 c 104 art 1 s 40</a>-44</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.686">
        <h1 class="shn">169.686 SEAT BELT USE REQUIRED; PENALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.686.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Seat belt requirement.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.685">169.685</a>, a properly adjusted and fastened seat belt, including both the shoulder and lap belt when the vehicle is so equipped, shall be worn by the driver and passengers of a passenger vehicle, commercial motor vehicle, type III vehicle, and type III Head Start vehicle. Notwithstanding the equipment exemption in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.685#stat.169.685.1">169.685, subdivision 1</a>, this paragraph applies to the driver and passengers of an autocycle equipped with seat belts.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who is 15 years of age or older and who violates paragraph (a) is subject to a fine of $25. The driver of the vehicle in which a violation occurs is subject to a $25 fine for each violation of paragraph (a) by the driver or by a passenger under the age of 15, but the court may not impose more than one surcharge under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/357.021#stat.357.021.6">357.021, subdivision 6</a>, on the driver. The Department of Public Safety shall not record a violation of this subdivision on a person's driving record.</p>
          <p>(c) The driver of a bus is not subject to the fine under paragraph (b) for a violation of paragraph (a) by a passenger under the age of 15. This paragraph does not apply to (1) a school bus, including a type III vehicle; and (2) a Head Start bus, including a type III Head Start vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.686.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Passenger vehicle" means:</p>
          <p>(1) a passenger automobile defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.24">168.002, subdivision 24</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) a pickup truck;</p>
          <p>(3) a van;</p>
          <p>(4) a commuter van, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.126">168.126</a>; and</p>
          <p>(5) a recreational vehicle, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.27">168.002, subdivision 27</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) "Passenger vehicle" does not include a motorcycle, motorized bicycle, bus, school bus, a vehicle designed to operate exclusively on railroad tracks, a farm truck as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.8">168.002, subdivision 8</a>, or special mobile equipment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.31">168.002, subdivision 31</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) "Pickup truck" means a truck, regardless of manufacturer's nominal rated carrying capacity, that is commonly known as a pickup truck.</p>
          <p>(e) "Van" means a vehicle, regardless of the manufacturer's nominal rated carrying capacity, of a box-like design that (1) has no barrier or separation between the operator's area and the remainder of the cargo-carrying area, or (2) is designed to carry 15 or fewer passengers, including the driver.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.686.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Seat belt exemptions.</span></h2>
          <p>This section shall not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) a person driving a passenger vehicle in reverse;</p>
          <p>(2) a person riding in a vehicle in which all the seating positions equipped with safety belts are occupied by other persons in safety belts;</p>
          <p>(3) a person who is in possession of a written certificate from a licensed physician verifying that because of medical unfitness or physical disability the person is unable to wear a seat belt;</p>
          <p>(4) a person who is actually engaged in work that requires the person to alight from and reenter a motor vehicle at frequent intervals and who, while engaged in that work, does not drive or travel in that vehicle at a speed exceeding 25 miles per hour;</p>
          <p>(5) a rural mail carrier of the United States Postal Service or a newspaper delivery person while in the performance of duties;</p>
          <p>(6) a person driving or riding in a passenger vehicle manufactured before January 1, 1965; and</p>
          <p>(7) a person driving or riding in a pickup truck while engaged in normal farming work or activity.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.686.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Appropriation; special account.</span></h2>
          <p>The fines collected for a violation of subdivision 1 must be deposited in the state treasury and credited to a special account to be known as the emergency medical services relief account. Ninety percent of the money in the account shall be distributed to the eight regional emergency medical services systems designated by the director of the Office of Emergency Medical Services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144E.50">144E.50</a>, for personnel education and training, equipment and vehicle purchases, and operational expenses of emergency life support transportation services. The board of directors of each emergency medical services region shall establish criteria for funding. Ten percent of the money in the account shall be distributed to the commissioner of public safety for the expenses of traffic safety educational programs conducted by State Patrol troopers.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.686.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/310/#laws.0.3.0">1986 c 310 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/648/#laws.0.1.0">1988 c 648 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/288/#laws.0.1.0">1989 c 288 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/204/#laws.0.1.0">1991 c 204 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/26/#laws.0.9.0">1993 c 26 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/600/#laws.0.5.0">1994 c 600 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/324/#laws.0.4.0">1996 c 324 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/199/#laws.0.14.0">1997 c 199 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/92/#laws.0.1.0">2003 c 92 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/82/#laws.0.2.0">2009 c 82 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/165/#laws.0.2.0">2009 c 165 s 2</a>-4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/168/#laws.0.6.0">2009 c 168 s 6</a>,7,14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/76/#laws.1.80.0">2011 c 76 art 1 s 80</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/114/#laws.0.3.0">2016 c 114 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/169/#laws.0.2.0">2016 c 169 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/122/#laws.1.24.0">2024 c 122 art 1 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.63.22.0">2024 c 127 art 63 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.69">
        <h1 class="shn">169.69 MUFFLER.</h1>
        <p>Every motor vehicle shall at all times be equipped with a muffler in good working order which blends the exhaust noise into the overall vehicle noise and is in constant operation to prevent excessive or unusual noise, and no person shall use a muffler cutout, bypass, or similar device upon a motor vehicle on a street or highway. The exhaust system shall not emit or produce a sharp popping or crackling sound. Every motor vehicle shall at all times be equipped with such parts and equipment so arranged and kept in such state of repair as to prevent carbon monoxide gas from entering the interior of the vehicle.</p>
        <p>No person shall have for sale, sell or offer for sale or use on any motor vehicle any muffler that fails to comply with the specifications as required by the commissioner of public safety.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.69.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-258</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.108.0">1937 c 464 s 108</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.20.0">1939 c 430 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1953/0/306/#laws.0.1.0">1953 c 306 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.25.0">1971 c 491 s 25</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.691"><b>169.691</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/500/#laws.0.2.0">1974 c 500 s 2</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.692"><b>169.692</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/500/#laws.0.2.0">1974 c 500 s 2</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.693">
        <h1 class="shn">169.693 MOTOR VEHICLE NOISE LIMITS.</h1>
        <p>It is unlawful to operate a motor vehicle in violation of motor vehicle noise rules adopted by the Pollution Control Agency.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.693.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/500/#laws.0.1.0">1974 c 500 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.70">
        <h1 class="shn">169.70 REAR VIEW MIRROR.</h1>
        <p>Every motor vehicle constructed, loaded, or connected with another vehicle that obstructs the driver's view to the rear from the driver's position must be equipped with a mirror or other technology that reflects or displays to the driver a view of the highway for a distance of at least 200 feet to the rear of the vehicle.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.70.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-259</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.109.0">1937 c 464 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.5.31.0">2023 c 68 art 5 s 31</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.71">
        <h1 class="shn">169.71 WINDSHIELD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.71.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Prohibitions generally; exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person shall not drive or operate any motor vehicle with:</p>
          <p>(1) a windshield cracked or discolored to an extent to limit or obstruct proper vision;</p>
          <p>(2) any objects suspended between the driver and the windshield, other than:</p>
          <p>(i) sun visors;</p>
          <p>(ii) rearview mirrors;</p>
          <p>(iii) driver feedback and safety monitoring equipment when mounted immediately behind, slightly above, or slightly below the rearview mirror;</p>
          <p>(iv) global positioning systems or navigation systems when mounted or located near the bottommost portion of the windshield;</p>
          <p>(v) electronic toll collection devices; and</p>
          <p>(vi) an identifying device as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.58#stat.169.58.5">169.58, subdivision 5</a>, when the device is mounted or located near the bottommost portion of the windshield; or</p>
          <p>(3) any sign, poster, or other nontransparent material upon the front windshield, sidewings, or side or rear windows of the vehicle, other than a certificate or other paper required to be so displayed by law or authorized by the state director of the Division of Emergency Management or the commissioner of public safety.</p>
          <p>(b) Paragraph (a), clauses (2) and (3), do not apply to law enforcement vehicles.</p>
          <p>(c) Paragraph (a), clause (2), does not apply to authorized emergency vehicles.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.71.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Windshield wiper.</span></h2>
          <p>The windshield on every motor vehicle shall be equipped with a device for cleaning rain, snow or other moisture from the windshield, which device shall be so constructed as to be controlled or operated by the driver of the vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.71.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Defrosting requirement.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall drive any motor vehicle with the windshield or front side windows covered with steam or frost to such an extent as to prevent proper vision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.71.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Glazing material; prohibitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person must not drive or operate any motor vehicle required to be registered in the state of Minnesota upon any street or highway under the following conditions:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) when the windshield is composed of, covered by, or treated with any material which has the effect of making the windshield more reflective or in any other way reducing light transmittance through the windshield;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) when any window on the vehicle is composed of, covered by, or treated with any material that has a highly reflective or mirrored appearance;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) when any side window or rear window is composed of or treated with any material so as to obstruct or substantially reduce the driver's clear view through the window or has a light transmittance of less than 50 percent plus or minus three percent in the visible light range or a luminous reflectance of more than 20 percent plus or minus three percent; or</p>
          <p class="in">(4) when any material has been applied after August 1, 1985, to any motor vehicle window without an accompanying permanent marking which indicates the percent of transmittance and the percent of reflectance afforded by the material. The marking must be in a manner so as not to obscure vision and be readable when installed on the vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.71.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Glazing material; exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Subdivision 4 does not apply to glazing materials that:</p>
          <p>(1) have not been modified since the original installation, nor to original replacement windows and windshields, that were originally installed or replaced in conformity with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 205;</p>
          <p>(2) are required to satisfy prescription or medical needs, provided:</p>
          <p>(i) the vehicle's driver or a passenger possesses a prescription or a physician's statement of medical need;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) the prescription or statement specifically states the minimum percentage that light transmittance may be reduced to satisfy the prescription or medical needs of the patient; and</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) the prescription or statement contains an expiration date, which must be no more than two years after the date the prescription or statement was issued; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) are applied to:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) the rear windows of a pickup truck as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.26">168.002, subdivision 26</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) the rear windows or the side windows on either side behind the driver's seat of a van as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.40">168.002, subdivision 40</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) the side and rear windows of a vehicle used to transport human remains by a funeral establishment holding a license under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/149A.50">149A.50</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) the side and rear windows of a limousine as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.15">168.002, subdivision 15</a>; or</p>
          <p class="in">(v) the rear and side windows of a police vehicle.</p>
          <p>(b) For the purposes of paragraph (a), clause (2), a driver of a vehicle may rely on a prescription or physician's statement of medical need issued to a person not present in the vehicle if:</p>
          <p>(1) the prescription or physician's statement of medical need is issued to (i) the driver's parent, child, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, or spouse, or (ii) a person for whom the driver is a personal care attendant;</p>
          <p>(2) the prescription or physician's statement of medical need specifies the make, model, and license plate of one or two vehicles that will have tinted windows; and</p>
          <p>(3) the driver is in possession of the prescription or physician's statement of medical need.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.71.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Glazing material; prohibitions on sale.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) No person shall sell or offer for sale or use on any motor vehicle, windows or windshields that are composed of, covered by, or treated with material that fails to comply with the provisions of subdivision 4. No person shall apply or offer to apply, as part of a business transaction, material to motor vehicle windows or windshields that fails to comply with the provisions of subdivision 4.</p>
          <p>(b) Violation of this subdivision is a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(c) This subdivision does not apply to sale or offers for sale of a motor vehicle containing windows or windshields composed of, covered by, or treated with material that fails to comply with the provisions of subdivision 4.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.71.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-260</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.110.0">1937 c 464 s 110</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.21.0">1939 c 430 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.30.0">1947 c 428 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1953/0/745/#laws.0.4.0">1953 c 745 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/174/#laws.0.1.0">1959 c 174 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/521/#laws.0.11.0">1959 c 521 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/0/34/#laws.0.1.0">1961 c 34 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.26.0">1971 c 491 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/428/#laws.0.5.0">1974 c 428 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/234/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 234 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/71/#laws.0.2.0">1987 c 71 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/636/#laws.0.10.0">1988 c 636 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/301/#laws.0.7.0">1991 c 301 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/26/#laws.0.10.0">1993 c 26 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/215/#laws.0.44.0">1997 c 215 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.8.2.0">2005 c 136 art 8 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/186/#laws.0.1.0">2008 c 186 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/235/#laws.0.2.0">2008 c 235 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/59/#laws.5.5.0">2009 c 59 art 5 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/304/#laws.0.1.0">2010 c 304 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/351/#laws.0.32.0">2010 c 351 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.59.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 59</a>-61</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.72">
        <h1 class="shn">169.72 TIRE SURFACE; METAL STUDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.72.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Solid rubber, metal, and studded tires; exceptions; permits.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Every solid rubber tire on a vehicle must have rubber on its entire traction surface at least one inch thick above the edge of the flange of the entire periphery.</p>
          <p>(b) No person shall operate or move on any highway any motor vehicle, trailer, or semitrailer, having any metal tire in contact with the roadway, except in case of emergency.</p>
          <p>(c) Except as provided in this section, no tire on a vehicle moved on a highway shall have on its periphery any block, stud, flange, cleat, or spike or any other protuberances of any material other than rubber which projects beyond the tread of the traction surface of the tire.</p>
          <p>(d) It is permissible to use any of the following on highways:</p>
          <p>(1) implements of husbandry with tires having protuberances which will not injure the highway;</p>
          <p>(2) tire chains of reasonable proportions upon any vehicle when required for safety because of snow, ice, or other conditions tending to cause a vehicle to skid; and</p>
          <p>(3) tires on a bicycle as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.222#stat.169.222.6">169.222, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
          <p>(e) The commissioner and local authorities in their respective jurisdictions may, in their discretion, issue special permits authorizing the operation upon a highway of traction engines or tractors having movable tracks with transverse corrugations upon the periphery of such movable tracks or farm tractors or other farm machinery, the operation of which upon a highway would otherwise be prohibited under this chapter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.72.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/378/#laws.0.3.0">1973 c 378 s 3</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.72.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/310/#laws.0.1.0">1996 c 310 s 1</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.72.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Occasional use of studded tires by nonresidents.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding the provisions of subdivision 1, a person, operating a motor vehicle properly licensed and registered in another state or province of a foreign country which authorizes the use of tires with metal studs or wire embedded tires on its highways, may operate the motor vehicle with tires having metal type studs or with tires having wire embedded therein on the highways of this state while occasionally within the state, and such use while occasionally within the state is not unlawful; provided that, the metal type studs shall not exceed 5/16 of an inch in diameter inclusive of the stud casing with an average protrusion beyond the tread surface of not more than 7/64 of an inch, and the number of studs in a tire shall not exceed two percent of the total net contact area. Use of a vehicle in this state on more than 30 days in any consecutive six-month period is not occasionally. Except, a person whose regular place of employment is within the state or who is a student at an educational institution located within the state, shall not operate a vehicle, regardless of its place of registration, upon any highway within the state if such vehicle is equipped with tires which would be unauthorized were the vehicle registered in this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.72.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Rural postal carrier.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A rural mail carrier of the United States Postal Service may apply to the commissioner for a permit to operate a rural mail delivery vehicle with tires having metal studs. An applicant must submit with the application for the permit (1) verification that the applicant is employed as a United States postal carrier, (2) a map showing the applicant's mail delivery route, and (3) identification of the vehicle the applicant uses on that mail delivery route.</p>
          <p>(b) If the commissioner determines that (1) the applicant is employed as a United States postal carrier, and (2) less than 25 percent of the total mileage on the applicant's mail delivery route is paved, the commissioner may issue the permit. A permit under this subdivision is valid beginning November 1 of a calendar year and expires on April 15 of the following calendar year.</p>
          <p>(c) A permit under this subdivision authorizes the permit holder to operate a motor vehicle equipped with tires having metal studs that meet the limitations in subdivision 4, while (1) traveling between the permit holder's residence and a mail pickup station, and (2) delivering United States mail on the permit holder's delivery route as shown in the map accompanying the permit application. The permit is valid only for the vehicle identified in the permit.</p>
          <p>(d) The commissioner may amend a permit under this subdivision when (1) the permit holder submits evidence of a change in the permit holder's mail delivery route, or (2) the permit holder changes vehicles used in the route.</p>
          <p>(e) The commissioner may revoke a permit when the commissioner determines that (1) the vehicle named in the permit is or has been operated in violation of this subdivision or the terms of the permit, or (2) the commissioner determines that more than 25 percent of the total mileage of the permit holder's mail delivery route is paved.</p>
          <p>(f) Operation of a motor vehicle identified in a permit in violation of this subdivision or the terms of a permit issued under this subdivision is a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(g) A permit holder under this subdivision must remove tires having metal studs from the vehicle identified in the permit (1) by 12:01 a.m. on April 16 of each year, and (2) whenever the permit holder transfers ownership of the vehicle or ceases employment as a United States postal carrier.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.72.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-261</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.111.0">1937 c 464 s 111</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1965/0/168/#laws.0.1.0">1965 c 168 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/13/#laws.0.1.0">1967 c 13 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/245/#laws.0.1.0">1969 c 245 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/43/#laws.0.1.0">Ex1971 c 43 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/378/#laws.0.1.0">1973 c 378 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/389/#laws.0.1.0">1974 c 389 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/166/#laws.0.7.0">1976 c 166 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/187/#laws.0.13.0">1993 c 187 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/486/#laws.0.1.0">1994 c 486 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/287/#laws.3.34.0">2012 c 287 art 3 s 34</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.721">
        <h1 class="shn">169.721 UNSAFE TIRES; DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.721.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.721">169.721</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.727">169.727</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.721.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Passenger automobile.</span></h2>
          <p>"Passenger automobile" means any motor vehicle designed and used for the carrying of not more than nine persons, excluding motorcycles and motor scooters, but including within its meaning station wagons or other highway use motor vehicles using passenger automobile type tires.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.721.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of public safety.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.721.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/35/#laws.0.1.0">1976 c 35 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.722">
        <h1 class="shn">169.722 RULES FOR TIRE SAFETY.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner shall promulgate rules pursuant to chapter 14 providing for the safe operating conditions of tires for use on passenger automobiles. The rules shall be so promulgated that a law enforcement officer may determine whether or not a tire is in compliance by visual inspection or by the use of simple measuring gauges. The rules shall be based on and include effects of tread wear and depth of tread, and shall incorporate all of the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.723">169.723</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.722.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/35/#laws.0.2.0">1976 c 35 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.130.0">1982 c 424 s 130</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.723">
        <h1 class="shn">169.723 TIRES CONSIDERED UNSAFE.</h1>
        <p>A tire shall be considered unsafe if it has:</p>
        <p>(1) any part of the ply or cord exposed; or</p>
        <p>(2) any bump, bulge or separation; or</p>
        <p>(3) a tread design depth of less than 2/32 (1/16) of an inch measured in the tread groove nearest the center of the tire at three locations equally spaced around the circumference of the tire, exclusive of tie bars or for those tires with tread wear indicators; or</p>
        <p>(4) been worn to the level of the tread wear indicators in any two tread grooves at three locations; or</p>
        <p>(5) a marking "not for highway use," or "for racing purposes only," or "unsafe for highway use;" or</p>
        <p>(6) tread or sidewall cracks, cuts or snags deep enough to expose the body cords; or</p>
        <p>(7) been regrooved or recut below the original tread design depth, except special taxicab tires which have extra undertread rubber and are identified as such.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.723.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/35/#laws.0.3.0">1976 c 35 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.724">
        <h1 class="shn">169.724 PROHIBITION; OPERATING AUTOMOBILE WITH UNSAFE TIRES.</h1>
        <p>No person shall drive, move or cause to be driven or moved any passenger automobile upon the highways of this state, unless such passenger automobile is equipped with tires in safe operating condition in accordance with rules promulgated by the commissioner.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.724.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/35/#laws.0.4.0">1976 c 35 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.725"><b>169.725</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/255/#laws.0.21.0">2014 c 255 s 21</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.726">
        <h1 class="shn">169.726 AUTOMOBILE SALE PROHIBITED UNLESS TIRES ARE SAFE.</h1>
        <p>No person or organization shall sell or offer for sale, other than to a motor vehicle dealer, any passenger automobile for use on the public highways of this state, unless the passenger automobile is equipped with tires that are in compliance with the rules promulgated by the commissioner under authority of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.722">169.722</a>. If the tires are not in compliance with the rules, the person or organization selling or offering to sell the passenger automobile shall cause, prior to sale, the tires to be removed from the vehicle and shall equip the vehicle with tires that are in compliance with the rules; unless the vehicle is towed or hauled away. No person, firm, corporation or organization shall sell or offer for sale, other than to a tire dealer, tires for highway use not in compliance with these rules.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.726.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/35/#laws.0.6.0">1976 c 35 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.727">
        <h1 class="shn">169.727 UNSAFE TIRES; MISDEMEANOR.</h1>
        <p>Any person who violates the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.721">169.721</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.727">169.727</a> or any rule promulgated pursuant thereto is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.727.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/35/#laws.0.7.0">1976 c 35 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.73">
        <h1 class="shn">169.73 BUMPERS, SAFEGUARDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.73.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, "private passenger vehicle" means a four-wheeled passenger automobile as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.24">168.002, subdivision 24</a>; a van as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.40">168.002, subdivision 40</a>; a pickup truck as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.26">168.002, subdivision 26</a>; and a jeep-type automobile or other multipurpose vehicle. "Private passenger vehicle" does not include a collector vehicle or collector military vehicle as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.10">168.10</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) "Suspension system" includes both the front and rear wheels and tires of a vehicle as specified in subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.73.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Bumper requirement.</span></h2>
          <p>All private passenger vehicles shall be equipped with front and rear bumpers, except that pickup trucks and vans shall be equipped with front bumpers and with either rear bumpers or reflectors.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.73.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>MS 1978 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/498/#laws.0.7.0">1980 c 498 s 7</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.73.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Bumper restrictions.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall operate a private passenger vehicle that: (a) was originally equipped with bumpers as standard equipment, unless the vehicle is equipped with bumpers equal to the original equipment; or (b) has a suspension system or body so modified that the height of the vehicle or any bumpers varies more than six inches from the original manufactured height for the vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.73.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>MS 1978 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/498/#laws.0.7.0">1980 c 498 s 7</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.73.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Maximum bumper height.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding the restrictions contained in subdivision 3, bumpers required under this section shall not exceed a height of (1) 20 inches on any passenger automobile or station wagon or (2) 25 inches on any four-wheel drive multipurpose type vehicle, van as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.40">168.002, subdivision 40</a>, or pickup truck as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.26">168.002, subdivision 26</a>, when the vehicle is being operated on a public highway. The height of the bumper shall be determined by measuring from the bottom of the bumper, excluding any vertical bumper attachments, to the ground. A vehicle which has an original bumper which does not exceed a height of 30 inches may be modified by attaching a full width bumper to the regular bumper to meet the height requirement. The attached bumper must be at least 4.5 inches in vertical height, be centered on the vehicle's centerline, extend at least ten inches on either side of the frame, and be attached to the frame in at least four places with angle braces at no less than 45 degrees so that it effectively transfers impact to an extent equal to or greater than the original bumper.</p>
          <p>(b) Competent evidence that a vehicle was originally manufactured with bumpers higher than prescribed in this subdivision shall be an affirmative defense in any action under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.73.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Rear-end protection for other vehicles.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Vehicles other than private passenger vehicles, collector vehicles, collector military vehicles, and other vehicles specifically exempted by law from such requirements must meet the rear-end protection requirements of federal motor carrier regulations, Code of Federal Regulations, title 49, section 393.86.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding contrary regulations cited in paragraph (a), a truck-tractor and semitrailer combination with a semitrailer length longer than 50 feet whose frame or body extends more than 36 inches beyond the rear of its rearmost axle must not be operated on the highways of this state unless equipped with a bumper or underride guard on the extreme rear of the frame or body. The bumper or underride guard must:</p>
          <p>(1) provide a continuous horizontal beam having a maximum ground clearance of 22 inches, as measured with the vehicle empty and on level ground; and</p>
          <p>(2) extend to within four inches of the lateral extremities of the semitrailer on both left and right sides.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.73.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>MS 1978 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/498/#laws.0.7.0">1980 c 498 s 7</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.73.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who violates this section is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.73.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-262</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.112.0">1937 c 464 s 112</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.22.0">1939 c 430 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1955/0/647/#laws.0.1.0">1955 c 647 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/203/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 203 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/498/#laws.0.5.0">1980 c 498 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/199/#laws.0.2.0">1981 c 199 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/170/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 170 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/549/#laws.0.29.0">1984 c 549 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/336/#laws.0.6.0">1986 c 336 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/204/#laws.0.4.0">1989 c 204 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/333/#laws.0.15.0">1991 c 333 s 15</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.733">
        <h1 class="shn">169.733 WHEEL FLAPS ON TRUCK AND TRAILER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.733.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Vehicles generally.</span></h2>
          <p>Every truck, truck-tractor, trailer, semitrailer, pole trailer, and rear-end dump truck, excepting rear-end dump farm trucks, must be provided with wheel flaps or other suitable protection above and behind the rearmost wheels of the vehicle or combination of vehicles to prevent, as far as practicable, the wheels from throwing dirt, water, or other materials on the windshields of following vehicles. The flaps or protectors must be at least as wide as the tires they are protecting and have a ground clearance of not more than nine inches from the ground when the vehicle is empty.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.733.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Vehicle with conveyor belt.</span></h2>
          <p>For a dump truck or truck with a rigid box fastened to its frame and having a conveyor belt or chain in the bottom of the vehicle that moves the cargo to the rear end of the vehicle, the flaps must be mounted as far to the rear of the vehicle as practicable and have a ground clearance of not more than 18 inches when the vehicle is loaded.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.733.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Bottom-dump vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to meeting the requirements of subdivision 1, a bottom-dump cargo vehicle transporting sand, gravel, aggregate, dirt, lime rock, silica, or similar material must be equipped with a center flap between the wheel flaps, which must have a ground clearance of six inches or less when the vehicle is fully loaded.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.733.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Alternative requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>If the motor vehicle is so designed and constructed that the above requirements are accomplished by means of body construction or other means of enclosure, then no protectors or flaps are required.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.733.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Extended flaps.</span></h2>
          <p>If the rear wheels are not covered at the top by fenders, body or other parts of the vehicle, the flap or other protective means must be extended at least to a point directly above the center of the rearmost axle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.733.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/1/#laws.4.35.0">1Sp2005 c 1 art 4 s 35</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.733.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/640/#laws.0.1.0">1951 c 640 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1953/0/619/#laws.0.1.0">1953 c 619 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/136/#laws.0.1.0">1976 c 136 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/498/#laws.0.1.0">1978 c 498 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/548/#laws.0.1.0">1990 c 548 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/372/#laws.1.7.0">1998 c 372 art 1 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/1/#laws.4.35.0">1Sp2005 c 1 art 4 s 35</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.734">
        <h1 class="shn">169.734 AUTOMOBILE FENDERS.</h1>
        <p>Every passenger automobile shall have fenders, or other devices, that are designed to prevent, as far as practicable, water, dirt, or other material being thrown up and to the rear by the wheels of the vehicle.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.734.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/68/#laws.0.2.0">1975 c 68 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.74">
        <h1 class="shn">169.74 SAFETY GLASS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.74.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Required.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall sell any new motor vehicle, nor shall any new motor vehicle be registered thereafter unless the vehicle is equipped with safety glass wherever glass is used in doors, windows, and windshields.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.74.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Safety glass" means any product composed of glass, or other material, as may be approved by the commissioner of public safety, as safety glass.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.74.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Replacement.</span></h2>
          <p>All glass replacement in doors, windows, and windshields or partitions of motor vehicles shall be made with materials meeting the requirements of this chapter for safety glass if glass is used therefor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.74.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Other material prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>No glazing material other than of a type meeting the requirements of this chapter shall be sold, offered for sale, offered for use, or used for installation in doors, windows or windshields of motor vehicles or of passenger-carrying trailers or semitrailers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.74.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Frostshield.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in this section shall be construed to include frostshields.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.74.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-263</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.113.0">1937 c 464 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.31.0">1947 c 428 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.27.0">1971 c 491 s 27</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.743"><b>169.743</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/255/#laws.0.21.0">2014 c 255 s 21</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.75">
        <h1 class="shn">169.75 FLARES, FLAGS, OR REFLECTORS REQUIRED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.75.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Number required.</span></h2>
