      <div class="section" id="stat.169.826">
        <h1 class="shn">169.826 GROSS WEIGHT SEASONAL INCREASES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.826.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Winter increase amounts.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The limitations provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a> are increased by ten percent between the dates set by the commissioner for each zone established by the commissioner based on a freezing index model each winter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.826.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Harvest season increase amount; permit.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The limitations provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a> are increased by ten percent from the beginning of harvest to November 30 each year for the movement of sugar beets, carrots, and potatoes from the field of harvest to the point of the first unloading. Transfer of the product from a farm vehicle or small farm trailer, within the meaning of chapter 168, to another vehicle is not considered to be the first unloading. A permit issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.86#stat.169.86.1">169.86, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), is required. The commissioner shall not issue permits under this subdivision if to do so will result in a loss of federal highway funding to the state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.826.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/64/#laws.0.57.0">2009 c 64 s 57</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.826.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duration.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The duration of a ten percent increase in load limits is subject to limitation by order of the commissioner, subject to implementation of springtime load restrictions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.826.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Excess weight permit.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">When the ten percent increase is in effect, a permit is required for a motor vehicle, trailer, or semitrailer combination that has a gross weight in excess of 80,000 pounds, an axle group weight in excess of that prescribed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.824">169.824</a>, or a single axle weight in excess of 20,000 pounds and which travels on interstate routes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.826.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Weight limits set by other law.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">In cases where gross weights in an amount less than that set forth in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a> are fixed, limited, or restricted on a highway or bridge by or under another section of this chapter, the lesser gross weight as fixed, limited, or restricted may not be exceeded and must control instead of the gross weights set forth in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.826.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/64/#laws.0.57.0">2009 c 64 s 57</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.826.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/320/#laws.1.20.0">2010 c 320 art 1 s 20</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.826.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Expiration date.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon request of the permit applicant, the expiration date for a permit issued under this section must be the same as the expiration date of the permitted vehicle's registration.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.826.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/321/#laws.0.4.0">1981 c 321 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.42.0">1982 c 424 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/617/#laws.0.11.0">1982 c 617 s 11</a>-13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/198/#laws.0.9.0">1983 c 198 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/398/#laws.13.6.0">1986 c 398 art 13 s 6</a>-9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/452/#laws.0.20.0">1986 c 452 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/1/3/#laws.4.13.0">1Sp1986 c 3 art 4 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/112/#laws.0.4.0">1991 c 112 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/333/#laws.0.18.0">1991 c 333 s 18</a>,19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/578/#laws.0.7.0">1992 c 578 s 7</a>-10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/635/#laws.1.16.0">1994 c 635 art 1 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/372/#laws.1.8.0">1998 c 372 art 1 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/433/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 433 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/156/#laws.0.1.0">2001 c 156 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/213/#laws.0.10.0">2001 c 213 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/364/#laws.0.13.0">2002 c 364 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/19/#laws.2.34.0">1Sp2003 c 19 art 2 s 34</a>,35; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.47.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/320/#laws.2.2.0">2010 c 320 art 2 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/312/#laws.11.10.0">2014 c 312 art 11 s 10</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.8261">
        <h1 class="shn">169.8261 FOREST PRODUCTS SPECIAL PERMIT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.8261.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> For purposes of this section, "raw or unfinished forest products" include wood chips, paper, pulp, oriented strand board, laminated strand lumber, hardboard, treated lumber, untreated lumber, or barrel staves.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.8261.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Six-axle and over-width vehicle permit.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A road authority may issue an annual permit authorizing a vehicle or combination of vehicles with a total of six or more axles to haul raw or unfinished forest products by the most direct route to the nearest paved highway on any highway with gross weights permitted under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829 </a>and be operated with:</p>
          <p>(1) a gross vehicle weight of up to:</p>
          <p>(i) 90,000 pounds; and</p>
          <p>(ii) 99,000 pounds during the period set by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826">169.826</a>, subdivision 1; and</p>
          <p>(2) a total outside width of the vehicle or the load that does not exceed 114 inches.</p>
          <p>(b) In addition to the conditions in subdivision 2, a vehicle or combination of vehicles that is operated with a permit under this subdivision and transporting a load that exceeds 108 inches must:</p>
          <p>(1) display red or orange flags, 18 inches square, as markers at the front and rear and on both sides of the load; and</p>
          <p>(2) not be operated on any road in a metropolitan county, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/473.121">473.121</a>, subdivision 4.</p>
          <p>(c) A vehicle or combination of vehicles with a permit under this subdivision may only be operated on an interstate highway:</p>
          <p>(1) as provided under United States Code, title 23, section 127(q), for operation on the specified segment of marked Interstate Highway 35; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the gross vehicle weight does not exceed 80,000 pounds.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.8261.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Conditions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) A vehicle or combination of vehicles operated under this section must:</p>
          <p>(1) comply with seasonal load restrictions in effect between the dates set by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87#stat.169.87.2">169.87, subdivision 2</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) comply with bridge load limits posted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.84">169.84</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) be equipped and operated with six or more axles and brakes on all wheels;</p>
          <p>(4) be operated under a permit issued by each road authority having jurisdiction over a road on which the vehicle is operated, if required by the road authority;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) obey all road and bridge postings, including those pertaining to lane or roadway width; and</p>
          <p class="in">(6) not exceed 20,000 pounds gross weight on any single axle.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) A vehicle operated under this section may exceed the legal axle weight limits listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.824">169.824</a> by not more than 12.5 percent; except that, the weight limits may be exceeded by not more than 23.75 percent during the time when seasonal increases are authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826#stat.169.826.1">169.826, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.8261.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Expiration date.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon request of the permit applicant, the expiration date for a permit issued under this section must be the same as the expiration date of the permitted vehicle's registration.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.8261.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/295/#laws.1.10.0">2004 c 295 art 1 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/6/#laws.3.50.0">1Sp2005 c 6 art 3 s 50</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/287/#laws.1.55.0">2008 c 287 art 1 s 55</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/64/#laws.0.7.0">2009 c 64 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/320/#laws.1.6.0">2010 c 320 art 1 s 6</a>; art 2 s 3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/312/#laws.11.11.0">2014 c 312 art 11 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.64.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 64</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.4.52.0">2023 c 68 art 4 s 52</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.827">
        <h1 class="shn">169.827 GROSS WEIGHT REDUCTION ON RESTRICTED ROUTE.</h1>
        <p>The maximum weight on any single axle, two consecutive axles spaced within eight feet or less, three consecutive axles spaced within nine feet or less, or four consecutive axles spaced within 14 feet or less shall not exceed 18,000 pounds, 34,000 pounds, 43,000 pounds, or 51,500 pounds respectively multiplied by a factor of the axle weight in tons allowed on the restricted route divided by nine.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.827.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/321/#laws.0.4.0">1981 c 321 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.42.0">1982 c 424 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/617/#laws.0.11.0">1982 c 617 s 11</a>-13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/198/#laws.0.9.0">1983 c 198 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/398/#laws.13.6.0">1986 c 398 art 13 s 6</a>-9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/452/#laws.0.20.0">1986 c 452 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/1/3/#laws.4.13.0">1Sp1986 c 3 art 4 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/112/#laws.0.4.0">1991 c 112 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/333/#laws.0.18.0">1991 c 333 s 18</a>,19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/578/#laws.0.7.0">1992 c 578 s 7</a>-10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/635/#laws.1.16.0">1994 c 635 art 1 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/372/#laws.1.8.0">1998 c 372 art 1 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/433/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 433 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/156/#laws.0.1.0">2001 c 156 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/213/#laws.0.10.0">2001 c 213 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/364/#laws.0.13.0">2002 c 364 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/64/#laws.0.8.0">2009 c 64 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.828">
        <h1 class="shn">169.828 AXLE RESTRICTIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.828.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Consecutive axle weight and number of axles.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">No vehicle alone nor any single vehicle of a combination of vehicles shall be equipped with more than four axles unless the additional axles are steering axles or castering axles; provided that the limitation on the number of axles as provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829 </a>shall not apply to any vehicle operated under permit pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.86">169.86</a>. No vehicle alone nor any single vehicle of a combination of vehicles shall exceed the posted weight limit for a single vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.828.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Variable load axle.</span></h2>
          <p>A vehicle or combination of vehicles equipped with one or more variable load axles shall have the pressure control preset so that the weight carried on the variable load axle may not be varied by the operator during transport of any load. The actuating control for the axle shall function only as an on-and-off switch. The provisions of this subdivision do not apply to any farm truck registered prior to July 1, 1981, under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.1c">168.013, subdivision 1c</a>, for 57,000 pounds or less. This subdivision does not apply to rear-loading refuse-compactor vehicles, except that any refuse-compactor vehicle having a tridem rear axle must comply with this subdivision before being issued a special permit under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.86#stat.169.86.5">169.86, subdivision 5</a>, paragraph (h).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.828.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/321/#laws.0.4.0">1981 c 321 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.42.0">1982 c 424 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/617/#laws.0.11.0">1982 c 617 s 11</a>-13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/198/#laws.0.9.0">1983 c 198 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/398/#laws.13.6.0">1986 c 398 art 13 s 6</a>-9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/452/#laws.0.20.0">1986 c 452 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/1/3/#laws.4.13.0">1Sp1986 c 3 art 4 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/112/#laws.0.4.0">1991 c 112 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/333/#laws.0.18.0">1991 c 333 s 18</a>,19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/578/#laws.0.7.0">1992 c 578 s 7</a>-10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/635/#laws.1.16.0">1994 c 635 art 1 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/372/#laws.1.8.0">1998 c 372 art 1 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/433/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 433 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/156/#laws.0.1.0">2001 c 156 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/213/#laws.0.10.0">2001 c 213 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/364/#laws.0.13.0">2002 c 364 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/320/#laws.2.4.0">2010 c 320 art 2 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.829">
        <h1 class="shn">169.829 WEIGHT LIMITS NOT APPLICABLE TO CERTAIN VEHICLES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.829.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">City vehicle except on trunk highway.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.828">169.828</a> do not apply to vehicles operated exclusively in any city in this state which has in effect an ordinance regulating the gross weight of vehicles operated within that city.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) This subdivision does not apply to trunk highways.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.829.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.4.129.0">2023 c 68 art 4 s 129</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.829.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Utility vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.828">169.828</a> do not apply to a utility vehicle that does not exceed a weight of 20,000 pounds per axle and is owned by:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) a public utility, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/216B.02">216B.02</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) a municipality or municipal utility that operates that vehicle for its municipal electric, gas, or water system; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) a cooperative electric association organized under chapter 308A.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.829.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Certain emergency vehicles.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.80">169.80</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.88">169.88 </a>governing size, weight, and load do not apply to a fire apparatus, a law enforcement special response vehicle, or a licensed land emergency ambulance service vehicle.</p>
          <p>(b) Emergency vehicles designed to transport personnel and equipment to support the suppression of fires and to mitigate other hazardous situations are subject to the following weight limitations when operated on an interstate highway: (1) 24,000 pounds on a single steering axle; (2) 33,500 pounds on a single drive axle; (3) 52,000 pounds on a tandem rear drive steer axle; and (4) 62,000 pounds on a tandem axle. The gross weight of an emergency vehicle operating on an interstate highway must not exceed 86,000 pounds.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.829.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Sewage septic tank trucks.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For the purposes of this subdivision, "emergency pumping services" means a sewage septic tank truck's response to:</p>
          <p>(1) uncontrolled and unintended seepage of the contents of a septic system into the ground, around a structure, or into a body of surface water;</p>
          <p>(2) damage or malfunction to a septic system that requires removal of the contents of the septic system for repair or maintenance; or</p>
          <p>(3) a condition that creates an immediate hazard to the health, welfare, or safety of a person.</p>
          <p>(b) When a sewage septic tank truck used exclusively to transport sewage from septic or holding tanks is performing emergency pumping services, sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826">169.826 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.828">169.828</a> do not apply, and the weight limitations under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.824">169.824</a> are increased by ten percent when transporting sewage from a single point of service to the point of unloading.</p>
          <p>(c) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.824#stat.169.824.1">169.824, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (d); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826">169.826, subdivision </a>3; or any other law to the contrary, a permit is not required to operate a vehicle under this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(d) The seasonal weight increases under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826#stat.169.826.1">169.826, subdivision 1</a>, do not apply to a vehicle operated under this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(e) A vehicle operated under this subdivision is subject to bridge load limits posted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.84">169.84</a>.</p>
          <p>(f) A vehicle operated under this subdivision must not be operated with a load that exceeds the tire manufacturer's recommended load, the manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating as affixed to the vehicle, or other certification of gross vehicle weight rating under Code of Federal Regulations, title 49, sections 567.4 to 567.7.</p>
          <p>(g) The exceptions under this subdivision do not apply to a sewage septic tank truck's operation on an interstate highway.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.829.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/321/#laws.0.4.0">1981 c 321 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.42.0">1982 c 424 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/617/#laws.0.11.0">1982 c 617 s 11</a>-13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/198/#laws.0.9.0">1983 c 198 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/398/#laws.13.6.0">1986 c 398 art 13 s 6</a>-9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/452/#laws.0.20.0">1986 c 452 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/1/3/#laws.4.13.0">1Sp1986 c 3 art 4 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/112/#laws.0.4.0">1991 c 112 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/333/#laws.0.18.0">1991 c 333 s 18</a>,19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/578/#laws.0.7.0">1992 c 578 s 7</a>-10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/635/#laws.1.16.0">1994 c 635 art 1 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/372/#laws.1.8.0">1998 c 372 art 1 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/433/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 433 s 1</a>,4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/156/#laws.0.1.0">2001 c 156 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/213/#laws.0.10.0">2001 c 213 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/364/#laws.0.13.0">2002 c 364 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/97/#laws.0.3.0">2003 c 97 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/19/#laws.2.63.0">1Sp2003 c 19 art 2 s 63</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.69.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 69</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/287/#laws.1.56.0">2008 c 287 art 1 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/320/#laws.2.5.0">2010 c 320 art 2 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/3/#laws.3.67.0">1Sp2017 c 3 art 3 s 67</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.65.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 65</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/104/#laws.1.48.0">2024 c 104 art 1 s 48</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.8295">
        <h1 class="shn">169.8295 WEIGHT LIMITS; VEHICLES TRANSPORTING MILK.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.8295.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Weight limits increase.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The weight limitations under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a> are increased by ten percent for a single-unit vehicle transporting fluid milk from the point of production to (1) another point of production for additional loading, or (2) the point of first processing.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.824#stat.169.824.1">169.824, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (d); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826">169.826, subdivision </a>3; or other law to the contrary, a permit is not required to operate a vehicle under this section.</p>
          <p>(c) The seasonal weight increases under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826#stat.169.826.1">169.826, subdivision 1</a>, do not apply to a vehicle operated under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.8295.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Requirements; restrictions.</span></h2>
          <p>A vehicle operated under this section:</p>
          <p>(1) is subject to seasonal load restrictions under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87">169.87</a>, except as otherwise provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87#stat.169.87.4">169.87, subdivision 4</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) is subject to bridge load limits posted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.84">169.84</a>; and</p>
          <p>(3) must not be operated with a load that exceeds the tire manufacturer's recommended load, the manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating as affixed to the vehicle, or other certification of gross vehicle weight rating under Code of Federal Regulations, title 49, sections 567.4 to 567.7.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.8295.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/86/#laws.0.1.0">2017 c 86 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.8296">
        <h1 class="shn">169.8296 WEIGHT LIMITS; TOWING AND RECOVERY VEHICLE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.8296.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Annual permit.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may issue permits to an applicant who pays a single $300 annual fee to cover all tow trucks and towing vehicles owned by the applicant and who meets any other conditions prescribed by the commissioner. The proceeds of this fee must be deposited in the trunk highway fund. The permit authorizes the tow truck or towing vehicle, when towing a disabled or damaged vehicle to a place of repair or safekeeping, to exceed the length and weight limitations of this chapter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.8296.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Applicability with urgent movement.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.828">169.828</a> do not apply to a tow truck or towing vehicle when towing a disabled or damaged vehicle and the movement is urgent and for the purpose of removing the disabled vehicle from the roadway to a place of repair or safekeeping. A permit is not required for a vehicle operating under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.8296.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Seasonal load restrictions; exemption.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this subdivision, "recovery vehicle" means a vehicle equipped with a boom that is used to move or recover an inoperable vehicle.</p>
          <p>(b) The seasonal load restrictions under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87">169.87, subdivisions 1</a> and 2, do not apply to a tow truck, towing vehicle, or a recovery vehicle that does not exceed a weight of 20,000 pounds per single axle and is being operated for the purpose of towing or recovering another vehicle that:</p>
          <p>(1) is involved in a vehicle crash or is inoperable and is located within a public road right-of-way; or</p>
          <p>(2) has entered a public body of water adjacent to the roadway.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.8296.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.4.53.0">2023 c 68 art 4 s 53</a>
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="section" id="stat.169.84">
        <h1 class="shn">169.84 LOAD LIMIT ON BRIDGE.</h1>
        <p>Subject to the limitations upon wheel and axle loads prescribed in this chapter, the gross weight of any vehicle or combination of vehicles driven onto or over a bridge on any highway shall not exceed the safe capacity of the bridge, as may be indicated by warning posted on the bridge or the approaches thereto.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.84.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-276</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.126.0">1937 c 464 s 126</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1953/0/22/#laws.0.1.0">1953 c 22 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.85">
        <h1 class="shn">169.85 WEIGHING; PENALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.85.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Driver to stop for weighing.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The driver of a vehicle that has been lawfully stopped may be required by an officer to submit the vehicle and load to a weighing by means of portable or stationary scales.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) In addition, the officer may require that the vehicle be driven to the nearest available scales, but only if:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the distance to the scales is no further than five miles, or if the distance from the point where the vehicle is stopped to the vehicle's destination is not increased by more than ten miles as a result of proceeding to the nearest available scales; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) if the vehicle is a commercial motor vehicle, no more than two other commercial motor vehicles are waiting to be inspected at the scale.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) Official traffic-control devices as authorized by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06">169.06</a> may be used to direct the driver to the nearest scale.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) When a truck weight enforcement operation is conducted by means of portable or stationary scales, signs giving notice of the operation must be posted within the highway right-of-way and adjacent to the roadway within two miles of the operation. The driver of a truck or combination of vehicles registered for or with a gross vehicle weight exceeding 10,000 pounds shall proceed to the scale site and submit the vehicle to weighing and inspection.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.85.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Unloading.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Upon weighing a vehicle and load, as provided in this section, an officer may require the driver to stop the vehicle in a suitable place and remain standing until a portion of the load is removed that is sufficient to reduce the gross weight of the vehicle to the limit permitted under either section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.3">168.013, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (b), or sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a>, whichever is the lesser violation, if any. A suitable place is a location where loading or tampering with the load is not prohibited by federal, state, or local law, rule, or ordinance.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Except as provided in paragraph (c), a driver may be required to unload a vehicle only if the weighing officer determines that (1) on routes subject to the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a>, the weight on an axle exceeds the lawful gross weight prescribed by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a>, by 2,000 pounds or more, or the weight on a group of two or more consecutive axles in cases where the distance between the centers of the first and last axles of the group under consideration is ten feet or less exceeds the lawful gross weight prescribed by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a>, by 4,000 pounds or more; or (2) the weight is unlawful on an axle or group of consecutive axles on a road restricted in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87">169.87</a>. Material unloaded must be cared for by the owner or driver of the vehicle at the risk of the owner or driver.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) The driver is not required to unload under paragraph (b) when the gross weight of the vehicle does not exceed:</p>
          <p>(1) the sum of the vehicle's registered gross weight, the weight allowance set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.3">168.013, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (b), and, if applicable, the weight allowance permitted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826">169.826</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) the weight allowed by special permit issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.86">169.86</a> for a vehicle that is operated in conformity with the limitations and conditions of the permit.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.85.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>A driver of a vehicle who (1) fails or refuses to stop and submit the vehicle and load to a weighing as required in this section, (2) fails or refuses, when directed by an officer upon a weighing of the vehicle, to stop the vehicle and otherwise comply with the provisions of this section, or (3) fails to comply with an official traffic-control device as authorized by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.06">169.06</a> that directs the driver to the nearest scale is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.85.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Arrest.</span></h2>
          <p>A peace officer may arrest the driver of a motor vehicle if the peace officer has probable cause to believe that the driver has operated the vehicle in violation of subdivision 3 within the past four hours.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.85.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Identification of driver.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who owns or leases a motor vehicle that a peace officer has probable cause to believe has been operated in violation of subdivision 3 must identify the driver of the motor vehicle upon request of the peace officer. Violation of this subdivision is a petty misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.85.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Officer defined.</span></h2>
          <p>When used in this section, the word "officer" means a member of the State Patrol, an employee of the Department of Public Safety described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299D.06">299D.06</a>, or a peace officer or person under the officer's direction and control employed by a local unit of government who is trained in weight enforcement by the Department of Public Safety.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.85.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-277</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.127.0">1937 c 464 s 127</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/212/#laws.0.1.0">1951 c 212 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1953/0/719/#laws.0.1.0">1953 c 719 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/68/#laws.0.3.0">1975 c 68 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/248/#laws.0.9.0">1977 c 248 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/321/#laws.0.6.0">1981 c 321 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/198/#laws.0.11.0">1983 c 198 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/455/#laws.3.21.0">1996 c 455 art 3 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/159/#laws.2.30.0">1997 c 159 art 2 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/230/#laws.0.3.0">1997 c 230 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/364/#laws.0.14.0">2002 c 364 s 14</a>,15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/371/#laws.3.5.0">2002 c 371 art 3 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/19/#laws.2.36.0">1Sp2003 c 19 art 2 s 36</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.76.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 76</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/1/#laws.4.37.0">1Sp2005 c 1 art 4 s 37</a>,38; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.1.48.0">2008 c 350 art 1 s 48</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/64/#laws.0.9.0">2009 c 64 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/320/#laws.2.6.0">2010 c 320 art 2 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/287/#laws.4.25.0">2012 c 287 art 4 s 25</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.851">
        <h1 class="shn">169.851 WEIGHT RECORD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.851.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.862">169.862</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.871">169.871</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.872">169.872</a>, the terms defined in subdivisions 2 and 3 have the meanings given to them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.851.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Document.</span></h2>
          <p>"Document" includes a bill of lading, freight bill, weight certification, or other similar document.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.851.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">First haul.</span></h2>
          <p>"First haul" has the meaning given it in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.3">168.013, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (d), clause (3).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.851.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Relevant evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A document evidencing the receipt of goods issued by the person consigning the goods for shipment or a person engaged in the business of transporting or forwarding goods, which states a gross weight of the vehicle and load or the weight of the load when combined with the empty weight of the vehicle that is in excess of the prescribed maximum weight limitation permitted by this chapter, is relevant evidence that the weight of the vehicle and load is unlawful.</p>
          <p>(b) For the purposes of this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.871">169.871</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.872">169.872</a>, a document required to be kept under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.872">169.872</a> indicating a unit of measure that, when converted to weight and combined with the weight of the empty vehicle, indicates a gross weight in excess of the prescribed maximum weight limitation permitted by this chapter, is relevant evidence that the weight of the vehicle and load is unlawful.</p>
          <p>(c) The provisions in paragraphs (a) and (b) do not limit the introduction of other competent evidence bearing upon the question of whether or not there is a violation of the prescribed maximum weight limitations permitted by this chapter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.851.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exception for farm and forest products.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Subdivision 4 does not apply to the first haul of unprocessed or raw farm products and the transportation of raw and unfinished forest products, including wood chips, when the maximum weight limitations permitted under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a> are not exceeded by more than ten percent.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.851.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/485/#laws.0.1.0">1980 c 485 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/321/#laws.0.7.0">1981 c 321 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/600/#laws.0.7.0">1994 c 600 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/174/#laws.0.1.0">1995 c 174 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/364/#laws.0.16.0">2002 c 364 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/371/#laws.3.7.0">2002 c 371 art 3 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/6/#laws.3.51.0">1Sp2005 c 6 art 3 s 51</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/320/#laws.2.7.0">2010 c 320 art 2 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.73.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 73</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.86">
        <h1 class="shn">169.86 SPECIAL PERMIT TO EXCEED HEIGHT, WIDTH, OR LOAD; FEES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Permit authorities; restrictions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner, with respect to highways under the commissioner's jurisdiction, and local authorities, with respect to highways under their jurisdiction, may, in their discretion, upon application in writing and good cause being shown therefor, issue a special permit, in writing, authorizing the applicant to move a vehicle or combination of vehicles of a size or weight of vehicle or load exceeding the maximum specified in this chapter, exceeding the gross weight for which the vehicle is registered under chapter 168, or otherwise not in conformity with the provisions of this chapter, upon any highway under the jurisdiction of the party granting such permit and for the maintenance of which such party is responsible.</p>
          <p>(b) Permits relating to over-width, over-length manufactured homes shall not be issued to persons other than manufactured home dealers or manufacturers for movement of new units owned by the manufactured home dealer or manufacturer, until the person has presented a statement from the county auditor and treasurer where the unit is presently located, stating that all personal and real property taxes have been paid. Upon payment of the most recent single year delinquent personal property or current year taxes only, the county auditor or treasurer must issue a taxes paid statement to a manufactured home dealer or a financial institution desiring to relocate a manufactured home that has been repossessed. This statement must be dated within 30 days of the contemplated move. The statement from the county auditor and treasurer where the unit is presently located, stating that all personal and real property taxes have been paid, may be made by telephone. If the statement is obtained by telephone, the permit shall contain the date and time of the telephone call and the names of the persons in the auditor's office and treasurer's office who verified that all personal and real property taxes had been paid.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner may not grant a permit authorizing the movement, in a three-vehicle combination, of a semitrailer or trailer that exceeds 28-1/2 feet, except that the commissioner (1) may renew a permit that was granted before April 16, 1984, for the movement of a semitrailer or trailer that exceeds the length limitation in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.81#stat.169.81.2">169.81, subdivision 2</a>, or (2) may grant a permit authorizing the transportation of empty trailers that exceed 28-1/2 feet when using a B-train hitching mechanism as defined in Code of Federal Regulations, title 23, section 658.5, from a point of manufacture in the state to the state border.</p>
          <p>(d) The state as to state trunk highways, a statutory or home rule charter city as to streets in the city, or a town as to roads in the town, may issue permits authorizing the transportation of combinations of vehicles exceeding the limitations in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.81">169.81</a>, subdivisions 2a and 3, over highways, streets, or roads within its boundaries. Combinations of vehicles authorized by this paragraph may be restricted as to the use of state trunk highways by the commissioner, to the use of streets by the city road authority, and to the use of roads by the town road authority. Nothing in this paragraph or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.81">169.81</a>, subdivisions 2a and 3, alters or changes the authority vested in local authorities under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.04">169.04</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Seasonal permits for certain haulers.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner of transportation, upon application in writing therefor, may issue special permits annually to any hauler authorizing the hauler to move vehicles or combinations of vehicles with weights exceeding by not more than ten percent the weight limitations contained in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a>, on interstate highways during the times and within the zones specified in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Permit for snowplowing vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner or a local authority may issue an annual permit to a person that authorizes the person to operate on any highway under the jurisdiction of the grantor of the permit, a motor vehicle bearing a snowplow blade that when deployed does not exceed ten feet in width. The permit authorizes operation of the vehicle between October 1 and April 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Required information.</span></h2>
          <p>The application for a permit shall specifically describe in writing the vehicle or vehicles and loads to be moved and the particular highways and period of time for which a permit is requested.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Authority to issue permit; conditions, financial responsibility.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner or local authority may issue or withhold such permit; or, if such permit is issued, limit or prescribe conditions of operation of such vehicle or vehicles, when necessary to assure against undue damage to the road foundations, surfaces or structures, and may require such undertaking or other security as may be deemed necessary to compensate for any injury or damage to any roadway or road structure, and in addition may require that the operator or owner of such vehicle or vehicles have in effect with respect to the operation of such vehicle or vehicles a policy of liability insurance or bond affording substantially the same coverage with respect to injury to persons and damage to property as is required for proof of financial responsibility under the No-Fault Automobile Insurance Act, sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/65B.14">65B.14</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/65B.41">65B.41</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/65B.71">65B.71</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Denial of permit; manufactured home frames.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner or local authority may not deny a permit for the transport to a manufacturing plant of manufactured home frames not more than 15-1/2 feet in width during periods of seasonal weight restrictions unless the load exceeds the weight restrictions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.3b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3b.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/100/#laws.0.30.0">2020 c 100 s 30</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Display and inspection of permit.</span></h2>
          <p>A permit must be carried in the vehicle or combination of vehicles to which it refers and must be open to inspection by any peace officer or authorized agent of any authority granting the permit. A permit may be carried in electronic format if it is easily read. No person shall violate any of the terms or conditions of a special permit.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Fees; proceeds deposited; appropriation.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner, with respect to highways under the commissioner's jurisdiction, may charge a fee for each permit issued. The fee for an annual permit that expires by law on the date of the vehicle registration expiration must be based on the proportion of the year that remains until the expiration date. All fees for permits issued by the commissioner of transportation must be deposited as provided in paragraph (i) and in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/174.525">174.525</a>. Except for those annual permits for which the permit fees are specified elsewhere in this chapter, the fees are:</p>
          <p class="in">(a) $15 for each single trip permit.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) $36 for each job permit. A job permit may be issued for like loads carried on a specific route for a period not to exceed two months. "Like loads" means loads of the same product, weight, and dimension.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) $60 for an annual permit to be issued for a period not to exceed 12 consecutive months. Annual permits may be issued for:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) motor vehicles used to alleviate a temporary crisis adversely affecting the safety or well-being of the public;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) motor vehicles that travel on interstate highways and carry loads authorized under subdivision 1a;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) motor vehicles operating with gross weights authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826#stat.169.826.1a">169.826, subdivision 1a</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) special pulpwood vehicles described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.863">169.863</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) motor vehicles bearing snowplow blades not exceeding ten feet in width;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) noncommercial transportation of a boat by the owner or user of the boat; and</p>
          <p class="in">(7) motor vehicles carrying bales of agricultural products authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.862">169.862</a>.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) $120 for an oversize annual permit to be issued for a period not to exceed 12 consecutive months. Annual permits may be issued for:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) mobile cranes;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) construction equipment, machinery, and supplies;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) manufactured homes and manufactured storage buildings;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) implements of husbandry;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) double-deck buses;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) commercial boat hauling and transporting waterfront structures, including, but not limited to, portable boat docks and boat lifts; and</p>
          <p class="in">(7) three-vehicle combinations consisting of two empty, newly manufactured trailers for cargo, horses, or livestock, not to exceed 28-1/2 feet per trailer; provided, however, the permit allows the vehicles to be moved from a trailer manufacturer to a trailer dealer only while operating on twin-trailer routes designated under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.81#stat.169.81.3">169.81, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (c).</p>
          <p class="in">(e) For vehicles that have axle weights exceeding the weight limitations of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a>, an additional cost added to the fees listed above. However, this paragraph applies to any vehicle described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.3">168.013, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (b), but only when the vehicle exceeds its gross weight allowance set forth in that paragraph, and then the additional cost is for all weight, including the allowance weight, in excess of the permitted maximum axle weight. The additional cost is equal to the product of the distance traveled times the sum of the overweight axle group cost factors shown in the following chart:</p>

          <p class="bl">The amounts added are rounded to the nearest cent for each axle or axle group. The additional cost does not apply to paragraph (c), clauses (1) and (3).</p>
          <p class="bl">For a vehicle found to exceed the appropriate maximum permitted weight, a cost-per-mile fee of 22 cents per ton, or fraction of a ton, over the permitted maximum weight is imposed in addition to the normal permit fee. Miles must be calculated based on the distance already traveled in the state plus the distance from the point of detection to a transportation loading site or unloading site within the state or to the point of exit from the state.</p>
          <p class="in">(f) As an alternative to paragraph (e), an annual permit may be issued for overweight, or oversize and overweight, mobile cranes; construction equipment, machinery, and supplies; implements of husbandry; and commercial boat hauling. The fees for the permit are as follows:</p>

          <p class="bl">If the gross weight of the vehicle is more than 155,000 pounds the permit fee is determined under paragraph (e).</p>
          <p class="in">(g) For vehicles which exceed the width limitations set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.80">169.80</a> by more than 72 inches, an additional cost equal to $120 added to the amount in paragraph (a) when the permit is issued while seasonal load restrictions pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87">169.87</a> are in effect.</p>
          <p class="in">(h) $85 for an annual permit to be issued for a period not to exceed 12 months, for refuse-compactor vehicles that carry a gross weight of not more than: 22,000 pounds on a single rear axle; 38,000 pounds on a tandem rear axle; or, subject to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.828#stat.169.828.2">169.828, subdivision 2</a>, 46,000 pounds on a tridem rear axle. A permit issued for up to 46,000 pounds on a tridem rear axle must limit the gross vehicle weight to not more than 62,000 pounds.</p>
          <p class="in">(i) $300 for a motor vehicle described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.8261">169.8261</a>. The fee under this paragraph must be deposited as follows:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the first $50,000 in each fiscal year must be deposited in the trunk highway fund for costs related to administering the permit program and inspecting and posting bridges; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) all remaining money in each fiscal year must be deposited in the bridge inspection and signing account as provided under subdivision 5b.</p>
          <p class="in">(j) $200 for an annual permit for a vehicle operating under authority of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.824#stat.169.824.2">169.824, subdivision 2</a>, clause (2).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Additional tax for excessive gross weight.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">When a special permit is issued under this chapter, the commissioner shall collect in addition to the permit fee an additional tax for excessive gross weight, if the weight allowed under the permit is greater than the gross weight for which the vehicle is registered under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013">168.013</a>. The tax shall be calculated as the difference between the registration tax paid under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.1e">168.013, subdivision 1e</a>, and the additional tax that would be due under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013">168.013</a>, subdivision 1e, at the gross weight allowed under the permit, prorated by the number of days for which the permit is effective. Proceeds of the surcharge must be deposited in the state treasury and credited to the highway user tax distribution fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.5b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5b.<span class="headnote">Bridge inspection and signing account; appropriation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A bridge inspection and signing account is established in the special revenue fund. The account consists of fees for special permits as specified under this chapter, and any other money donated, allotted, transferred, or otherwise provided to the account.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) The revenue in the bridge inspection and signing account under this subdivision is annually appropriated to the commissioner for:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) inspection of local bridges and identification of local bridges to be posted, including contracting with a consultant for some or all of these functions; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) erection of weight-posting signs on local bridges.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Articulated bus.</span></h2>
          <p>Articulated buses operated by public transit operators may exceed the length and weight limitations of this chapter, subject only to an annual permit from the commissioner for such operation, and shall not be subject to any city ordinance or to any permit from any local road authority. The application for a permit shall contain such information as may be required by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Agreement with other state.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) On behalf of the state of Minnesota, the commissioner may enter into agreements with authorized representatives of other states for the reciprocal administration and granting of permits to allow the movement of vehicles of sizes and weights that do not conform to Minnesota law. The agreement may authorize representatives of other states to issue permits to allow vehicles that do not conform to the size and weight provisions of this chapter to travel on highways under the jurisdiction of the commissioner.</p>
          <p>(b) An agreement entered into under paragraph (a), and all amendments to it, must be in writing and may provide for exchanging information for audit and enforcement activities, collecting fees established under this chapter, and distributing fees collected under the agreement. It must state that no permit issued under the agreement excuses a vehicle operator from compliance with a law of this state other than the laws governing size and weight of vehicles.</p>
          <p>(c) For purposes of paragraphs (a) and (b), "state" means a state, territory, or possession of the United States, the District of Columbia, a foreign country, and a state or province of a foreign country.</p>
          <p>(d) Fees collected under authority of the agreement must be deposited in the Minnesota state treasury and credited to the trunk highway fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.86.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.</h2>
          <p>MS 2010 [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168B.15">168B.15</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.86.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-278</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.128.0">1937 c 464 s 128</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1943/0/226/#laws.0.4.0">1943 c 226 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1953/0/307/#laws.0.1.0">1953 c 307 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/262/#laws.0.1.0">1967 c 262 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/549/#laws.0.3.0">1973 c 549 s 3</a>;
