      <div class="section" id="stat.169.871">
        <h1 class="shn">169.871 EXCESS WEIGHT; CIVIL PENALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.871.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Civil liability.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The owner or lessee of a vehicle that is operated with a gross weight in excess of a weight limit imposed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.8295">169.8295</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.84">169.84 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.851">169.851</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87">169.87</a> or a shipper who ships or tenders goods for shipment in a single truck or combination vehicle that exceeds a weight limit imposed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.8295">169.8295</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.84">169.84 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.851">169.851</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87">169.87</a> is liable for a civil penalty as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the total gross excess weight is not more than 1,000 pounds, one cent per pound for each pound in excess of the legal limit;</p>
          <p>(2) if the total gross excess weight is more than 1,000 pounds but not more than 3,000 pounds, $10 plus five cents per pound for each pound in excess of 1,000 pounds;</p>
          <p>(3) if the total gross excess weight is more than 3,000 pounds but not more than 5,000 pounds, $110 plus ten cents per pound for each pound in excess of 3,000 pounds;</p>
          <p>(4) if the total gross excess weight is more than 5,000 pounds but not more than 7,000 pounds, $310 plus 15 cents per pound for each pound in excess of 5,000 pounds;</p>
          <p>(5) if the total gross excess weight is more than 7,000 pounds, $610 plus 20 cents per pound for each pound in excess of 7,000 pounds.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, if a person found guilty of a violation of a weight limit imposed under this section or sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.8295">169.8295</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.84">169.84 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.851">169.851</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87">169.87</a> is also found by the court to have knowingly and contemporaneously attempted to evade a fixed weigh station or to otherwise avoid weighing by means of stationary scales under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.85">169.85</a> or other law, the court must impose a penalty of twice the amount otherwise authorized under paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(c) Any penalty imposed upon a defendant under this subdivision must not exceed the penalty prescribed by this subdivision. Any fine paid by the defendant in a criminal overweight action that arose from the same overweight violation is applied toward payment of the civil penalty under this subdivision. A peace officer or Department of Public Safety employee described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299D.06">299D.06</a> who cites a driver for a violation of the weight limitations established by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.81">169.81</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.851">169.851</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87">169.87</a> must give written notice to the driver that the driver or another may also be liable for the civil penalties provided herein in the same or separate proceedings.</p>
          <p>(d) A penalty imposed upon the owner or lessee of a vehicle that is based on violations identified by the use of shippers' weight records under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.872">169.872</a> must not exceed an aggregate of $10,000.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.871.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Special permit violations.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The owner or lessee of a vehicle that is operated with a gross weight in excess of an adjusted weight limit and a shipper who ships or tenders goods for shipment in a single truck or combination vehicle that exceeds an adjusted weight limit is liable for a civil penalty. The civil penalty is the greater of (1) as calculated at a rate of five cents per pound for each pound in excess of the highest weight allowed by the permit or under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826#stat.169.826.1">169.826, subdivision 1</a>, or (2) $100.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Any penalty imposed upon a defendant under this subdivision shall not exceed the penalty prescribed by this subdivision. Any fine paid by the defendant in a criminal overweight action that arose from the same overweight violation may not be applied toward payment of the civil penalty under this subdivision. A peace officer or Department of Public Safety employee described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299D.06">299D.06</a> who cites a driver for a violation of the adjusted weight limit shall give written notice to the driver that the driver or another may also be liable for the civil penalty provided in this subdivision in the same or separate proceedings.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) For purposes of this subdivision, "adjusted weight limit" means a weight limit (1) imposed by a permit issued under this chapter, or (2) imposed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.826">169.826</a>, subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.871.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Civil penalty for first two violations.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding subdivision 1, paragraph (a), clauses (1) to (5), a civil penalty under subdivision 1 for a violation in a motor vehicle in the course of a first haul as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.3">168.013, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (d), clause (3), of a weight limit imposed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.823">169.823 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.829">169.829</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.84">169.84 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.851">169.851</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87">169.87</a> that is not preceded by two or more violations of the gross weight limits in those sections in that motor vehicle within the previous 12 months, may not exceed $150.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.871.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Jurisdiction.</span></h2>
          <p>The district court may hear, try and determine actions commenced under this section. Trials under this section shall be to the court, sitting without a jury. Trials to the court under this section shall, if possible, be conducted at the same time as pretrial motions or trials in the criminal prosecution under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.81">169.81</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.87">169.87</a>, if any, subject to the agreement of the defendant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.871.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Appearance.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/8.01">8.01</a>, county or city attorneys may appear in civil actions commenced under this section at the request of the attorney general.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.871.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>Civil actions under this section may be commenced in any county in which the vehicle was loaded, unloaded or operated in violation of subdivision 1 unless there is agreement that the action may be tried in another county or municipality.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.871.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Fines; proceeds allocated.</span></h2>
          <p>Any penalty imposed and fines collected pursuant to this section shall be disposed of as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299D.03#stat.299D.03.5">299D.03, subdivision 5</a>, with the following exceptions:</p>
          <p>(a) If the violation occurs in the county, and the county attorney appears in the action, the remaining five-eighths shall be credited to the highway user tax distribution fund.</p>
          <p>(b) If the violation occurs within the municipality, and the city attorney appears in the action, the remaining one-third shall be paid to the highway user tax distribution fund.</p>
          <p>(c) Except as provided in paragraph (d), when the attorney general appears in the action, all penalties imposed and fines collected shall be credited to the highway user tax distribution fund.</p>
          <p>(d) If the violation occurs in Hennepin County, and the arrest or apprehension is made by the county sheriff, three-eighths of the civil penalty shall be credited to the general revenue fund of the county and the remaining five-eighths shall be credited to the highway user tax distribution fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.871.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Costs and disbursements.</span></h2>
          <p>The prevailing party in any action commenced under this section shall be entitled to reasonable costs incurred in the action.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.871.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Shipper's good-faith exception.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The penalty imposed by subdivision 1 shall not be imposed on a shipper who in good faith ships goods or tenders goods for shipment in a vehicle that does not exceed the maximum gross weight for which the truck is licensed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.1e">168.013, subdivision 1e</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) For purposes of this section, "good faith" means that (1) the vehicle is licensed pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.1e">168.013, subdivision 1e</a>, (2) the operator of the vehicle is not under the control of the shipper, (3) the operator has requested that the vehicle be loaded to the maximum gross weight for which the vehicle is licensed, and (4) the road leading from the shipper's immediate place of shipment may be legally used for the allowed gross weight of the vehicle with its legally maximum load.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.871.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/485/#laws.0.2.0">1980 c 485 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/618/#laws.0.10.0">1980 c 618 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/321/#laws.0.10.0">1981 c 321 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/3/2/#laws.1.14.0">3Sp1981 c 2 art 1 s 14</a>,15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/198/#laws.0.13.0">1983 c 198 s 13</a>,14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/299/#laws.0.12.0">1985 c 299 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/606/#laws.0.1.0">1988 c 606 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/455/#laws.3.23.0">1996 c 455 art 3 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/230/#laws.0.4.0">1997 c 230 s 4</a>,5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/254/#laws.2.16.0">1998 c 254 art 2 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/297/#laws.0.1.0">2002 c 297 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/320/#laws.1.15.0">2010 c 320 art 1 s 15</a>-17; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/86/#laws.0.2.0">2017 c 86 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.77.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 77</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.872">
        <h1 class="shn">169.872 RECEIPT OF CERTAIN OVERWEIGHT LOADS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.872.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Record keeping.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who weighs goods before or after unloading or a person who loads or unloads goods on the basis of liquid volume measure shall keep a written record of the origin, weight, and composition of each shipment, the date of loading or receipt, the name and address of the shipper, the total number of axles on the vehicle or combination of vehicles, and the registration number of the power unit or some other means of identification by which the shipment was transported. The record shall be retained for 14 days and shall be open to inspection and copying by a state law enforcement officer or motor transport representative, except state conservation officers, upon demand. No search warrant is required to inspect or copy the record. This subdivision does not apply to a person weighing goods who is not involved in the shipping, receiving, and transporting of those goods, or to a person weighing raw and unfinished farm products transported in a single-unit vehicle with not more than three axles or by a trailer towed by a farm tractor when the transportation is the first haul of the product.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.872.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Limit on civil penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A civil penalty for excessive weight under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.871">169.871</a> may be imposed based on a record of a shipment under this section only if a state law enforcement officer or motor transportation representative: (1) has inspected and copied the record within 14 days of the date the shipment was received by the person keeping the record; and (2) has assessed the penalty within 90 days of the date the officer or representative inspected and copied the record.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.872.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>Except for records relating to the loading and unloading of the first haul of unprocessed or raw farm products and the transportation of raw and unfinished forest products, a record kept and maintained as provided in subdivision 1 that shows that a vehicle has exceeded a gross weight limit imposed by this chapter is relevant evidence of a violation of this chapter. The foregoing provisions do not limit the introduction of other competent evidence bearing upon the question of whether or not there is a violation of the prescribed maximum weight limitation permitted by this chapter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.872.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who fails to keep, maintain, or open for inspection and copying, those documents as required in subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor. A person who does not accurately record the information required to be contained in those documents required in subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.872.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/485/#laws.0.3.0">1980 c 485 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/321/#laws.0.11.0">1981 c 321 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/3/2/#laws.1.16.0">3Sp1981 c 2 art 1 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/299/#laws.0.13.0">1985 c 299 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/297/#laws.0.2.0">2002 c 297 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/287/#laws.3.38.0">2012 c 287 art 3 s 38</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.88">
        <h1 class="shn">169.88 DAMAGES; LIABILITY.</h1>
        <p>(a) Any person driving any vehicle, object, or contrivance upon any highway or highway structure shall be liable for all damage which the highway or highway structure may sustain as a result of any illegal operation, driving, or moving of such vehicle, object, or contrivance, or as a result of operation, driving or moving any vehicle, object, or contrivance weighing in excess of the maximum weight in this chapter but authorized by a special permit issued as provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.80">169.80</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.88">169.88</a>.</p>
        <p>(b) When such driver is not the owner of such vehicle, object, or contrivance, but is so operating, driving, or moving the same with the express or implied permission of the owner, then the owner and driver shall be jointly and severally liable for any such damage.</p>
        <p>(c) Any person who by willful acts or failure to exercise due care, damages any road, street, or highway or highway structure shall be liable for the amount thereof.</p>
        <p>(d) Damages under this section may be recovered in a civil action brought by the authorities in control of such highway or highway structure.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.88.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-280</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.130.0">1937 c 464 s 130</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/509/#laws.0.1.0">1967 c 509 s 1</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.881">
        <h1 class="shn">169.881 VEHICLE PLATOONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.881.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Vehicle platoon plan.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person may apply to the commissioner for approval of a plan to use a platooning system on freeways and expressways, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/160.02">160.02</a>, on the trunk highway system. A platooning system may only be used if a plan has been approved by the commissioner. The commissioner must consult with the commissioner of public safety prior to approving the plan, regarding identifiable public safety concerns.</p>
          <p>(b) A plan is valid for one year from the date of issuance, unless the plan is for a shorter period of time, in which case the plan is valid for the shorter time period.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.881.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Required information.</span></h2>
          <p>The plan must include but is not limited to the following information submitted in the manner prescribed by the commissioner:</p>
          <p>(1) total length of the vehicle platoon;</p>
          <p>(2) the configuration of the vehicle platoon, including spacing between vehicles;</p>
          <p>(3) proposed route and section of freeway or expressway;</p>
          <p>(4) proposed time frames the vehicle platoon will be operating;</p>
          <p>(5) certification that each human driver in the vehicle platoon has a valid driver's license for the type or class of vehicle being driven;</p>
          <p>(6) certification that the vehicle height, width, and weight limits conform to this chapter; and</p>
          <p>(7) vehicle identification information.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.881.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Authority to approve plan.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner may grant or deny a vehicle platoon plan. The approved plan may include reasonable conditions and restrictions to ensure public safety, minimize congestion, or prevent undue damage to roads or structures.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner must provide written notice to the applicant and to the commissioner of public safety if a plan is denied and must list the reasons for the denial. The commissioner must approve or deny a plan within 60 days.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.881.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>Vehicle platoons must meet the following requirements:</p>
          <p>(1) the platoon must not include more than three vehicles;</p>
          <p>(2) each vehicle in the vehicle platoon must have a platooning system installed;</p>
          <p>(3) while platooning, each vehicle must have the platooning system engaged;</p>
          <p>(4) each vehicle in the vehicle platoon must have a human driver present and in the driver seat who is monitoring performance of the vehicle at all times and who holds a valid driver's license for the type or class of vehicle being driven;</p>
          <p>(5) each vehicle in the vehicle platoon must meet the vehicle height, width, and weight limits under this chapter;</p>
          <p>(6) each vehicle in the platoon must be covered by minimum liability insurance; and</p>
          <p>(7) each vehicle in the platoon must have a paper or electronic copy of the approved plan in the vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.881.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Operations.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, a vehicle platoon must allow reasonable access for the movement of other motor vehicles to change lanes and enter or exit the roadway.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.881.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/3/#laws.3.70.0">1Sp2019 c 3 art 3 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.1.55.0">2020 c 83 art 1 s 55</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">OFFENSES, PENALTIES, AND JUDICIAL PROVISIONS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.89">
        <h1 class="shn">169.89 PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.89.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Violation; when petty misdemeanor enhanced to misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Unless otherwise declared in this chapter with respect to particular offenses, it is a petty misdemeanor for any person to do any act forbidden or fail to perform any act required by this chapter; except that:</p>
          <p>(1) a violation which is committed in a manner or under circumstances so as to endanger or be likely to endanger any person or property; or</p>
          <p>(2) exclusive of violations relating to the standing or parking of an unattended vehicle, a violation of any of the provisions of this chapter, classified therein as a petty misdemeanor, when preceded by two or more petty misdemeanor convictions within the immediate preceding 12-month period;</p>
          <p class="bl">is a misdemeanor to which the provisions of subdivision 2 shall not apply.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.89.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Petty misdemeanor penalty; no jury trial.</span></h2>
          <p>A person charged with a petty misdemeanor is not entitled to a jury trial but shall be tried by a judge without a jury. If convicted, the person is not subject to imprisonment but shall be punished by a fine of not more than $300.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.89.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Obsolete]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.89.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Driver's record.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person is arrested for a violation of any provision of this chapter, or a violation of any provision of a city ordinance regulating traffic, the court before whom the matter is heard shall determine the driver's record of the person from the commissioner of public safety before pronouncing sentence and the expense incident to the procurement of this information is taxable as costs upon the conviction.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.89.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Driver improvement clinic; attendance.</span></h2>
          <p>In conjunction with or in lieu of other penalties provided by law for violation of this chapter or a municipal ordinance enacted in conformance thereto, the trial court may in its judgment of conviction order the convicted person to attend and satisfactorily complete a course of study at an approved driver improvement clinic or youth-oriented driver improvement clinic. The commissioner of public safety may, upon the motion of the commissioner of public safety or upon recommendation of the court, suspend, for a period of not to exceed 30 days, the operator's license, provisional license, permit, or nonresident operating privilege of any person who fails or refuses to comply with an order to attend an approved driver improvement clinic or youth-oriented driver improvement clinic. The requirement of attendance at an approved driver improvement clinic or youth-oriented driver improvement clinic is not a fine, imprisonment, or sentence within the meaning of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.02">609.02</a>. The court may not order a convicted person to attend any driver improvement clinic or youth-oriented driver improvement clinic which is located more than 35 miles from the person's residence. For the purposes of this section "an approved driver improvement clinic or youth-oriented driver improvement clinic" means a clinic whose curriculum and mode of instruction conform to standards promulgated by the commissioner of public safety.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.89.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-281</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.131.0">1937 c 464 s 131</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.27.0">1939 c 430 s 27</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.34.0">1947 c 428 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1965/0/711/#laws.0.5.0">1965 c 711 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/118/#laws.0.1.0">1969 c 118 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/1129/#laws.1.18.0">1969 c 1129 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.15.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/123/#laws.5.7.0">1973 c 123 art 5 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/421/#laws.0.2.0">1973 c 421 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/233/#laws.0.1.0">1979 c 233 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/520/#laws.0.2.0">1980 c 520 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.3.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/388/#laws.0.2.0">1998 c 388 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.5.1.0">2000 c 488 art 5 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.891">
        <h1 class="shn">169.891 JURISDICTION; LIMITATION OF ACTIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.891.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Petty misdemeanors.</span></h2>
          <p>Courts which heretofore have had jurisdiction over misdemeanors have the same jurisdiction over petty misdemeanors.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.891.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Limitation.</span></h2>
          <p>The period for commencing an action against any person for a petty misdemeanor shall be the same as that for a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.891.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.16.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 16</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.90">
        <h1 class="shn">169.90 OFFENSES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.90.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Attempt, conspire, aid, cause, or permit offense.</span></h2>
          <p>Every person who commits or attempts to commit, conspires to commit, or aids or abets in the commission of, any act declared herein to be an offense, whether individually or in connection with one or more other persons or as principal, agent, or accessory, shall be guilty of such offense, and every person who falsely, fraudulently, forcibly, or willfully induces, causes, coerces, requires, permits, or directs another to violate any provision of this chapter, is likewise guilty of such offense.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.90.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Require or permit offense by another.</span></h2>
          <p>It is unlawful for the owner, or any other person, employing or otherwise directing the driver of any vehicle to require or knowingly to permit the operation of such vehicle upon a highway in any manner contrary to law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.90.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>MS 1969 [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.42">169.42, subd 2</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.90.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-282</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-283</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.132.0">1937 c 464 s 132</a>,133; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.17.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 17</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.169.901"><b>169.901</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/24/#laws.0.5.0">2001 c 24 s 5</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.905">
        <h1 class="shn">169.905 TRAFFIC STOP; QUESTIONING LIMITED.</h1>
        <p>A peace officer making a traffic stop for a violation of this chapter or chapter 168 must not ask if the operator can identify the reason for the stop. A peace officer making such a traffic stop must inform the vehicle's operator of a reason for the stop unless it would be unreasonable to do so under the totality of the circumstances. A peace officer's failure to comply with this section must not serve as the basis for exclusion of evidence or dismissal of a charge or citation. Section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/645.241">645.241</a> does not apply to violations of this section.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.905.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.3.1.0">2024 c 123 art 3 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">ARREST AND APPEARANCE PROCEDURES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.91">
        <h1 class="shn">169.91 ARREST.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.91.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Procedure.</span></h2>
          <p>When any person is arrested for any violation of any law or ordinance relating to the operation or registration of vehicles punishable as a petty misdemeanor, misdemeanor, gross misdemeanor, or felony, the arrested person shall be taken into custody and immediately taken before a judge within the county in which the offense charged is alleged to have been committed and who has jurisdiction over the offenses and is nearest or most accessible with reference to the place where the arrest is made, in any of the following cases:</p>
          <p>(1) when a person arrested demands an immediate appearance before a judge;</p>
          <p>(2) when a person is arrested and charged with an offense under this chapter causing or contributing to an accident resulting in injury or death to any person;</p>
          <p>(3) when the person is arrested upon a charge of negligent homicide;</p>
          <p>(4) when the person is arrested upon a charge of driving or operating or being in actual physical control of any motor vehicle while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs;</p>
          <p>(5) when the person is arrested upon a charge of failure to stop in the event of an accident causing death, personal injuries, or damage to property;</p>
          <p>(6) when there is reasonable cause for believing that the person arrested may leave the state, except as provided in subdivision 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.91.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.49.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 49</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.91.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Notice to appear.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person is arrested for any violation of any law or ordinance relating to motor vehicles, their registration or their operation, or the use of the highways, the arresting officer shall prepare a written notice to appear in court. This place must be before a judge within the county in which the offense charged is alleged to have been committed who has jurisdiction and is nearest or most accessible with reference to the place of arrest. If the offense is a petty misdemeanor, the notice to appear must include a statement that a failure to appear will be considered a plea of guilty and waiver of the right to trial, unless the failure to appear is due to circumstances beyond the person's control.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.91.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Reciprocal agreements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner of public safety is empowered to enter into and carry out reciprocal agreements with duly authorized representatives of other states, districts, territories and possessions of the United States and provinces of foreign countries having laws or compacts authorizing the release of residents of party jurisdictions upon personal recognizance following arrest for violation of a law or ordinance relating to the operation of a motor vehicle.</p>
          <p>(b) When a reciprocal agreement is in effect, a law enforcement officer observing a violation of any traffic rule by a resident of a party jurisdiction shall issue an appropriate citation and shall not, subject to the provisions of paragraph (c), require the nonresident to post bond or collateral to secure appearance for trial but shall accept the nonresident's personal recognizance, except the nonresident has the right upon request to post bond or collateral in a manner provided by law and in that case the provisions of this subdivision do not apply.</p>
          <p>(c) A nonresident shall not be entitled to be released on personal recognizance if immediate appearance before a judge is required by subdivision 1 or the offense is:</p>
          <p>(1) one which, upon conviction, would result in the revocation of a person's driver's license under the laws of this state; or</p>
          <p>(2) a violation of a highway weight limitation; or</p>
          <p>(3) a violation of a law governing transportation of hazardous materials; or</p>
          <p>(4) driving a motor vehicle without a valid driver's license.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.91.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-284</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-285</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.134.0">1937 c 464 s 134</a>,135; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.28.0">1939 c 430 s 28</a>,29; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1947/0/428/#laws.0.35.0">1947 c 428 s 35</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1955/0/845/#laws.0.1.0">1955 c 845 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/1/19/#laws.0.4.0">Ex1961 c 19 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.18.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/783/#laws.0.1.0">1978 c 783 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/359/#laws.0.12.0">1983 c 359 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/681/#laws.0.9.0">1988 c 681 s 9</a>,10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/333/#laws.0.1.0">1989 c 333 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.92">
        <h1 class="shn">169.92 FAILURE TO APPEAR.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.92.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Appearance by counsel.</span></h2>
          <p>A person may appear in court either in person or through an appearance by counsel. A person is not required to sign a written promise to appear.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.92.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Notice to commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person fails to appear in court in response to a notice to appear prepared under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.91#stat.169.91.3">169.91, subdivision 3</a>, or fails to comply with other orders of the court regarding the appearance or proceedings, the court shall notify the commissioner of public safety of the nonappearance or noncompliance upon a form provided by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.92.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Nonappearance by nonresident.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon receipt of notice from the court that a nonresident did not appear in court, the commissioner of public safety shall forward a copy of the report to the driver licensing authority of the state, district, territory, possession, or province of residence of the person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.92.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>MS 2020 [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.16">171.16, subd 3a</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.92.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-286</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.136.0">1937 c 464 s 136</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/783/#laws.0.4.0">1978 c 783 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/681/#laws.0.11.0">1988 c 681 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/228/#laws.0.1.0">1989 c 228 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/333/#laws.0.6.0">1989 c 333 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/346/#laws.0.2.0">1996 c 346 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/5/#laws.4.67.0">1Sp2021 c 5 art 4 s 67</a>,149</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.93">
        <h1 class="shn">169.93 ARREST WITHOUT WARRANT.</h1>
        <p>The provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.90">169.90</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.95">169.95</a> shall govern all police officers in making arrests without a warrant for violations of this chapter for offenses committed in their presence, but the procedure prescribed herein shall not otherwise be exclusive of any other method prescribed by law for the arrest and prosecution of a person for an offense of like grade.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.93.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-287</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.137.0">1937 c 464 s 137</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">RECORDS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.94">
        <h1 class="shn">169.94 RECORD OF CONVICTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.94.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Not admissible as evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>No record of the conviction of any person for any violation of this chapter shall be admissible as evidence in any court in any civil action.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.94.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Not to affect credibility as witness.</span></h2>
          <p>The conviction of a person upon a charge of violating any provision of this chapter or other traffic rule less than a felony shall not affect or impair the credibility of such person as a witness in any civil or criminal proceeding.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.94.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-288</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-289</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.138.0">1937 c 464 s 138</a>,139; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.95">
        <h1 class="shn">169.95 COURT TO KEEP SEPARATE RECORDS OF VIOLATIONS.</h1>
        <p>(a) Every court administrator shall keep a full record of every case in which a person is charged with a violation of any law or ordinance, regulating the operation of vehicles on highways.</p>
        <p>(b) Within ten days after the conviction or forfeiture of bail of a person upon a charge of violating any provisions of any law or ordinance, regulating the operation of vehicles on highways, the court administrator of the court in which the conviction was had or bail was forfeited, shall immediately forward to the Department of Public Safety an abstract of the record of the court covering the case in which the person was convicted or forfeited bail. The abstract must be certified by the person required to prepare it to be true and correct.</p>
        <p>(c) The abstract must be made upon a form furnished by the Department of Public Safety, and shall include the name and address of the party charged, the driver's license number of the person involved, the nature of the offense, the date of hearing, the plea, the judgment, or whether bail was forfeited, and the amount of the fine or forfeiture, as the case may be.</p>
        <p>(d) Every court shall also forward a report to the Department of Public Safety reporting the conviction of any person of manslaughter or other felony in the commission of which a vehicle was used.</p>
        <p>(e) The failure, refusal, or neglect of any judicial officer to comply with any of the requirements of this section shall constitute misconduct in the office and shall be grounds for removal.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.95.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-290</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.140.0">1937 c 464 s 140</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/1129/#laws.1.18.0">1969 c 1129 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/123/#laws.5.7.0">1973 c 123 art 5 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/363/#laws.0.28.0">1981 c 363 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/359/#laws.0.13.0">1983 c 359 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/1/3/#laws.1.82.0">1Sp1986 c 3 art 1 s 82</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">UNIFORM INTERPRETATION</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.96">
        <h1 class="shn">169.96 INTERPRETATION AND EFFECT.</h1>
        <p>(a) This chapter shall be interpreted and construed as to effectuate its general purpose to make uniform the law of those states which enact it.</p>
        <p>(b) In all civil actions, a violation of any of the provisions of this chapter, by either or any of the parties to such action or actions shall not be negligence per se but shall be prima facie evidence of negligence only.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.96.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-291</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.141.0">1937 c 464 s 141</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/430/#laws.0.30.0">1939 c 430 s 30</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">UNIVERSITY TRAFFIC RULES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.965">
        <h1 class="shn">169.965 UNIVERSITY REGENTS TO REGULATE TRAFFIC AND PARKING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.965.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authority.</span></h2>
          <p>The regents of the University of Minnesota may, from time to time, make, adopt, and enforce such rules, regulations, or ordinances as it may find expedient or necessary relating to the regulation of traffic and parking, upon parking facilities, highways, streets, private roads, and roadways situated on property owned, leased, or occupied by the regents of the University of Minnesota or the University of Minnesota.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.965.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Petty misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who violates such rule, regulation, or ordinance shall be guilty of a petty misdemeanor and subject to the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.891">169.891</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.90#stat.169.90.1">169.90, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.965.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>The prosecution may be before a district court having jurisdiction over the place where the violation occurs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.965.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Enforcement.</span></h2>
          <p>Every sheriff, police officer, or other peace officer shall see that all rules, regulations, and ordinances are obeyed, and shall arrest and prosecute offenders.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.965.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Enforcement powers.</span></h2>
          <p>The regents of the University of Minnesota are hereby authorized to appoint and employ, and fix the compensation to be paid out of funds of the regents of the University of Minnesota, persons who shall have and may exercise on property owned, leased, or occupied by the regents of the University of Minnesota or the University of Minnesota the same powers of arrest for violation of rules, regulations, or ordinances adopted by the regents of the University of Minnesota pursuant to the Highway Traffic Regulation Act, chapters 169 and 169A, as amended, as possessed by a sheriff, police officer, or peace officer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.965.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Judicial notice.</span></h2>
          <p>All persons shall take notice of such rules, regulations, and ordinances without pleading and proof of the same.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.965.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Notice, hearing, filing, and effect.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The regents of the University of Minnesota shall fix a date for a public hearing on the adoption of any such proposed rule, regulation, or ordinance. Notice of such hearing shall be published in a legal newspaper in the county in which the property affected by the rule, regulation, or ordinance is located. The publication shall be at least 15 days and not more than 45 days before the date of the hearing.</p>
          <p>(b) If, after the public hearing, the proposed rule, regulation, or ordinance shall be adopted by a majority of the members of the Board of Regents of the University of Minnesota, the same shall be considered to have been enacted by the regents of the University of Minnesota. A copy of the same shall be signed by the president, attested by the secretary, and filed with the secretary of state of the state of Minnesota, together with proof of publication. Upon such filing, the rule, regulation, or ordinance, as the case may be, shall thenceforth be in full force and effect.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.965.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Allocation of fines.</span></h2>
          <p>The fines collected in Hennepin, St. Louis, and Stevens Counties shall be paid into the treasury of the University of Minnesota, except that the portion of the fines necessary to cover all costs and disbursements incurred in processing and prosecuting the violations in the court shall be retained by the court administrator in Hennepin and St. Louis Counties and by the city of Morris in Stevens County.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.965.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1957/0/456/#laws.0.1.0">1957 c 456 s 1</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.19.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/82/#laws.0.3.0">1977 c 82 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/359/#laws.0.14.0">1983 c 359 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/513/#laws.1.21.0">1992 c 513 art 1 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/603/#laws.0.3.0">1992 c 603 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/254/#laws.2.17.0">1998 c 254 art 2 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/478/#laws.2.7.0">2000 c 478 art 2 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/10/#laws.2.4.0">2005 c 10 art 2 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.78.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 78</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.966">
        <h1 class="shn">169.966 BOARD TO REGULATE TRAFFIC ON STATE UNIVERSITIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.966.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authority.</span></h2>
          <p>The Board of Trustees of the Minnesota State Colleges and Universities may from time to time make, adopt, and enforce such rules or ordinances not inconsistent with this chapter, as it may find expedient or necessary relating to the regulation of traffic and parking upon parking facilities and private roads and roadways situated on property owned, leased, occupied, or operated by state universities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.966.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Parking facilities.</span></h2>
          <p>The Board of Trustees may establish rents, charges, or fees for the use of parking facilities owned, leased, occupied, or operated by the board. The money collected by the board as rents, charges, or fees in accordance with this subdivision shall be deposited in the university activity fund and is annually appropriated to the Board of Trustees for state university purposes and to maintain and operate parking lots and parking facilities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.966.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Petty misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who violates such rule or ordinance shall be guilty of a petty misdemeanor and subject to the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.891">169.891 </a>and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.90#stat.169.90.1">169.90, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.966.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>The prosecution may be before a district court having jurisdiction over the place where the violation occurs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.966.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Enforcement.</span></h2>
          <p>Every sheriff, police officer, or other peace officer shall see that all rules and ordinances are obeyed and shall arrest and prosecute offenders.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.966.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Enforcement powers.</span></h2>
          <p>The Board of Trustees may appoint and employ, and fix the compensation to be paid out of funds which may be available for such purposes, persons who shall have and may exercise on property owned, leased, or occupied by the state universities the same powers of arrest for violation of rules or ordinances adopted by the board as possessed by a sheriff, police officer, or peace officer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.966.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Judicial notice.</span></h2>
          <p>All persons shall take notice of such rules and ordinances without pleading and proof of the same.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.966.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Notice, hearing, filing, and effect.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The Board of Trustees shall fix a date for a public hearing on the adoption of any such proposed rule or ordinance. Notice of such hearing shall be published in a legal newspaper in the county in which the property affected by the rule or ordinance is located. The publication shall be at least 15 days and not more than 45 days before the date of the hearing.</p>
          <p>(b) If, after the public hearing, the proposed rule or ordinance shall be adopted by a majority of the members of the board, the same shall be considered to have been enacted by the board. A copy of the same shall be signed by the president and filed with the county recorder of each county where the rule or ordinance shall be in effect, together with proof of publication. Upon such filing, the rule or ordinance, as the case may be, shall thenceforth be in full force and effect.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.966.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Delegation.</span></h2>
          <p>The Board of Trustees may delegate its responsibilities under this section to a state university president. Actions of the president shall be presumed to be those of the board. The university president shall file with the board president the results of any public hearings and the subsequent adoption of any proposed rule or ordinance enacted pursuant thereto.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.966.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/0/278/#laws.0.1.0">1961 c 278 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/701/#laws.0.2.0">1969 c 701 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.16.0">1971 c 23 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.20.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/321/#laws.0.2.0">1975 c 321 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/359/#laws.0.15.0">1983 c 359 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/618/#laws.0.6.0">1984 c 618 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/654/#laws.4.25.0">1984 c 654 art 4 s 25</a>,26; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/254/#laws.2.18.0">1998 c 254 art 2 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/1/#laws.2.19.0">1Sp2001 c 1 art 2 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/10/#laws.2.4.0">2005 c 10 art 2 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.79.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 79</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CITATION</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.97">
        <h1 class="shn">169.97 CITATION; HIGHWAY TRAFFIC REGULATION ACT.</h1>
        <p>This chapter shall be cited as the "Highway Traffic Regulation Act."</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.97.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/13">2720-292</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1937/0/464/#laws.0.142.0">1937 c 464 s 142</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">DRIVER IMPROVEMENT CLINICS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.971">
        <h1 class="shn">169.971 DRIVER IMPROVEMENT CLINICS; DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.971.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.971">169.971</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.973">169.973</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.971.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Driver improvement clinic.</span></h2>
          <p>"Driver improvement clinic" means a formal course of study established under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.972">169.972</a>, designed primarily to assist persons convicted of traffic violations in correcting improper driving habits and to familiarize them with the provisions of the Highway Traffic Regulation Act.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.971.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Youth-oriented driver improvement clinic.</span></h2>
          <p>"Youth-oriented driver improvement clinic" means a driver improvement clinic designed for traffic violators age 18 and under to assist them in correcting improper driving practices and review provisions of traffic law with a focus on driving problems common to young and novice drivers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.971.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Municipality.</span></h2>
          <p>"Municipality" means any city, however organized, and any county or town.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.971.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Court.</span></h2>
          <p>"Court" means a district court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.971.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of public safety.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.971.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1965/0/711/#laws.0.1.0">1965 c 711 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/1129/#laws.1.18.0">1969 c 1129 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/123/#laws.5.7.0">1973 c 123 art 5 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/359/#laws.0.16.0">1983 c 359 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/254/#laws.2.19.0">1998 c 254 art 2 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/388/#laws.0.3.0">1998 c 388 s 3</a>,4</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.972">
        <h1 class="shn">169.972 ESTABLISHMENT OF DRIVER IMPROVEMENT CLINIC; FEES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.972.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authority to establish clinic.</span></h2>
          <p>Subject to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.971">169.971</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.973">169.973</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.20#stat.171.20.3">171.20, subdivision 3</a>, any court, municipality, association of municipalities, or any regularly established safety organization may establish and conduct a driver improvement clinic or a youth-oriented driver improvement clinic.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.972.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Fees.</span></h2>
          <p>The court, municipality or organization conducting a driver improvement clinic or a youth-oriented driver improvement clinic may establish reasonable tuition fees not to exceed $50, but not to exceed the actual cost of the course.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.972.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1965/0/711/#laws.0.2.0">1965 c 711 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/194/#laws.0.1.0">1973 c 194 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/385/#laws.0.1.0">1984 c 385 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/388/#laws.0.5.0">1998 c 388 s 5</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.973">
        <h1 class="shn">169.973 REGULATION OF CLINIC; DIRECTOR.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.973.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Commissioner's authority; rules; curriculum.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of public safety shall supervise the administration and conduct of driver improvement clinics and youth-oriented driver improvement clinics. The commissioner of public safety shall promulgate rules setting forth standards for the curriculum and mode of instruction of driver improvement clinics and youth-oriented driver improvement clinics and such other matters as the commissioner of public safety considers necessary for the proper administration of such clinics. In the preparation of such standards the commissioner of public safety shall consult with the state associations of judges. A driver improvement clinic established under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.971">169.971</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.973">169.973</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.20#stat.171.20.3">171.20, subdivision 3</a>, shall conform to the standards promulgated by the commissioner of public safety. The course of study at a driver improvement clinic and youth-oriented driver improvement clinic may not exceed a cumulative total of nine hours with no single class session lasting more than three hours. The course of study at a driver improvement clinic and youth-oriented driver improvement clinic shall include instruction in railroad crossing safety.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.973.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Director.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of public safety may appoint a driver improvement clinic director within the Department of Public Safety and such other employees as are necessary to accomplish the purposes of Laws 1965, chapter 711.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.169.973.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1965/0/711/#laws.0.3.0">1965 c 711 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/1129/#laws.1.18.0">1969 c 1129 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/491/#laws.0.34.0">1971 c 491 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/468/#laws.0.3.0">1990 c 468 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.16.13.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 16 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/388/#laws.0.6.0">1998 c 388 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.10.8.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 10 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.169.974">
        <h1 class="shn">169.974 OPERATION OF MOTORCYCLE; MOTOR SCOOTER; MOTOR BIKE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.974.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>Motorcycles as used herein shall mean the vehicles defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.011#stat.169.011.44">169.011, subdivision 44</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.974.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">License endorsement and permit requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person must not operate a motorcycle on any street or highway without having a valid driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement as provided by law. A person may operate an autocycle without a motorcycle endorsement if the person has a valid driver's license issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.02">171.02</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner of public safety must issue a motorcycle endorsement only if the applicant (1) has in possession a valid motorcycle instruction permit as provided in paragraph (c), (2) has passed a written examination and road test administered by the Department of Public Safety for the endorsement, and (3) in the case of applicants under 18 years of age, presents a certificate or other evidence of having successfully completed an approved motorcycle driver's safety course in this or another state, in accordance with rules adopted by the commissioner of public safety for courses offered by a public, private, or commercial school or institute. The commissioner of public safety may waive the road test for any applicant on determining that the applicant possesses a valid license to operate a motorcycle issued by a jurisdiction that requires a comparable road test for license issuance.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner of public safety must issue a motorcycle instruction permit to any person over 16 years of age who (1) is in possession of a valid driver's license, (2) is enrolled in an approved motorcycle driver's safety course, and (3) has passed a written examination for the permit and paid a fee prescribed by the commissioner of public safety. A motorcycle instruction permit is effective for one year and may be renewed under rules prescribed by the commissioner of public safety.</p>
          <p>(d) A person who is operating by virtue of a motorcycle instruction permit must not:</p>
          <p>(1) carry any passengers on the streets and highways of this state on the motorcycle while the person is operating the motorcycle;</p>
          <p>(2) drive the motorcycle at night; or</p>
          <p>(3) drive the motorcycle without wearing protective headgear that complies with standards established by the commissioner of public safety.</p>
          <p>(e) Notwithstanding paragraphs (a) to (d), the commissioner of public safety may issue a special motorcycle permit, restricted or qualified as the commissioner of public safety deems proper, to any person demonstrating a need for the permit and unable to qualify for a driver's license.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.974.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Vehicle equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any motorcycle with a seat designed or suited for use by a passenger must be equipped with footrests or floorboards for the passenger.</p>
          <p>(b) No person shall operate any motorcycle on the streets and highways unless such motorcycle is equipped with:</p>
          <p>(1) at least one rear view mirror so attached and adjusted as to reflect to the operator a view of the roadway for a distance of at least 200 feet to the rear of the motorcycle; and</p>
          <p>(2) not less than one horn that is audible at a distance of at least 200 feet under normal conditions.</p>
          <p>(c) All other applicable provisions of this chapter pertaining to motorcycle and other motor vehicle equipment shall apply to motorcycles, except those which by their nature have no application.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.974.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Equipment for operator and passenger.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) No person under the age of 18 shall operate or ride a motorcycle on the streets and highways of this state without wearing protective headgear that complies with standards established by the commissioner of public safety; and no person shall operate a motorcycle without wearing an eye-protective device.</p>
          <p>(b) The provisions of this subdivision do not apply to (1) persons during their participation in a parade for which parade a permit or other official authorization has been granted by a local governing body or other governmental authority, or (2) persons riding within an enclosed cab autocycle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.974.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Driving rules.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An operator of a motorcycle must ride only upon a permanent and regular seat which is attached to the vehicle for that purpose. No other person may ride on a motorcycle, except that passengers may ride (1) upon a permanent and regular operator's seat if designed for two persons, (2) upon additional seats attached to or in the vehicle, or (3) in a sidecar attached to the vehicle. The operator of a motorcycle is prohibited from carrying passengers in a number in excess of the designed capacity of the motorcycle or sidecar attached to it. A passenger is prohibited from being carried in a position that interferes with the safe operation of the motorcycle or the view of the operator.</p>
          <p>(b) No person may ride upon a motorcycle as a passenger unless the person can reach the footrests or floorboards with both feet.</p>
          <p>(c) Except for passengers of sidecars, drivers and passengers of three-wheeled motorcycles, and persons in an autocycle, no person may operate or ride upon a motorcycle except while sitting astride the seat, facing forward, with one leg on either side of the motorcycle.</p>
          <p>(d) No person may operate a motorcycle while carrying animals, packages, bundles, or other cargo that prevent the person from keeping both hands on the handlebars.</p>
          <p>(e) Motorcycles may, with the consent of both drivers, be operated not more than two abreast in a single traffic lane if the vehicles fit safely within the designated space of the lane.</p>
          <p>(f) Except under the conditions specified in paragraph (g), no person may operate a motorcycle:</p>
          <p>(1) between lanes of moving or stationary vehicles headed in the same direction of travel;</p>
          <p>(2) abreast of moving or stationary vehicles within the same traffic lane; or</p>
          <p>(3) to overtake or pass another vehicle within the same traffic lane.</p>
          <p>(g) A person may operate a motorcycle and overtake and pass another vehicle in the same direction of travel and within the same traffic lane if the motorcycle is operated:</p>
          <p>(1) at not more than 25 miles per hour; and</p>
          <p>(2) no more than 15 miles per hour over the speed of traffic in the relevant traffic lanes.</p>
          <p>(h) Motor vehicles including motorcycles are entitled to the full use of a traffic lane and no motor vehicle may be driven or operated in a manner so as to deprive a motorcycle of the full use of a traffic lane.</p>
          <p>(i) A person operating a motorcycle upon a roadway must be granted the rights and is subject to the duties applicable to a motor vehicle as provided by law, except as to those provisions which by their nature can have no application.</p>
          <p>(j) Paragraphs (e) and (f) of this subdivision do not apply to police officers in the performance of their official duties.</p>
          <p>(k) No person may operate a motorcycle on a street or highway unless the headlight or headlights are lighted at all times the motorcycle is so operated.</p>
          <p>(l) A person parking a motorcycle on the roadway of a street or highway must:</p>
          <p>(1) if parking in a marked parking space, park the motorcycle completely within the marked space; and</p>
          <p>(2) park the motorcycle in such a way that the front of the motorcycle is pointed or angled toward the nearest lane of traffic to the extent practicable and necessary to allow the operator to (i) view any traffic in both directions of the street or highway without having to move the motorcycle into a lane of traffic and without losing balance or control of the motorcycle, and (ii) ride the motorcycle forward and directly into a lane of traffic when the lane is sufficiently clear of traffic.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.974.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/230/#laws.0.46.0">1999 c 230 s 46</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.169.974.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Noise limits.</span></h2>
          <p>After December 31, 1978, noise rules adopted by the Pollution Control Agency for motor vehicles pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.693">169.693</a> shall also apply to motorcycles.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
